## 2. Load & clean
Import the software-specific outputs and standardize precursor identifiers, sample names, intensity columns, and metadata. Duplicate precursor–run records are resolved using intensity availability and identification scores, where applicable. Zero intensities are treated as missing values (NA), while nonzero intensities are preserved. Basic QC statistics, including precursor counts, duplicate records, and missing values, are reported for each software.

```{r load_clean}
# -----------------------
# ---- helpers ------------
# --------------------
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Import and standardize one software at a time
# ------------------------------------------------------------
read_precursors <- function(software) {
  if (software == "AlphaDIA") {
    # Identify the 84 intensity columns before importing
    header <- names(data.table::fread(file_alpha, nrows = 0L))
    run_cols <- header[2:85]
    stopifnot(length(run_cols) == 84L)

    dt <- fread(file_alpha, colClasses = c(precursor.mod_seq_charge_hash = "character",
                setNames(rep("character", length(run_cols)), run_cols)))

    id_cols <- c("precursor.mod_seq_charge_hash", "precursor.sequence",
                 "precursor.charge", "pg.name")
    stopifnot(all(id_cols %in% names(dt)))

    dt <- melt(dt, id.vars = id_cols, measure.vars = run_cols,
               variable.name = "Run", value.name = "Precursor.Quantity",
               variable.factor = FALSE)

    dt[, Precursor.Quantity := readr::parse_double(Precursor.Quantity)]

    setnames(dt, id_cols,
             c("Precursor.Id", "Stripped.Sequence", "Precursor.Charge",
               "Protein.Group"))

  } else if (software == "DIANN") {
    dt <- fread(file_diann, colClasses = c(Precursor.Id = "character"))
    run_cols <- names(dt)[11:94]
    id_cols <- c("Precursor.Id", "Modified.Sequence", "Stripped.Sequence",
                 "Precursor.Charge", "Protein.Group", "Protein.Ids",
                 "Protein.Names", "Genes", "Proteotypic")
    stopifnot(length(run_cols) == 84L, all(id_cols %in% names(dt)))
    dt <- melt(dt, id.vars = id_cols, measure.vars = run_cols,
               variable.name = "Run", value.name = "Precursor.Quantity",
               variable.factor = FALSE)

  } else if (software == "Spectronaut") {
    dt <- as.data.table(readRDS(file_spectronaut))
    old <- c("R.FileName", "EG.PrecursorId", "PEP.StrippedSequence",
             "PG.ProteinGroups", "FG.Quantity", "EG.PEP", "EG.Cscore",
             "EG.IsDecoy", "EG.IsImputed", "Potential.contaminant")
    new <- c("Run", "Precursor.Id", "Stripped.Sequence", "Protein.Group",
             "Precursor.Quantity", "PEP", "Cscore", "Decoy", "IsImputed",
             "Potential.contaminant")
    stopifnot(all(old %in% names(dt)))
    dt <- dt[, ..old]
    setnames(dt, old, new)

  } else if (software == "MaxDIA") {
    old <- c(
    "Raw file", "Modified sequence", "Sequence",
    "Charge", "Leading proteins", "Proteins",
    "Intensity", "Q-value", "PEP",
    "Reverse", "Potential contaminant",
    "DIA evidence type",
    "Score", "ML score",
    "Match score", "Match q-value")

    dt <- fread(file_maxdia, select = old,
                colClasses = list(character = c(
                  "Raw file", "Modified sequence", "Sequence",
                  "Leading proteins", "Proteins",
                  "Reverse", "Potential contaminant",
                  "DIA evidence type", "Intensity"),
      integer = "Charge",
      numeric = c(
        "Q-value", "PEP",
        "Score", "ML score",
        "Match score", "Match q-value"
      )
    )
  )
    dt[, Intensity := readr::parse_double(Intensity)]
    stopifnot(all(old %in% names(dt)))

    setnames(dt, old, c(
    "Run", "Modified.Sequence", "Stripped.Sequence",
    "Precursor.Charge", "Protein.Group", "Protein.Ids",
    "Precursor.Quantity", "Q.Value", "PEP",
    "Reverse", "Potential.contaminant",
    "DIA.evidence.type",
    "Score", "ML.Score",
    "Match.Score", "Match.Q.Value"))

    dt[, Precursor.Id := paste(Modified.Sequence, Precursor.Charge, sep = "_")]

  } else stop("Unknown software: ", software)


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Standardize missing text annotations
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  for (field in intersect(
    c("Genes", "Reverse", "Potential.contaminant"),
    names(dt)
  )) {

    v <- dt[[field]]

    if (is.character(v)) {
      # Empty or whitespace-only strings become NA
      v[!is.na(v) & trimws(v) == ""] <- NA_character_
      data.table::set(dt, j = field, value = v)
    }
  }

  # Apply filename standardization to distinct run labels (not 20 million rows).
  original_runs <- unique(as.character(dt$Run))
  cleaned_runs <- sub("\\.raw$", "", basename(original_runs), ignore.case = TRUE)
  if (anyNA(original_runs) || anyDuplicated(cleaned_runs)) {
    stop(software, ": missing or colliding run names after standardization")
  }
  dt[, Run := cleaned_runs[match(as.character(Run), original_runs)]]
  dt[, Precursor.Id := as.character(Precursor.Id)]
  if (anyNA(dt$Precursor.Id) || any(!nzchar(dt$Precursor.Id))) {
    stop(software, ": missing/empty precursor IDs")
  }
  if (!is.numeric(dt$Precursor.Quantity)) {
    stop(software, ": intensity is not numeric")
  }
  dt
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# ------- Resolve duplicates, clean intensities -----------
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
clean_precursors <- function(dt, software) {
  n_before <- nrow(dt)
  duplicates <- n_before - uniqueN(dt, by = c("Run", "Precursor.Id"))
  zeros_before <- sum(dt$Precursor.Quantity == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  missing_before <- sum(is.na(dt$Precursor.Quantity))

  # Original priorities: nonmissing quantity, then best identification scores.
  if (software %in% c("Spectronaut", "MaxDIA")) {
    dt[, .missing_qty := is.na(Precursor.Quantity)]
    if (software == "Spectronaut") {
      setorderv(dt, c("Run", "Precursor.Id", ".missing_qty", "PEP", "Cscore"),
               order = c(1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, -1L), na.last = TRUE)
    } else {
      setorderv(dt, c("Run", "Precursor.Id", ".missing_qty", "PEP", "Q.Value"),
               order = rep(1L, 5L), na.last = TRUE)
    }
    dt <- unique(dt, by = c("Run", "Precursor.Id"))
    dt[, .missing_qty := NULL]
  } else if (duplicates != 0L) {
    stop(software, ": unexpected duplicate precursor-run keys")
  }

  stopifnot(uniqueN(dt, by = c("Run", "Precursor.Id")) == nrow(dt))
  if (any(is.infinite(dt$Precursor.Quantity)) ||
      any(dt$Precursor.Quantity < 0, na.rm = TRUE)) {
    stop(software, ": invalid negative/infinite intensities")
  }
  # As in the original workflow: zero intensity means not quantified.
  dt[!is.na(Precursor.Quantity) & Precursor.Quantity == 0,
     Precursor.Quantity := NA_real_]

  n_runs <- uniqueN(dt$Run)
  n_ids <- uniqueN(dt$Precursor.Id)
  if (n_runs != 84L) stop(software, ": expected 84 runs, found ", n_runs)
  per_run <- dt[, .N, by = Run]$N

  message(sprintf(
    "raw rows: %s | duplicate rows removed: %s | cleaned rows: %s | runs: %s | unique precursors: %s | raw zeros: %s | raw NA: %s | cleaned NA: %s",
    format(n_before, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE),
    format(duplicates, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE),
    format(nrow(dt), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE),
    n_runs, format(n_ids, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE),
    format(zeros_before, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE),
    format(missing_before, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE),
    format(sum(is.na(dt$Precursor.Quantity)), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)
  ))
  message(sprintf("precursor observations per run (min / median / max): %s / %s / %s",
                  min(per_run), median(per_run), max(per_run)))
  dt
}

# --------------------------------
# ---- list of cleaned objects --------------
# ----------------------------
cleaned_precursors <- setNames(vector("list", length(software_names)),
                               software_names)

for (software in software_names) {
  message("\n======== ", software, " ========")
  start_time <- Sys.time()

  message("Loading ...")
  dt <- read_precursors(software)

  message("cleaning ...")
  cleaned_precursors[[software]] <- clean_precursors(dt, software)

  message(sprintf("Done! %s (%.2f minutes)", software,
                  as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), start_time, units = "mins"))))
  rm(dt)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

```

## 3. Inspect scores BEFORE joining

Evaluate the available identification confidence scores, including PEP, Cscore, q-values, and other software-specific scores. Target and Decoy distributions are summarized and visualized using all available observations, with individual density curves for each run and average curves across runs. This step examines identification quality and run-to-run variability before integration. The scores are used only for QC and are not included in the final combined objects.

```{r inspect_scores, results='asis', message=TRUE, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# -----------------------
# ---- helpers ------------
# --------------------
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Identify Target and Decoy records (any score column)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

get_identification_class <- function(dt) {

  if ("Decoy" %in% names(dt)) {

    v <- toupper(trimws(as.character(dt$Decoy)))

    class <- rep(NA_character_, length(v))

    class[v %in% c("FALSE", "0", "TARGET")] <- "Target"
    class[v %in% c("TRUE", "1", "DECOY")] <- "Decoy"

    return(class)
  }

  if ("Reverse" %in% names(dt)) {

    # MaxDIA: "+" = Decoy; blank/NA = Target
    v <- toupper(trimws(as.character(dt$Reverse)))

    class <- rep(NA_character_, length(v))

    class[is.na(v) |
            v %in% c("", "-", "FALSE", "0")] <- "Target"

    class[v %in% c("+", "TRUE", "1")] <- "Decoy"

    return(class)
  }

  NULL
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Inspect scores and plot run-specific densities
# ------------------------------------------------------------

inspect_scores <- function(dt, software, plot_scores = TRUE) {

  score_candidates <- c(
    "PEP", "Cscore", "Q.Value",
    "Score", "ML.Score",
    "Match.Score", "Match.Q.Value"
  )

  scores <- intersect(score_candidates, names(dt))

  scores <- scores[
    vapply(
      scores,
      function(s) is.numeric(dt[[s]]),
      logical(1)
    )
  ]

  cat("\n",
      "====================================================\n",
      " IDENTIFICATION SCORE QC: ", software, "\n",
      "====================================================\n",
      sep = "")

  cat("Total runs:", uniqueN(dt$Run), "\n")
  cat("Total precursor-run records:",
      format(nrow(dt), big.mark = ","), "\n")

  if (!length(scores)) {
    cat("No identification score columns available.\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  cat("Scores available:",
      paste(scores, collapse = ", "), "\n\n")

  # Determine Target/Decoy class
  class <- get_identification_class(dt)

  if (is.null(class)) {
    class <- rep("All", nrow(dt))
    message(software, ": no Target/Decoy annotation")
  }

  if (anyNA(class)) {
    warning(
      software, ": ", sum(is.na(class)),
      " records have unknown identification class"
    )
  }

  # Temporary column (removed on exit)
  dt[, .QC_Class := class]

  on.exit(
    dt[, .QC_Class := NULL],
    add = TRUE
  )

  cat("Identification classes:\n")

  print(
    dt[, .(N = .N), by = .QC_Class][
      order(.QC_Class)
    ]
  )

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Process each available score
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  for (score in scores) {

    cat("\n",
        "----------------------------------------------------\n",
        " Software: ", software, "\n",
        " Score: ", score, "\n",
        " Analysis: Target/Decoy score distribution\n",
        " Unit: precursor-run observations\n",
        "----------------------------------------------------\n",
        sep = "")

    # Summary over ALL precursor-run records
    qc <- dt[
      !is.na(.QC_Class),
      {
        values <- get(score)
        finite <- values[is.finite(values)]

        .(
          records = .N,
          valid_scores = length(finite),
          missing_pct = round(
            100 * (1 - length(finite) / .N), 2
          ),
          median_score = if (length(finite)) {
            median(finite)
          } else NA_real_,
          p05 = if (length(finite)) {
            unname(quantile(finite, 0.05))
          } else NA_real_,
          p95 = if (length(finite)) {
            unname(quantile(finite, 0.95))
          } else NA_real_
        )
      },
      by = .(.QC_Class)
    ][order(.QC_Class)]

    setnames(qc, ".QC_Class", "Class")

    # Descriptive caption attached to the table
    table_title <- paste0(
      software, " | ", score,
      " — Target/Decoy summary across ",
      uniqueN(dt$Run), " LC-MS runs"
    )

    cat("\n\n")

    cat(
      as.character(
        knitr::kable(
          as.data.frame(qc),
          format = if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "latex" else "html",
          caption = table_title,
          digits = 3,
          row.names = FALSE
        )
      )
    )

    cat("\n\n")

    if (!plot_scores) next

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Calculate density using ALL scores in each run
    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # stats::density() uses every finite observation.
    # n = 512 is the number of density grid points,
    #
    # Only the calculated density coordinates are retained
    # for ggplot, avoiding enormous plot data frames.
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    score_range <- range(dt[[score]], finite = TRUE)

    if (!all(is.finite(score_range)) ||
        diff(score_range) == 0) {
      message(software, " / ", score,
              ": insufficient score variation")
      next
    }

    density_dt <- dt[
      ,
      {
        values <- get(score)
        values <- values[is.finite(values)]

        if (is.na(.QC_Class[1L]) ||
            length(values) < 2L ||
            min(values) == max(values)) {

          NULL

        } else {

          den <- stats::density(
            values,
            n = 512L,
            from = score_range[1L],
            to = score_range[2L],
            na.rm = TRUE
          )

          .(
            Value = den$x,
            Density = den$y
          )
        }
      },
      by = .(Run, Class = .QC_Class)
    ]

    if (nrow(density_dt) == 0L) {
      message("No density curves for ", software, " / ", score)
      next
    }

    density_dt[
      , Class := factor(
        Class,
        levels = c("Target", "Decoy", "All")
      )
    ]

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Plot all 84 run-specific density curves
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    mean_density <- density_dt[,
                               .(MeanDensity = mean(Density)),
                               by = .(Class, Value)]

    p <- ggplot() +

    # All run-specific curves: transparent
    geom_line(
      data = density_dt,
      aes(
        x = Value,
        y = Density,
        color = Class,
        group = interaction(Run, Class)
      ),
      linewidth = 0.25,
      alpha = 0.12,
      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +

    # Thick average curve for each identification class
    geom_line(
      data = mean_density,
      aes(
        x = Value,
        y = MeanDensity,
        color = Class,
        group = Class
      ),
      linewidth = 1.5,
      alpha = 1,
      show.legend = TRUE
    ) +

    scale_color_manual(
      values = c(
        Target = "#E76F66",
        Decoy = "#00AEB8",
        All = "#555555"
      ),
      drop = TRUE
    ) +

    guides(
      color = guide_legend(
        override.aes = list(
          linewidth = 1.5,
          alpha = 1
        )
      )
    ) +

    labs(
      title = paste0(software, " | ", score, " distribution"),
      subtitle = paste0(
        uniqueN(density_dt$Run),
        " runs | Transparent: individual runs",
        " | Bold: mean density across runs"
      ),
      x = score,
      y = "Density",
      color = "Identification"
    ) +

    theme_classic(base_size = 13) +

    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "top"
    )

  print(p)


    cat(
      "\nDensity curves generated for",
      uniqueN(density_dt$Run),
      "runs | Score:", score,
      "| Software:", software, "\n"
    )

    rm(density_dt, mean_density)
  }

  invisible(NULL)
}
```

## 4. Combine qf assays
Combine precursor intensities from all 84 runs into a single matrix for each software, matching rows by Precursor.Id. Only precursor annotations consistent across runs are retained in rowData, while sample information is stored in colData. Identification scores and inconsistent metadata are excluded. The resulting objects are validated and saved as compressed RDS files for downstream analysis. Existing files are skipped to avoid unnecessary processing.
```{r build_and_save, message=TRUE, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
# -----------------------
# ---- helpers ------------
# --------------------
make_sample_annotation <- function(runs) {
  sampleId <- runs
  genotype <- ifelse(grepl("c-jun_KO", sampleId, ignore.case = TRUE), "KO",
                     ifelse(grepl("CTRL", sampleId, ignore.case = TRUE),
                            "CTRL", NA_character_))
  jnk <- grepl("JNK-IN-8", sampleId, ignore.case = TRUE)
  cddp <- grepl("cDDP", sampleId, ignore.case = TRUE)
  treatment <- ifelse(jnk & cddp, "JNK_IN_8_cDDP",
                      ifelse(jnk, "JNK_IN_8", ifelse(cddp, "cDDP", "Untreated")))
  time <- ifelse(grepl("06h", sampleId, ignore.case = TRUE), "6h",
                 ifelse(grepl("24h", sampleId, ignore.case = TRUE), "24h",
                        ifelse(treatment == "Untreated", "Baseline", NA_character_)))
  sample_set <- ifelse(grepl("^Group[1-4]", sampleId),
                       sub("^(Group[1-4]).*", "\\1", sampleId), NA_character_)
  rep <- ifelse(grepl("[0-9]+$", sampleId),
                sub(".*?([0-9]+)$", "\\1", sampleId, perl = TRUE), NA_character_)
  condition <- ifelse(!is.na(genotype) & !is.na(time),
                      paste(genotype, treatment, time, sep = "_"), NA_character_)

  DataFrame(runCol = runs, sampleId = sampleId, sample_set = sample_set,
            genotype = factor(genotype), treatment = factor(treatment),
            time = factor(time), rep = factor(rep),
            condition = factor(condition), row.names = runs)
}

# ----------------
make_combined_qf <- function(dt, software) {
  runs <- sort(unique(dt$Run))
  ids <- unique(dt$Precursor.Id)
  nr <- length(runs)
  n <- length(ids)
  ri <- match(dt$Precursor.Id, ids)
  ci <- match(dt$Run, runs)
  stopifnot(!anyNA(ri), !anyNA(ci))

  # Column-major linear indexing, no 84-way merge and no large cbind() index.
  pos <- (ci - 1L) * n + ri
  if (anyDuplicated(pos)) stop(software, ": duplicate precursor-run positions")
  mat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n, ncol = nr,
                dimnames = list(ids, runs))
  mat[pos] <- dt$Precursor.Quantity


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Retain only consistent precursor-level metadata
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  rd <- DataFrame(
    Precursor.Id = ids,
    row.names = ids
  )

  # Identification scores were already examined in Chunk 3.
  # Do not include them in the combined QFeatures.
  score_fields <- c(
    "PEP", "Cscore", "Q.Value",
    "Score", "ML.Score",
    "Match.Score", "Match.Q.Value"
  )

  # Fields that belong to the intensity matrix or sample metadata
  base_fields <- c(
    "Run", "Precursor.Id", "Precursor.Quantity"
  )

  # Identify score columns to remove
  removed_scores <- intersect(names(dt), score_fields)

  # Remaining precursor metadata columns
  fields <- setdiff(
    names(dt),
    c(base_fields, score_fields)
  )

  # Essential fields must be consistent
  identity_fields <- c(
    "Decoy", "IsDecoy", "isDecoy",
    "Reverse", "Precursor.Charge"
  )

  retained_fields <- character()
  dropped_fields <- character()

  for (field in fields) {

    v <- dt[[field]]

    if (is.factor(v)) {
      v <- as.character(v)
    }

    # Skip unsupported data types
    if (!is.atomic(v) || !is.null(dim(v))) {
      dropped_fields <- c(dropped_fields, field)
      message(software, ": unsupported metadata: ", field)
      next
    }

    # One representative nonmissing value per precursor
    retained <- rep(v[NA_integer_], n)

    observed <- which(!is.na(v))

    if (length(observed) > 0L) {
      retained[ri[observed]] <- v[observed]
    }

    # Check whether a precursor has conflicting values
    conflict <- !is.na(v) & v != retained[ri]

    inconsistent <- any(conflict)

    if (inconsistent) {

      # Conflicting identity/decoy annotations should not be ignored
      if (field %in% identity_fields) {
        stop(
          software,
          ": conflicting precursor annotation: ",
          field
        )
      }

      dropped_fields <- c(dropped_fields, field)

    } else {

      # Retain consistent metadata
      rd[[field]] <- retained
      retained_fields <- c(retained_fields, field)
    }
  }

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Report metadata processing
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  message("\n--- ", software, ": rowData summary ---")

  message(
    "Retained metadata: ",
    if (length(retained_fields)) {
      paste(retained_fields, collapse = ", ")
    } else "None"
  )

  message(
    "Dropped inconsistent metadata: ",
    if (length(dropped_fields)) {
      paste(dropped_fields, collapse = ", ")
    } else "None"
  )

  message(
    "Excluded identification scores: ",
    if (length(removed_scores)) {
      paste(removed_scores, collapse = ", ")
    } else "None"
  )

  message(
    "Final rowData: ",
    nrow(rd), " precursors x ",
    ncol(rd), " metadata columns"
  )

  # Verify that no identification scores were retained
  stopifnot(
    !any(score_fields %in% colnames(rd))
  )

  # Verify precursor identity
  stopifnot(
    identical(rownames(rd), ids),
    identical(as.character(rd$Precursor.Id), ids)
  )

  cd <- make_sample_annotation(runs)

  se <- SummarizedExperiment(
    assays = list(intensity = mat), rowData = rd, colData = cd
  )

  qf <- QFeatures(list(precursors = se), colData = cd)

  stopifnot(
    ncol(qf[["precursors"]]) == 84L,
    identical(rownames(qf[["precursors"]]),
              as.character(rowData(qf[["precursors"]])$Precursor.Id)),
    identical(colnames(qf[["precursors"]]), rownames(colData(qf[["precursors"]])))
  )
  qf
}

combined_qf_files <- setNames(
  file.path(cache_dir, paste0("qf_", software_names, "_combined.rds")),
  software_names
)

for (software in software_names) {
  output <- combined_qf_files[[software]]
  if (file.exists(output)) {
    message("Already exists, skipping: ", software)
    next
  }

  message("\nProcessing ", software, "...")
  start_time <- Sys.time()

  # Combine 84 runs by Precursor.Id
  qf_combined <- make_combined_qf(cleaned_precursors[[software]], software)

  gc(verbose = FALSE)

  se <- qf_combined[["precursors"]]
  x <- assay(se, withDimnames = FALSE)

  stopifnot(ncol(se) == 84L, sum(x == 0, na.rm = TRUE) == 0L,
            identical(rownames(se), as.character(rowData(se)$Precursor.Id)),
            identical( colnames(se), rownames(colData(se))))

  message(sprintf("Combined: %s precursors x %s runs | zeros: %s | NA: %s",
                  nrow(se), ncol(se), sum(x == 0, na.rm = TRUE), sum(is.na(x))))

  rm(se, x)
  # Save
  saveRDS(qf_combined, output, compress = "gzip")

  message(sprintf("Saved %s (%.2f minutes)", output,
                  as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), start_time, units = "mins"))))
  rm(qf_combined)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

message("\nAll four combined QFeatures objects are ready.")

```


## 5. Summary qfs
The four saved QFeatures objects are reloaded individually to summarize their dimensions, quantitative coverage, and metadata. For each software, we report the number of unique precursors, LC-MS runs, quantified and missing intensity values, and zero intensities. We also evaluate precursor coverage across runs, including the median number of quantified precursors per run and the number consistently quantified in all 84 runs. Objects are processed sequentially to minimize memory usage.
```{r recover_combined_qfeatures, message=FALSE, results='hide'}
# ============================================================
# Locate saved combined QFeatures objects
# Inspect one software at a time
# ============================================================
combined_qf_files <- setNames(
  file.path(cache_dir, paste0("qf_", software_names, "_combined.rds")),
  software_names
)
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("cache_dir", "software_names", "combined_qf_files")))
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))


# Confirm all four files exist
if (!all(file.exists(combined_qf_files))) {
  stop("One or more combined QFeatures files are missing.")
}

# Inspect each software without keeping all objects in memory
combined_summary <- vector("list", length(software_names))
names(combined_summary) <- software_names

for (software in software_names) {

  qf <- readRDS(combined_qf_files[[software]])
  se <- qf[["precursors"]]
  x <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(se, withDimnames = FALSE)

  n_precursors <- nrow(se)
  n_runs <- ncol(se)
  total_values <- as.double(n_precursors) * n_runs

  # Count quantified observations without making
  # a full-size logical matrix
  per_run <- integer(n_runs)
  per_precursor <- integer(n_precursors)

  n_missing <- 0
  n_zero <- 0

  for (j in seq_len(n_runs)) {

    v <- x[, j]

    missing <- is.na(v)
    zero <- !missing & v == 0
    observed <- !missing & v > 0

    n_missing <- n_missing + sum(missing)
    n_zero <- n_zero + sum(zero)

    per_run[j] <- sum(observed)
    per_precursor <- per_precursor + as.integer(observed)
  }

  n_quantified <- sum(per_run)

  stopifnot(
    n_runs == 84L,
    n_quantified + n_missing + n_zero == total_values
  )

  combined_summary[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Precursors = n_precursors,
    Runs = n_runs,
    Quantified_Values = n_quantified,
    Missing_Values = n_missing,
    Missing_Pct = 100 * n_missing / total_values,
    Zero_Values = n_zero,
    Median_Per_Run = median(per_run),
    Min_Per_Run = min(per_run),
    Max_Per_Run = max(per_run),
    Precursors_All_Runs = sum(per_precursor == n_runs),
    RowData_Columns = ncol(rowData(se)),
    ColData_Columns = ncol(colData(se))
  )

  rm(qf, se, x, per_run, per_precursor)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

combined_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(combined_summary)
write.csv(combined_summary, "Outputs/combined_summary_84runs.csv", row.names = F)
print(tibble::as_tibble(combined_summary), width = Inf)

#print(as.tibble(make_sample_annotation(qf$runCol)), width = Inf)

```


## 6. Log-transformation
Intensity values were log2-transformed using the `logTransform()` function from the QFeatures package to reduce right-skewness and improve comparability of quantitative measurements. The transformed intensities were stored in a new assay named precursors_log, while the original filtered intensities were preserved in precursors. Both assays were retained within each software-specific QFeatures object, maintaining their metadata and processing relationships for subsequent analysis.

```{r precursor_histograms_before_normalization, eval=FALSE, fig.width=12, fig.height=7}
# ============================================================
# Log2 transformation of filtered precursor intensities
# Update existing filtered QFeatures files and R objects
# ============================================================
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("cache_dir", "software_names")))
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

combined_qf_files <- setNames(
  file.path(cache_dir, paste0("qf_", software_names, "_combined.rds")),
  software_names
)


for (software in software_names) {

  cat("\nLog2-transforming ", software, "...\n", sep = "")

  # Load existing filtered QFeatures
  qf_one <- readRDS(combined_qf_files[[software]])

  # Add log2-transformed assay
  if (!"precursors_log" %in% names(qf_one)) {

    # Log2 requires strictly positive finite intensities.
    # Missing observations (NA) are allowed.
    x <- assay(qf_one[["precursors"]], withDimnames = FALSE)
    stopifnot(!any(x <= 0, na.rm = TRUE), !any(is.infinite(x)))
    rm(x)

    qf_one <- QFeatures::logTransform(qf_one,
                                      base = 2, pc = 0,
                                      i = "precursors",
                                      name = "precursors_log")
    }

  # Overwrite existing filtered cache file
  saveRDS(qf_one, combined_qf_files[[software]])


  # Verify assay structure
  raw_se <- qf_one[["precursors"]]
  log_se <- qf_one[["precursors_log"]]

  stopifnot(
    identical(dim(raw_se), dim(log_se)),
    identical(rownames(raw_se), rownames(log_se)),
    identical(colnames(raw_se), colnames(log_se))
  )

  cat(sprintf("%s: %s precursors x %s runs",
    software, nrow(log_se), ncol(log_se)))

  plot(qf_one, main=software)

  rm(qf_one, raw_se, log_se)
  invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))
}

```

```{r precursor_density_before_normalization, eval=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=6, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
  run_densities <- lapply(seq_len(ncol(x)), function(j) {

      n = 512L,
      na.rm = TRUE

      Run = colnames(se)[j],
      Log2_Intensity = den$x,
      Density = den$y
    )

        nrow(density_data[[software]]), " density coordinates\n", sep = "")

    invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))
```

## 8. Hist precursor 

```{r precursor_density_before_normalization_extra, eval=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=6, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Pre-normalization log2 precursor intensity distributions
# One density curve per software, pooling all 84 runs
# ============================================================
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("cache_dir", "software_names")))
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

combined_qf_files <- setNames(
  file.path(cache_dir, paste0("qf_", software_names, "_combined.rds")),
  software_names
)

boxplot_list <- list()

for (software in software_names) {

  cat("\nProcessing ", software, "...\n", sep = "")

  qf_one <- readRDS(combined_qf_files[[software]])
  se <- qf_one[["precursors_log"]]

  x <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(se, withDimnames = FALSE)
  
  runs <- colnames(se)
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Calculate exact boxplot statistics for each run
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  run_stats <- lapply(seq_along(runs), function(j) {

    values <- x[, j]
    values <- values[is.finite(values)]

    if (!length(values)) return(NULL)

    # Quartiles from ALL finite intensities
    q <- as.numeric(stats::quantile(
      values,
      probs = c(0.25, 0.50, 0.75),
      names = FALSE
    ))

    iqr <- q[3] - q[1]
    # Tukey whiskers (1.5 * IQR)
    lower_limit <- q[1] - 1.5 * iqr
    upper_limit <- q[3] + 1.5 * iqr

    data.frame(
      Software = software,
      Run = runs[j],
      N = length(values),
      Whisker_Low = min(values[values >= lower_limit]),
      Q1 = q[1],
      Median = q[2],
      Q3 = q[3],
      Whisker_High = max(values[values <= upper_limit])
    )
  })

  boxplot_list[[software]] <- dplyr::bind_rows(run_stats)
  
  cat(software, ": ", nrow(boxplot_list[[software]]), " runs processed\n",sep = "")

  rm(qf_one, se, x, run_stats)
  invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))
}

boxplot_data <- dplyr::bind_rows(boxplot_list)
```

Unlike the other three software packages, Spectronaut has a distinctly multimodal intensity distribution, including a sharp peak near log2 intensity = 0 and a broader low-intensity population between approximately 2 and 7. This is particularly suspicious because almost every Spectronaut precursor has a reported intensity in all 84 runs, despite IsImputed = False throughout.

## *** Spectro 1 to NA
Replace Spectronaut raw intensity = 1 with NA

```{r}
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("cache_dir", "software_names")))
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))
```

## *** Removing outlier
One LC-MS run (Group1_c-jun_KO_1) exhibited an atypical precursor intensity distribution across multiple DIA analysis pipelines, most prominently in AlphaDIA and DIA-NN. Given the consistency of this observation across software tools and the availability of additional replicates for the corresponding condition, the run was excluded from downstream quantitative analysis. Normalization was subsequently recalculated using the remaining 83 runs.

```{r exclude_outlier_and_renormalize, message=FALSE, eval=run_analysis}
# ============================================================
# Exclude shared QC outlier and repeat normalization
# ============================================================
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("cache_dir", "software_names")))
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

combined_qf_files <- setNames(
  file.path(cache_dir, paste0("qf_", software_names, "_combined.rds")),
  software_names
)

excluded_run <- "Group1_c-jun_KO_1"

for (software in software_names) {
  
  message("Removing the Group1_c-jun_KO_1 ", software, "...")
  
  qf_one <- readRDS(combined_qf_files[[software]])

  # Remove the outlier column from all linked assays
  keep_runs <- colnames(qf_one[["precursors_log"]]) != excluded_run

  qf_one <- qf_one[, keep_runs, ]
  
  message("Remaining runs: ", length(qf_one$runCol))
  
  saveRDS(qf_one, combined_qf_files[[software]])
  
  rm(qf_one)
}

```

## 9. Filtering

```{r filter_combined_precursors, message=TRUE, eval=run_analysis}
# ============================================================
# Filter combined precursor-level QFeatures
#
# 1. Detection in >= 2/3 of samples in ANY condition
# 2. Remove decoys, reverse hits and contaminants
# 3. Retain proteotypic peptides where identifiable
# 4. Do NOT remove proteins supported by only one peptide
#
# IMPORTANT:
# Proteotypic status cannot yet be verified for AlphaDIA
# and Spectronaut using their current combined rowData.
# ============================================================
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("cache_dir", "software_names", "combined_qf_files")))
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

filtered_qf_files <- setNames(
  file.path(cache_dir, paste0("qf_", software_names, "_filtered_final.rds")),
  software_names
)

filter_summary <- list()

# Helper: nonmissing, nonempty text
valid_text <- function(z) {
  !is.na(z) & nzchar(trimws(as.character(z)))
}

# Helper: annotations indicating an unflagged entry
# Supports logical FALSE, numeric 0, and MaxQuant-style "-"
not_flagged <- function(z) {
  z <- tolower(trimws(as.character(z)))

  is.na(z) | z %in% c("", "-", "0", "false")
}

for (software in software_names) {

  message("Filtering ", software, "...")

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 1. Load one combined QFeatures object
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  qf_one <- readRDS(combined_qf_files[[software]])
  se <- qf_one[["precursors"]]

  rd <- as.data.frame(rowData(se))
  cd <- as.data.frame(colData(se))

  n_before <- nrow(se)

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 2. Condition-aware detection filter
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  conditions <- as.character(cd$condition)

  stopifnot(
    length(conditions) == ncol(se),
    !anyNA(conditions),
    identical(rownames(cd), colnames(se))
  )

  groups <- split(seq_along(conditions), conditions)

  keep_detection <- rep(FALSE, n_before)

  for (idx in groups) {

    min_obs <- ceiling(length(idx) * 2 / 3)

    # Only extract columns for the current condition
    x_group <- assay(se)[, idx, drop = FALSE]

    observed <- rowSums(
      !is.na(x_group) & x_group > 0
    )

    keep_detection <- keep_detection |
      (observed >= min_obs)

    rm(x_group, observed)
  }

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 3. Require valid precursor and protein annotations
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  required_columns <- c(
    "Precursor.Id",
    "Stripped.Sequence",
    "Protein.Group"
  )

  stopifnot(all(required_columns %in% names(rd)))

  keep_ids <-
    valid_text(rd$Precursor.Id) &
    valid_text(rd$Stripped.Sequence) &
    valid_text(rd$Protein.Group)

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 4. Remove decoys, reverse hits and contaminants
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  keep_quality <- rep(TRUE, n_before)

  # Spectronaut: logical Decoy TRUE/FALSE
  if ("Decoy" %in% names(rd)) {

    z <- tolower(trimws(as.character(rd$Decoy)))

    keep_quality <- keep_quality &
      !is.na(z) &
      z %in% c("false", "0", "-")
  }

  # MaxDIA: Reverse flag, typically "+" or blank
  if ("Reverse" %in% names(rd)) {

    keep_quality <- keep_quality &
      not_flagged(rd$Reverse)
  }

  # Spectronaut / MaxDIA: Potential.contaminant
  #
  # Spectronaut uses:
  #   "-" = not flagged
  #   "+" = contaminant
  #
  # MaxDIA may also use "+" / blank.
  if ("Potential.contaminant" %in% names(rd)) {

    keep_quality <- keep_quality &
      not_flagged(rd$Potential.contaminant)
  }

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 5. Proteotypic peptide filtering
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  keep_proteotypic <- rep(TRUE, n_before)
  proteotypic_unknown <- rep(FALSE, n_before)

  if ("Proteotypic" %in% names(rd)) {

    # DIA-NN: explicit proteotypic annotation
    z <- tolower(trimws(as.character(rd$Proteotypic)))

    keep_proteotypic <- !is.na(z) &
      z %in% c("true", "1")

  } else if ("Protein.Ids" %in% names(rd)) {

    # MaxDIA: proxy based on protein identifiers
    # Semicolon-separated multiple IDs are treated as
    # ambiguous protein assignments.
    ids <- trimws(as.character(rd$Protein.Ids))

    keep_proteotypic <- valid_text(ids) &
      !grepl(";", ids, fixed = TRUE)

    proteotypic_unknown <- !valid_text(ids)

  } else {

    # AlphaDIA and Spectronaut:
    # Current Protein.Group annotation alone is
    # insufficient to establish peptide uniqueness.
    #
    # Retain these rows but record unknown status.
    proteotypic_unknown <- rep(TRUE, n_before)
  }

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 6. Combine all filters
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  keep <- keep_detection &
    keep_ids &
    keep_quality &
    keep_proteotypic

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 7. Summarize filtering
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  filter_summary[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Before = n_before,
    Passed_Detection = sum(keep_detection),
    Passed_Annotations = sum(keep_ids),
    Passed_Quality = sum(keep_quality),
    Passed_Proteotypic = sum(keep_proteotypic),
    Unknown_Proteotypic_After_Filter = sum(keep & proteotypic_unknown),
    Retained = sum(keep),
    Removed = sum(!keep),
    Retained_Percent = round(100 * mean(keep), 2)
  )

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 8. Filter QFeatures
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  qf_filtered <- qf_one[keep, , ]

  filtered_se <- qf_filtered[["precursors"]]

  # Verify assay dimensions and sample metadata
  stopifnot(
    nrow(filtered_se) == sum(keep),
    ncol(filtered_se) == ncol(se),
    nrow(rowData(filtered_se)) == nrow(filtered_se),
    nrow(colData(filtered_se)) == ncol(filtered_se),
    identical(
      rownames(colData(filtered_se)),
      colnames(filtered_se)
    )
  )

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 9. Save filtered QFeatures
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  saveRDS(qf_filtered, filtered_qf_files[[software]])

  message(
    software, ": ",
    sum(keep), " / ", n_before,
    " precursors retained (",
    round(100 * mean(keep), 2), "%)"
  )

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 10. Release memory before next software
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  rm(
    qf_one, qf_filtered, se, filtered_se,
    rd, cd, keep, keep_detection,
    keep_ids, keep_quality,
    keep_proteotypic, proteotypic_unknown,
    conditions
  )

  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

# ============================================================
# Final filtering summary
# ============================================================

filter_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(filter_summary)
print(as.tibble(lapply(groups, length)),width = Inf)
print(tibble::as_tibble(filter_summary), width = Inf)

```

Precursor-level filtering was performed independently for AlphaDIA, DIA-NN, Spectronaut, and MaxDIA. Precursors were retained if they had positive, non-missing intensities in at least two-thirds of the samples within any one experimental condition, preserving condition-specific signals. Annotated decoys, reverse hits, and potential contaminants were excluded. Proteotypic filtering was applied using DIA-NN's explicit annotation and a single-protein-identifier criterion for MaxDIA; however, proteotypic status could not be reliably verified for AlphaDIA and Spectronaut, so these precursors were retained pending further assessment. No minimum peptide count per protein was imposed. Following filtering, AlphaDIA retained 62.5%, DIA-NN 67.8%, Spectronaut 90.8%, and MaxDIA 63.6% of their initial precursors. Spectronaut's higher retention reflects its nearly complete quantitative matrix, whereas detection-frequency filtering had a greater impact on the other pipelines. Differences in software-specific quantification and proteotypic annotations should therefore be considered when interpreting precursor coverage.





## 10. Normalization
Systematic technical variation between LC-MS runs can introduce differences in measured precursor intensities that are unrelated to biological conditions. Pre-normalization QC revealed batch-associated intensity shifts across the four DIA analysis pipelines. To account for run-level differences, the Median of Ratios method was applied independently to each software's log2-transformed precursor intensities. Normalization factors were calculated using `nfLogMedianOfRatios()` and subtracted from each corresponding run using `sweep()`. The normalized intensities were stored in a new assay named `precursors_norm`, preserving the original precursors and `precursors_log` assays.

```{r normalize_precursors, message=FALSE, eval=run_analysis}
# ============================================================
# Median of Ratios normalization for four DIA software tools
# ============================================================
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("cache_dir", "software_names")))
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

filtered_qf_files <- setNames(
  file.path(cache_dir, paste0("qf_", software_names, "_filtered_final.rds")),
  software_names
)


normalization_summary <- list()

for (software in software_names) {

  cat("\nNormalizing ", software, "...\n", sep = "")

  qf_one <- readRDS(filtered_qf_files[[software]])

  # Calculate log2 normalization factors
  nf_log <- msqrob2::nfLogMedianOfRatios(qf_one, "precursors_log")

  # Check normalization factors
  stopifnot(
    length(nf_log) == ncol(qf_one[["precursors_log"]]),
    all(is.finite(nf_log))
  )

  # Create normalized assay
  qf_one <- sweep(qf_one, MARGIN = 2, STATS = nf_log,
                  FUN = "-",
                  i = "precursors_log",
                  name = "precursors_norm")

  # Verify all three assays
  stopifnot(
    all(c("precursors", "precursors_log", "precursors_norm") %in% names(qf_one)),
    identical(dim(qf_one[["precursors_log"]]), dim(qf_one[["precursors_norm"]])))

  # Summarize normalization factors
  normalization_summary[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Min_Factor = min(nf_log),
    Median_Factor = median(nf_log),
    Max_Factor = max(nf_log),
    SD_Factor = sd(nf_log)
  )


  # Update existing filtered cache file (no new RDS)
  saveRDS(qf_one, filtered_qf_files[[software]])
  
  # Check assay structure
  names(qf_one)
  plot(qf_one, main=software)

  rm(qf_one, nf_log)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

normalization_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  normalization_summary
)

print(normalization_summary)

```

## 11. Before&After norm

```{r evaluate_precursor_normalization, eval=FALSE, fig.width=14, fig.height=10, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# ============================================================
# Evaluate Median of Ratios normalization
# Four DIA software packages, 84 runs each
# ============================================================
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("cache_dir", "software_names")))
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

filtered_qf_files <- setNames(
  file.path(cache_dir, paste0("qf_", software_names, "_filtered_final.rds")),
  software_names
)

density_list <- list()
median_list <- list()

for (software in software_names) {

  cat("\nProcessing normalization QC: ", software, "...\n", sep = "")
  qf_one <- readRDS(filtered_qf_files[[software]])

  se_before <- qf_one[["precursors_log"]]
  se_after  <- qf_one[["precursors_norm"]]
  
  before <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(se_before, withDimnames = FALSE)
  after <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(se_after, withDimnames = FALSE)

  runs <- colnames(se_before)

  batch <- dplyr::case_when(
    grepl("^Group1_", runs) ~ "Group 1",
    grepl("^Group2_", runs) ~ "Group 2",
    grepl("^Group3_", runs) ~ "Group 3",
    grepl("^Group4_", runs) ~ "Group 4",
    grepl("^20260331_", runs) ~ "20260331",
    TRUE ~ "Unknown"
  )

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Run-level medians and densities using ALL intensitiess
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  median_before <- rep(NA_real_, length(runs))
  median_after  <- rep(NA_real_, length(runs))

  run_densities <- vector("list", length(runs) * 2L)
  
  for (j in seq_along(runs)) {
    # Extract all finite intensities for this run
    x_before <- before[, j]
    x_before <- x_before[is.finite(x_before)]

    x_after <- after[, j]
    x_after <- x_after[is.finite(x_after)]

    # Run-level medians
    if (length(x_before)) {
      median_before[j] <- median(x_before)
    }

    if (length(x_after)) {
      median_after[j] <- median(x_after)
    }

    # Calculate KDE for each normalization stage
    for (stage in c("Before", "After")) {

      values <- if (stage == "Before") x_before else x_after

      if (length(values) < 2L || min(values) == max(values)) {
        next
      }

      den <- stats::density(
        values,
        n = 512L,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )

      idx <- (j - 1L) * 2L +
        if (stage == "Before") 1L else 2L

      run_densities[[idx]] <- data.frame(
        Software = software,
        Run = runs[j],
        Stage = stage,
        Log2_Intensity = den$x,
        Density = den$y
      )
    }
  }
  
  median_list[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Run = runs,
    Batch = batch,
    Before = as.numeric(median_before),
    After = as.numeric(median_after)
  )

  # Store density coordinates (not raw intensities)
  density_list[[software]] <- dplyr::bind_rows(run_densities)

  cat( software, ": ", length(runs), " runs; ",
       nrow(density_list[[software]]), " density coordinates\n", sep = "")

  rm(qf_one, se_before, se_after, before, after,
     run_densities, x_before, x_after, values, den)
  
  invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))
}

# ============================================================
```

The results strengthen the justification for excluding Group1_c-jun_KO_1, particularly for DIA-NN and MaxDIA.

## 12. Aggregation
The objective of aggregation is to summarise the precursor-level intensities into a protein expression value. The fact that different precursors have different intensities (2.), may be inconsistently identified (3.) and/or quantified (4.), and show sample correlations (5.) can lead to bias if we use simple summarisation approaches such as summing or averaging the precursor intensities for each sample. Instead, we will resort to more advanced summarisation approaches to accommodate for these issues. Here, we summarise the precursor-level data into protein intensities usin`g maxLFQ`. It is implemented in the `maxLFQ` function of the `iq` package.

```{r protein_aggregation_maxlfq, message=FALSE, eval=run_analysis}
# ============================================================
# Protein-level aggregation using MaxLFQ
# Four DIA software packages, 83 runs each
# ============================================================
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("cache_dir", "software_names")))
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

filtered_qf_files <- setNames(
  file.path(cache_dir, paste0("qf_", software_names, "_filtered_final.rds")),
  software_names
)

aggregation_summary <- list()

for (software in software_names) {

  message("Aggregating proteins for ", software, "...")

  qf_one <- readRDS(filtered_qf_files[[software]])

  # Verify normalized assay and protein identifiers
  stopifnot(
    "precursors_norm" %in% names(qf_one),
    "Protein.Group" %in%
      colnames(rowData(qf_one[["precursors_norm"]])),
    ncol(qf_one[["precursors_norm"]]) == 83L
  )

  # Aggregate normalized precursor intensities to proteins
  qf_one <- QFeatures::aggregateFeatures(
    qf_one,
    i = "precursors_norm",
    name = "proteins",
    fcol = "Protein.Group",
    fun = function(X, ...) {
      iq::maxLFQ(X)$estimate
    }
  )

  # Verify protein assay
  stopifnot(
    "proteins" %in% names(qf_one),
    ncol(qf_one[["proteins"]]) == 83L
  )

  # Summarize aggregation
  protein_x <- assay(qf_one[["proteins"]])

  aggregation_summary[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Precursors = nrow(qf_one[["precursors_norm"]]),
    Proteins = nrow(protein_x),
    Runs = ncol(protein_x),
    Quantified_Proteins = sum(
      rowSums(is.finite(protein_x)) > 0
    ),
    Complete_Proteins = sum(
      rowSums(is.finite(protein_x)) == ncol(protein_x)
    )
  )

  # Overwrite existing filtered cache file
  saveRDS(qf_one, filtered_qf_files[[software]])

  message(
    software, ": ",
    nrow(protein_x), " protein groups aggregated"
  )

  rm(qf_one, protein_x)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

aggregation_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  aggregation_summary
)

print(aggregation_summary)

```

## 13. Density protein

```{r protein_aggregation_density, eval=FALSE, fig.width=14, fig.height=9, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Protein-level intensity density plots
# Four DIA software packages
# ============================================================
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("cache_dir", "software_names")))
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

filtered_qf_files <- setNames(
  file.path(cache_dir, paste0("qf_", software_names, "_filtered_final.rds")),
  software_names
)


density_data <- list()

for (software in software_names) {

  cat("\nCalculating densities for ", software, "...\n", sep = "")
  
  # Load existing filtered QFeatures
  qf_one <- readRDS(filtered_qf_files[[software]])
  
  se <- qf_one[["proteins"]]
  x <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(se, withDimnames = FALSE)

  # Calculate density separately for each run
  run_densities <- lapply(seq_len(ncol(x)), function(j) {

    values <- x[, j]
    values <- values[is.finite(values)]

    if (length(values) < 2L ||
        min(values) == max(values)) {
      return(NULL)
    }
    
    den <- stats::density(
      values,
      n = 512L,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  
    data.frame(
      Software = software,
      Run = colnames(se)[j],
      Log2_Intensity = den$x,
      Density = den$y
    )
  })
  
    density_data[[software]] <- dplyr::bind_rows(run_densities)

    cat(software, ": ", ncol(se), " runs; ",
        nrow(density_data[[software]]), " density coordinates\n", sep = "")
    
    rm(qf_one, se, x, run_densities)
    invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))
}

density_data <- dplyr::bind_rows(density_data) %>%
  mutate(Software = factor(Software, levels = software_names))

# Plot all 84 run distributions for each software
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(density_data,
  ggplot2::aes(x = Log2_Intensity, y = Density, color = Software,
               group = interaction(Software, Run))) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.35, alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
  "AlphaDIA" = "#0072B2", "DIANN" = "#E69F00",
  "Spectronaut" = "#009E73", "MaxDIA" = "#CC79A7"))+
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Protein-level intensity distributions after MaxLFQ aggregation",
    subtitle = "83 LC-MS runs per software",
    x = "Normalized log2 protein intensity", y = "Density") +
  ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = 'top',
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold")
  )


ggplot2::ggsave(
  "Outputs/Protein_density.pdf",
  plot = p,
  width = 7,
  height = 5,
  bg = "white"

```
Overall, MaxLFQ aggregation produced reasonably consistent protein-level intensity distributions across the 83 runs in all four software packages.
- AlphaDIA: Narrow, closely overlapping distributions, indicating good run-to-run consistency.
- DIA-NN: Broader distributions with slightly more variability, but generally good overlap.
- Spectronaut: Strong overlap around the main peak, although a small low-intensity tail remains.
- MaxDIA: Good overall alignment, with some variability in peak height and distribution shape.

The protein-level distributions look suitable for proceeding to downstream QC and differential abundance analysis. There are no obvious extreme run-level outliers remaining.

The data processing is complete.

# NIMAA analyis

```{r NIMAAFunctions}
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("cache_dir", "software_names")))
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

filtered_qf_files <- setNames(
  file.path(cache_dir, paste0("qf_", software_names, "_filtered_final.rds")),
  software_names
)

arrange_NIMAA_matrix <- function(x) {

  # Step 1: Sort precursors by increasing missingness
  row_order <- order(rowSums(x == 0L))
  x <- x[row_order, , drop = FALSE]

  # Step 2: Sort runs by increasing missingness
  col_order <- order(colSums(x == 0L))
  x <- x[, col_order, drop = FALSE]

  # Step 3: Lexicographic ordering of precursor detection patterns
  # Equivalent in intent to NIMAA's arrange_if() step
  row_order3 <- do.call(order,
    c(lapply(seq_len(ncol(x)), function(j) -x[, j]),
      list(method = "radix")))

  x[row_order3, , drop = FALSE]
}

# NIMAA-style largest top-left complete rectangle
find_NIMAA_rectangle <- function(x) {

  first_missing <- max.col(x == 0L, ties.method = "first")

  # Correct rows containing no missing measurements
  complete_rows <- rowSums(x == 0L) == 0L
  first_missing[complete_rows] <- ncol(x) + 1L

  widths <- first_missing - 1L

  # A rectangle must be complete across ALL rows above its bottom edge
  widths <- cummin(widths)

  areas <- seq_len(nrow(x)) * widths
  best_row <- which.max(areas)

  list(
    rows = best_row,
    cols = widths[best_row],
    cells = areas[best_row]
  )
}
```
## 14. Precursor

Precursor detection was represented as a binary precursor-by-run matrix (observed = 1; missing = 0). The NIMAA-style `Rectangular_element_max` method was applied to all precursor features to identify a fully observed rectangular submatrix. The efficient implementation was checked against the original NIMAA output on a 5,000-precursor test matrix.

### - Checking incidence

```{r nimmaAnalysis, eval=!run_analysis, message=FALSE}
# Recover fully processed QFeatures from saved RDS files

qf_alpha <- readRDS(filtered_qf_files[["AlphaDIA"]])
qf_diann <- readRDS(filtered_qf_files[["DIANN"]])
qf_spectro <- readRDS(filtered_qf_files[["Spectronaut"]])
qf_maxdia <- readRDS(filtered_qf_files[["MaxDIA"]])

qf_NIMAA <- list(
  AlphaDIA = qf_alpha,
  "DIA-NN" = qf_diann,
  Spectronaut = qf_spectro,
  MaxDIA = qf_maxdia
)

stopifnot(all(vapply(
  qf_NIMAA,
  function(qf) "precursors_norm" %in% names(qf),
  logical(1)
)))

cat("Successfully recovered normalized QFeatures for all four pipelines.\n")

# ----------------------------------------
# ----- NIMAA-precursor-incidence -----
# -----------------------------------
# Binary precursor-by-run incidence matrices:
# 1 = observed finite abundance; 0 = missing
NIMAA_incidence <- lapply(qf_NIMAA, function(qf) {
  x <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(qf[["precursors"]])
  # Preserve feature and sample identifiers
  observed <- is.finite(x)
  # Store as integer values for incidence analysis
  storage.mode(observed) <- "integer"
  observed
})

# Validate matrix dimensions and observed fractions
NIMAA_incidence_check <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(names(NIMAA_incidence), function(software) {
    x <- NIMAA_incidence[[software]]

    data.frame(
      Software = software,
      Precursors = nrow(x),
      Runs = ncol(x),
      Observed_pct = round(100 * mean(x), 2),
      Missing_pct = round(100 * (1 - mean(x)), 2),
      Complete_precursors = sum(rowSums(x) == ncol(x)),
      Complete_runs = sum(colSums(x) == nrow(x))
    )
  })
)

print(NIMAA_incidence_check, row.names = FALSE)

```

```{r NIMAA-full-element-max, eval=run_analysis}
  lapply(names(NIMAA_full_arranged), function(software) {
    result <- find_NIMAA_rectangle(NIMAA_full_arranged[[software]])
    data.frame(
      Software = software,
      Method = "Rectangular_element_max",

# Confirm each selected rectangle contains only observed values

  r <- NIMAA_full_rectangles[NIMAA_full_rectangles$Software == s, ]

}, logical(1))))

nimma_precursore <- NIMAA_incidence_check%>%

  left_join(NIMAA_full_rectangles%>%
              dplyr::select(Software, Complete_Runs=Runs, Complete_Precursors=Precursors, Complete_cells),
            by = 'Software')%>%
  mutate(Complete_cells_pct=Complete_cells/(Precursors*Runs)*100)
```

```{r NIMAA-precursor-figure, eval=FALSE, fig.width=14, fig.height=9, dpi=300, message=FALSE}

software_colors <- c(
  "AlphaDIA"    = "#0072B2",
  "DIA-NN"      = "#E69F00",
  "Spectronaut" = "#009E73",
  "MaxDIA"      = "#CC79A7"

# ============================================================
# PRECURSOR-ONLY MEMORY-EFFICIENT RASTER
# ============================================================

make_precursor_raster <- function(x, color, max_columns = 2200L) {

  n_features <- nrow(x)
  n_runs <- ncol(x)
  n_display <- min(n_features, max_columns)

  boundaries <- floor(seq(
    0, n_features,
    length.out = n_display + 1L
  ))

  display_matrix <- matrix(
    0L, nrow = n_runs, ncol = n_display
  )

  for (j in seq_len(n_display)) {
    first <- boundaries[j] + 1L
    last <- boundaries[j + 1L]

    fraction <- colMeans(
      x[first:last, , drop = FALSE] == 1L,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )

    display_matrix[, j] <- as.integer(fraction >= 0.5)
  }

  display_matrix <- display_matrix[
    n_runs:1, , drop = FALSE
  ]

  as.raster(matrix(
    c("#FFFFFF", color)[as.vector(display_matrix) + 1L],
    nrow = nrow(display_matrix),
    ncol = ncol(display_matrix)
  ))
}

# ============================================================
# PRECURSOR PLOT FUNCTION
# ============================================================

plot_NIMAA_precursor <- function(software) {

  x <- NIMAA_full_arranged[[software]]

  rect <- NIMAA_full_rectangles |>
    dplyr::filter(
      Software == software,
      Method == "Rectangular_element_max"
    )

  stopifnot(nrow(rect) == 1L)

  n_features <- nrow(x)
  n_runs <- ncol(x)

  raster_image <- make_precursor_raster(
    x,
    software_colors[[software]]
  )

  ggplot() +
    annotation_raster(
      raster_image,
      xmin = 0.5,
      xmax = n_features + 0.5,
      ymin = 0.5,
      ymax = n_runs + 0.5
    ) +
    annotate(
      "rect",
      xmin = 0.5,
      xmax = rect$Precursors + 0.5,
      ymin = n_runs - rect$Runs + 0.5,
      ymax = n_runs + 0.5,
      fill = "#666666",
      alpha = 0.22,
      colour = "#333333",
      linewidth = 0.7
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      limits = c(0.5, n_features + 0.5),
      breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 3),
      labels = scales::label_comma(),
      expand = c(0, 0)
    ) +
    scale_y_reverse(
      limits = c(n_runs + 0.5, 0.5),
      breaks = c(1, 20, 40, 60, 83),
      expand = c(0, 0)
    ) +
    labs(
      title = software,
      subtitle = paste0(
        scales::comma(rect$Precursors),
        " precursors × ",
        rect$Runs,
        " runs"
      ),
      x = "Arranged precursors",
      y = "Arranged runs"
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 18) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        face = "bold", size = 23,
        margin = margin(b = 3)
      ),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(
        size = 17,
        margin = margin(b = 6)
      ),
      axis.title = element_text(
        size = 18, face = "bold"
      ),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16),
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        size = 16,
        angle = 45,
        hjust = 1,
        vjust = 1
      ),
      axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 0.5),
      panel.border = element_rect(
        colour = "grey50",
        fill = NA,
        linewidth = 0.4
      ),
      plot.margin = margin(5, 8, 5, 5)
    )
}
```

### - Nestedness

```{r NIMAA-nestedness-repeated, eval=run_analysis, eval=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=6, dpi=300}

set.seed(42)

n_repeats <- 20
n_precursors <- 5000

NIMAA_nestedness_repeated <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(names(NIMAA_incidence), function(software) {

    x <- NIMAA_incidence[[software]]

    dplyr::bind_rows(
      lapply(seq_len(n_repeats), function(i) {

        message(software, " | repetition ", i, "/", n_repeats)

        selected <- sample.int(
          nrow(x),
          size = min(n_precursors, nrow(x)),
          replace = FALSE
        )

        temperature <- bipartite::nested(
          x[selected, , drop = FALSE],
          method = "binmatnest"
        )

        data.frame(
          Software = software,
          Repetition = i,
          Nestedness_temperature = as.numeric(temperature)
        )
      })
    )
  })
)

# Summarise repeated nestedness estimates
NIMAA_nestedness_summary <- NIMAA_nestedness_repeated |>
  group_by(Software) |>
  summarise(Mean_temperature = mean(Nestedness_temperature, na.rm = TRUE),
            SD_temperature = sd(Nestedness_temperature, na.rm = TRUE),
            Min_temperature = min(Nestedness_temperature, na.rm = TRUE),
            Max_temperature = max(Nestedness_temperature, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(across(c(Mean_temperature, SD_temperature,
                  Min_temperature, Max_temperature),
                ~ round(.x, 2)))

print(as.data.frame(NIMAA_nestedness_summary), row.names = FALSE)

# ---------------------------------------
# ----- visualizing -----------------
# -------------------------------
# Use unrounded values for plotting
nestedness_plot_summary <- NIMAA_nestedness_repeated |>
  group_by(Software) |>
  summarise(
    Mean = mean(Nestedness_temperature),
    SD = sd(Nestedness_temperature),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Software = factor(Software, levels = rev(names(NIMAA_incidence))),
    Label = sprintf("%.2f ± %.2f", Mean, SD)
  )

nestedness_plot_data <- NIMAA_nestedness_repeated |>
  mutate(
    Software = factor(Software, levels = rev(names(NIMAA_incidence)))
  )

NIMAA_nestedness_figure <- ggplot() +
  # Individual random-sampling repetitions
  geom_jitter(
    data = nestedness_plot_data,
    aes(x = Nestedness_temperature, y = Software,
        colour = Software),
    height = 0.13,
    width = 0,
    alpha = 0.30,
    size = 2
  ) +
  # Mean ± SD
  geom_errorbarh(
    data = nestedness_plot_summary,
    aes(
      y = Software,
      xmin = Mean - SD,
      xmax = Mean + SD,
      colour = Software
    ),
    height = 0.20,
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = nestedness_plot_summary,
    aes(x = Mean, y = Software, colour = Software),
    size = 4.5
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = nestedness_plot_summary,
    aes(x = Mean + SD + 0.8, y = Software, label = Label),
    hjust = -0.1,
    vjust = 0.5,
    size = 4.5
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = software_colors) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 50),
    breaks = seq(0, 50, 10),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))
  ) +
  labs(
#    title = "Precursor-level nestedness across DIA pipelines",
#    subtitle = "20 random samples of 5,000 precursors per pipeline",
    x = "Precursor nestedness temperature",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 17),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(
      colour = "grey90", linewidth = 0.4
    ),

```
Spectronaut had the largest complete submatrix (6.25 million cells; 41.35% of its original matrix), including all 83 runs. DIA-NN included the greatest proportion of original precursors (45.66%) but only 42 runs. AlphaDIA included 81 runs and 20.14% of original matrix cells; MaxDIA included 58 runs and 12.45%.

Nestedness temperature was estimated using 5,000 randomly sampled precursors per pipeline, with all 83 runs. Spectronaut had the lowest temperature (6.96), followed by DIA-NN (17.71), AlphaDIA (23.78), and MaxDIA (28.50). Lower values indicate more nested detection patterns. Overall, Spectronaut showed the most complete and nested detection structure in this analysis. Differences in precursor sets and matrix fill limit direct interpretation of nestedness as quantitative performance.

Repeated sampling (20 iterations of 5,000 precursors) showed consistent differences in nestedness temperature across pipelines. Spectronaut had the lowest mean temperature (6.84 ± 0.22), followed by DIA-NN (18.08 ± 0.33), AlphaDIA (23.49 ± 0.35), and MaxDIA (28.50 ± 0.42). The low variability across repetitions indicates stable estimates under the sampling procedure, with Spectronaut exhibiting the most strongly nested precursor detection pattern.




The tutorial uses longForm() to visualize every measurement. Because your datasets are large, this version samples up to 2,000 quantified proteins per run for plotting, while retaining all protein measurements in the QFeatures objects.

```{r NIMAA-protein-figure, eval=FALSE, fig.width=14, fig.height=9, dpi=300, message=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# PROTEIN-ONLY RASTER
# Full resolution; no downsampling
# ============================================================

make_protein_raster <- function(x, color) {

  # Convert the full protein incidence matrix to a raster
  incidence <- t(x)[ncol(x):1, , drop = FALSE]

  as.raster(matrix(
    c("#FFFFFF", color)[as.integer(incidence) + 1L],
    nrow = nrow(incidence),
    ncol = ncol(incidence)
  ))
}
```

Protein-level NIMAA analysis showed substantially higher completeness than precursor-level analysis across all four DIA pipelines. **AlphaDIA** produced the largest complete submatrix (8,937 proteins × 82 runs; 77.92% matrix coverage), whereas **Spectronaut** achieved the highest proportional coverage (95.12%), followed by MaxDIA (88.60%), DIA-NN (76.85%), and AlphaDIA (77.92%).

Nestedness temperatures calculated using **all proteins and 83 runs** were lowest for MaxDIA (0.022) and Spectronaut (0.026), followed by AlphaDIA (1.150) and DIA-NN (1.448). These low values indicate highly nested protein detection patterns.

Overall, protein aggregation substantially reduced missingness, allowing nearly all runs to be preserved in complete submatrices. Spectronaut and MaxDIA exhibited the most complete and strongly nested protein-level detection patterns, while AlphaDIA provided the largest absolute number of complete protein measurements. These findings reflect detection completeness rather than quantitative accuracy.

# - - - - - - - - - - 
# Data exploration and QC
Data exploration aims to highlight the main sources of variation in the data prior to data modelling and can pinpoint to outlying or off-behaving samples.
## 16. QC
### - Charge state
```{r qc_charge_state, fig.width=16, fig.height=10, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Charge-state composition of quantified precursors
# Four DIA software packages, 83 runs each
# ============================================================
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("cache_dir", "software_names")))
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

filtered_qf_files <- setNames(
  file.path(cache_dir, paste0("qf_", software_names, "_filtered_final.rds")),
  software_names
)

charge_qc_list <- list()
charge_annotation_summary <- list()

for (software in software_names) {

  message("Processing charge states: ", software)

  se <- readRDS(filtered_qf_files[[software]])[["precursors_norm"]]
  x <- assay(se)

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 1. Extract precursor charge states
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  if (software == "Spectronaut") {

    # Spectronaut encodes charge at the end of Precursor.Id
    # Example: _PEPTIDE_.2 -> charge 2

    precursor_ids <- as.character(
      rowData(se)$Precursor.Id
    )

    charge <- suppressWarnings(
      as.integer(
        sub("^.*\\.([0-9]+)$", "\\1", precursor_ids)
      )
    )

    charge_source <- "Precursor.Id suffix"

  } else {

    # Other software: use existing charge annotation

    charge_candidates <- c(
      "Precursor.Charge",
      "PrecursorCharge",
      "Charge",
      "Charge.State"
    )

    charge_col <- intersect(
      charge_candidates,
      colnames(rowData(se))
    )

    if (length(charge_col) == 0L) {
      warning(software, ": no precursor charge column found")
      next
    }

    charge <- suppressWarnings(
      as.integer(
        as.character(rowData(se)[[charge_col[1]]])
      )
    )

    charge_source <- charge_col[1]
  }

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 2. Summarize charge annotations
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  charge_annotation_summary[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Charge_Source = charge_source,
    Total_Precursors = length(charge),
    Charge_1_to_4 = sum(charge %in% 1:4, na.rm = TRUE),
    Missing_Charge = sum(is.na(charge))
  )

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 3. Count quantified precursors per charge state and run
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  for (z in 1:4) {

    idx <- which(charge == z)

    if (length(idx) == 0L) next

    counts <- colSums(
      is.finite(x[idx, , drop = FALSE])
    )

    charge_qc_list[[paste(software, z)]] <- data.frame(
      Software = software,
      Run = colnames(se),
      Charge = as.character(z),
      Count = as.numeric(counts)
    )
  }

  rm(se, x)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

# ============================================================
# 4. Combine results
# ============================================================

charge_qc <- dplyr::bind_rows(charge_qc_list)

charge_annotation_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  charge_annotation_summary
)

print(charge_annotation_summary)

# Calculate percentages within each software and run
charge_qc <- charge_qc |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::group_by(Software, Run) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Percentage = 100 * Count / sum(Count, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()

charge_qc$Charge <- factor(
  charge_qc$Charge,
  levels = c("4", "3", "2", "1")
)

charge_qc$Software <- factor(
  charge_qc$Software,
  levels = software_names
)

# ============================================================
# 5. Plot charge-state composition
# ============================================================

ggplot2::ggplot(
  charge_qc,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = Run,
    y = Percentage,
    fill = Charge
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(
    width = 0.85
  ) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(
    ~ Software,
    ncol = 2,
    scales = "free_x"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_brewer(
    palette = "Blues",
    direction = -1
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Precursor charge-state composition across LC-MS runs",
    subtitle = "Relative proportions of quantified precursors with charge states 1–4",
    x = "LC-MS run",
    y = "Quantified precursor observations (%)",
    fill = "Charge state"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold")
  )

# ============================================================
# 6. Verify all four software packages are represented
# ============================================================

print(table(charge_qc$Software))
```

```{r qc_completeness_summary, message=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Summarize precursor completeness for all four tools
# ============================================================
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("cache_dir", "software_names")))
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

filtered_qf_files <- setNames(
  file.path(cache_dir, paste0("qf_", software_names, "_filtered_final.rds")),
  software_names
)

completeness_summary <- lapply(
  software_names,
  function(software) {

    se <- readRDS(filtered_qf_files[[software]])[["precursors_norm"]]
    x <- assay(se)

    observed_per_precursor <- rowSums(is.finite(x))
    observed_per_run <- colMeans(is.finite(x)) * 100

    data.frame(
      Software = software,
      Total_Precursors = nrow(x),
      Runs = ncol(x),
      Min_Run_Completeness = min(observed_per_run),
      Median_Run_Completeness = median(observed_per_run),
      Max_Run_Completeness = max(observed_per_run),
      Complete_Precursors = sum(
        observed_per_precursor == ncol(x)
      ),
      Complete_Precursors_Percent = 100 * mean(
        observed_per_precursor == ncol(x)
      )
    )
  }
)

completeness_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  completeness_summary
)

print(completeness_summary)
```
The charge-state distributions are generally stable across the 83 LC-MS runs in all four software pipelines, with predominantly doubly and triply charged precursors and no obvious major charge-state bias. However, precursor completeness differs substantially between pipelines. Spectronaut shows the highest median run-level completeness (94.2%) and proportion of precursors quantified across all 83 runs (41.4%), although this should be interpreted cautiously given its previously observed intensity-floor behavior. AlphaDIA and DIA-NN show comparable median completeness (72.5% and 75.7%) and complete precursor proportions (19.5% and 22.0%), whereas MaxDIA exhibits greater variability, including the lowest minimum run completeness (34.3%) and lowest proportion of complete precursors (9.7%). Overall, charge-state composition appears consistent, but differences in precursor missingness—particularly in MaxDIA—should be considered during downstream statistical modeling.

### - Identifications per sample

```{r qc_identifications_per_run, fig.width=17, fig.height=10, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Quantified precursors and protein groups per LC-MS run
# ============================================================
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("cache_dir", "software_names")))
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

filtered_qf_files <- setNames(
  file.path(cache_dir, paste0("qf_", software_names, "_filtered_final.rds")),
  software_names
)

identification_list <- list()

for (software in software_names) {

  se <- readRDS(filtered_qf_files[[software]])[["precursors_norm"]]
  x <- assay(se)

  protein_groups <- as.character(rowData(se)$Protein.Group)
  conditions <- as.character(colData(se)$condition)

  # Assign each precursor to its protein group
  group_index <- split(
    seq_along(protein_groups),
    protein_groups
  )

  # Exclude missing or empty protein identifiers
  group_index <- group_index[
    !is.na(names(group_index)) &
    nzchar(names(group_index))
  ]

  # Count protein groups with at least one quantified precursor
  protein_counts <- vapply(
    seq_len(ncol(x)),
    function(j) {
      sum(vapply(
        group_index,
        function(idx) any(is.finite(x[idx, j])),
        logical(1)
      ))
    },
    integer(1)
  )

  identification_list[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Run = colnames(se),
    Condition = conditions,
    Precursors = colSums(is.finite(x)),
    `Protein Groups` = protein_counts,
    check.names = FALSE
  )

  rm(se, x, group_index)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

identification_qc <- dplyr::bind_rows(identification_list)

identification_long <- identification_qc |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c("Precursors", "Protein Groups"),
    names_to = "Feature",
    values_to = "IDs"
  )

identification_long$Software <- factor(
  identification_long$Software,
  levels = software_names
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
  identification_long,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = Run,
    y = IDs,
    fill = Condition
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(width = 0.85) +
  facet_grid2(
    Software ~ Feature,
    scales = "free_y",
    independent = "y" 
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Quantified precursor and protein group identifications per run",
    subtitle = "83 LC-MS runs per software",
    x = "LC-MS run",
    y = "Number of quantified features",
    fill = "Condition"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```
The number of quantified precursors varies across runs and software pipelines, with AlphaDIA and DIA-NN showing relatively similar coverage patterns, Spectronaut exhibiting more consistent precursor counts, and MaxDIA displaying greater run-to-run variability. Protein group counts appear comparatively stable within each pipeline. These results suggest differences in precursor detection efficiency and coverage between software tools, without indicating a clear condition-specific identification bias.
