Precursor detection frequency differs substantially between software packages. Spectronaut shows a strong concentration of precursors quantified in nearly all 83 runs, indicating high data completeness. AlphaDIA and DIA-NN exhibit broader detection-frequency distributions, while MaxDIA shows the greatest proportion of precursors quantified in intermediate numbers of runs. These findings highlight software-dependent missingness patterns, with Spectronaut providing the most complete precursor matrix, although its previously observed intensity-floor behavior warrants caution.
### - Completeness condition

```{r qc_completeness_by_condition, fig.width=15, fig.height=9, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Precursor completeness within experimental conditions
# ============================================================
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("cache_dir", "software_names")))
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

filtered_qf_files <- setNames(
  file.path(cache_dir, paste0("qf_", software_names, "_filtered_final.rds")),
  software_names
)

condition_completeness_list <- list()

for (software in software_names) {

  se <- readRDS(filtered_qf_files[[software]])[["precursors_norm"]]
  x <- assay(se)

  conditions <- as.character(colData(se)$condition)
  condition_groups <- split(seq_along(conditions), conditions)

  condition_completeness_list[[software]] <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    lapply(names(condition_groups), function(cond) {

      idx <- condition_groups[[cond]]
      n_runs <- length(idx)

      n_detected <- rowSums(
        is.finite(x[, idx, drop = FALSE])
      )

      data.frame(
        Software = software,
        Condition = cond,
        Runs = n_runs,
        Complete_Percent = 100 * mean(
          n_detected == n_runs
        ),
        Two_Thirds_Percent = 100 * mean(
          n_detected >= ceiling(2 * n_runs / 3)
        )
      )
    })
  )

  rm(se, x)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

condition_completeness <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  condition_completeness_list
)

condition_completeness_long <- condition_completeness |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c("Complete_Percent", "Two_Thirds_Percent"),
    names_to = "Metric",
    values_to = "Percentage"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Metric = dplyr::recode(
      Metric,
      Complete_Percent = "All runs",
      Two_Thirds_Percent = "At least 2/3 of runs"
    )
  )

ggplot2::ggplot(
  condition_completeness_long,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = Condition,
    y = Percentage,
    fill = Metric
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(
    position = "dodge",
    width = 0.75
  ) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(
    ~ Software,
    ncol = 2
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Precursor completeness by experimental condition",
    subtitle = "Percentage of retained precursors meeting within-condition detection thresholds",
    x = "Experimental condition",
    y = "Precursors meeting threshold (%)",
    fill = "Detection threshold"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1
    ),
    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold")
  )

print(condition_completeness)
```
Spectronaut consistently demonstrates the highest within-condition completeness, with approximately 59–79% of precursors quantified in every replicate and 95–97% meeting the two-thirds detection threshold. AlphaDIA and DIA-NN show intermediate completeness, with 28–42% and 32–50% of precursors, respectively, quantified in all runs within a condition. MaxDIA exhibits the lowest and most variable completeness (16–42%), particularly in untreated baseline and 24-hour treatment groups. Across all pipelines, conditions containing more replicates generally show lower complete-case percentages, reflecting the greater difficulty of detecting a precursor in every run. Overall, these results emphasize the importance of accounting for software-specific missingness during downstream statistical modeling.

### - Dimensionality reduction

```{r protein_mds_qc, fig.width=15, fig.height=11, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Protein-level MDS: four DIA software packages
# Complete-case proteins, 83 LC-MS runs
# ============================================================
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("cache_dir", "software_names")))
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

filtered_qf_files <- setNames(
  file.path(cache_dir, paste0("qf_", software_names, "_filtered_final.rds")),
  software_names
)



mds_list <- list()
mds_summary <- list()

for (software in software_names) {

  message("Running protein-level MDS: ", software)

  qf_one <- readRDS(filtered_qf_files[[software]])

  # Retrieve protein assay with sample metadata
  se <- qf_one[["proteins"]]
  x <- assay(se)

  # Retain proteins quantified in all 83 runs
  keep <- rowSums(is.finite(x)) == ncol(x)

  se <- se[keep, ]

  stopifnot(nrow(se) >= 2L)

  # Convert to SingleCellExperiment
sce <- as(se, "SingleCellExperiment")

# Use the first assay explicitly, as in the tutorial
sce <- scater::runMDS(
  sce,
  exprs_values = 1
)

  # Extract MDS coordinates
  coords <- as.data.frame(
    SingleCellExperiment::reducedDim(sce, "MDS")
  )

  colnames(coords)[1:2] <- c("MDS1", "MDS2")

  coords$Software <- software
  coords$Run <- colnames(se)
  coords$Condition <- as.character(colData(se)$condition)
  coords$Genotype <- as.character(colData(se)$genotype)
  coords$Treatment <- as.character(colData(se)$treatment)

  coords$Batch <- dplyr::case_when(
    grepl("^Group1_", coords$Run) ~ "Group 1",
    grepl("^Group2_", coords$Run) ~ "Group 2",
    grepl("^Group3_", coords$Run) ~ "Group 3",
    grepl("^Group4_", coords$Run) ~ "Group 4",
    grepl("^20260331_", coords$Run) ~ "20260331",
    TRUE ~ "Unknown"
  )

  mds_list[[software]] <- coords

  mds_summary[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Proteins_Used = sum(keep),
    Runs = ncol(se)
  )

  rm(qf_one, se, x, sce, coords)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

```
The MDS plots reveal a strong acquisition batch effect across all four DIA software pipelines, with substantially weaker separation by biological condition. This is an important finding before statistical modeling.
1. MDS by experimental condition
Samples form several distinct clusters in AlphaDIA, DIA-NN, Spectronaut, and MaxDIA. However, these clusters contain mixtures of experimental conditions rather than showing clear separation by genotype or treatment. Some conditions are distributed across multiple clusters, suggesting that experimental condition is not the dominant source of variation in the first two MDS dimensions. MaxDIA also shows somewhat greater dispersion within clusters.
2. MDS by acquisition batch
The batch-colored plots show pronounced clustering according to acquisition batch in all four pipelines. AlphaDIA, DIA-NN, and Spectronaut exhibit particularly clear batch separation, while MaxDIA shows a similar pattern with slightly greater within-batch variability. Importantly, these patterns persist despite Median of Ratios normalization, indicating that global intensity normalization has not eliminated batch-associated variation.

These are substantial numbers of proteins for exploratory MDS, although each software uses a different set of complete-case proteins.

The results suggest that acquisition batch is a major source of protein-level variation, potentially masking biological differences between experimental conditions. This is consistent across all four analysis pipelines and therefore deserves attention before differential abundance analysis.

The key findings are:
- Untreated controls and KO samples are represented across all five acquisition batches, providing useful reference groups.
- 24-hour cisplatin treatments are represented in Groups 1–2 and the 20260331 batch, whereas 6-hour treatments occur exclusively in Groups 3–4.
- JNK inhibitor treatments follow the same time-dependent batch allocation.
- Every experimental condition appears in at least two batches, but the design is not fully crossed.
Most importantly, treatment duration (6 h versus 24 h) is confounded with acquisition batch among treated samples. Consequently, a direct comparison of 6-hour and 24-hour treatment effects cannot be reliably separated from batch effects without additional assumptions.

### - Correlation matrix

```{r qc_protein_spearman_correlation, fig.width=14, fig.height=12, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Protein-level Spearman sample correlation matrices
# ============================================================
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("cache_dir", "software_names", "sample_design")))
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

filtered_qf_files <- setNames(
  file.path(cache_dir, paste0("qf_", software_names, "_filtered_final.rds")),
  software_names
)

correlation_matrices <- list()
correlation_plot_data <- list()
correlation_summary <- list()

for (software in software_names) {

  message("Calculating correlations: ", software)

  qf_one <- readRDS(filtered_qf_files[[software]])
  se <- qf_one[["proteins"]]
  x <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(se, withDimnames = FALSE)

  # Spearman correlation across runs
  cor_mat <- stats::cor(x,
                        method = "spearman",
                        use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

  # Match sample metadata to correlation matrix columns
  metadata <- sample_design[
    match(colnames(cor_mat), sample_design$Run),
  ]

  stopifnot(!anyNA(metadata$Run))

  # Order runs by acquisition batch
  ordered_runs <- metadata$Run[
    order(metadata$Batch, metadata$Condition, metadata$Run)
  ]

  cor_mat <- cor_mat[
    ordered_runs,
    ordered_runs,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  correlation_matrices[[software]] <- cor_mat

  # Convert 83 x 83 matrix to plotting data
  plot_data <- as.data.frame(as.table(cor_mat))

  colnames(plot_data) <- c(
    "Run1", "Run2", "Correlation"
  )

  plot_data$Software <- software

  correlation_plot_data[[software]] <- plot_data

  # Summarize correlations within and between batches
  pair_idx <- which(
    upper.tri(cor_mat),
    arr.ind = TRUE
  )

  pair_data <- data.frame(
    Correlation = cor_mat[pair_idx],
    Run1 = rownames(cor_mat)[pair_idx[, 1]],
    Run2 = colnames(cor_mat)[pair_idx[, 2]]
  )

  batch_lookup <- setNames(
    as.character(sample_design$Batch),
    sample_design$Run
  )

  pair_data$Same_Batch <-
    batch_lookup[pair_data$Run1] ==
    batch_lookup[pair_data$Run2]

  correlation_summary[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Median_Within_Batch = median(
      pair_data$Correlation[pair_data$Same_Batch],
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    Median_Between_Batch = median(
      pair_data$Correlation[!pair_data$Same_Batch],
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    Minimum_Correlation = min(
      pair_data$Correlation,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    Median_Correlation = median(
      pair_data$Correlation,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  )

  rm(se, x, cor_mat, plot_data, pair_data)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

correlation_plot_data <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  correlation_plot_data
)

correlation_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(

)

  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Protein-level Spearman correlation matrices",
    subtitle = "83 LC-MS runs per software, ordered by acquisition batch",
    x = "LC-MS run",

    fill = "Spearman\ncorrelation"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = ggplot2::element_blank(),

    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold")
  )

```
The correlation matrices reveal high overall protein-level similarity between samples, but clear software-dependent differences and batch-associated variation. DIA-NN exhibits the strongest correlations (median 0.976), with only a small difference between within-batch (0.986) and between-batch (0.974) correlations, indicating highly consistent protein abundance rankings across runs. AlphaDIA and Spectronaut show good overall correlations (medians 0.851 and 0.817), but noticeably higher within-batch than between-batch similarity (differences of 0.084 and 0.093, respectively), supporting the batch effects observed in MDS. MaxDIA displays the lowest overall correlation (median 0.731), the lowest minimum correlation (0.521), and greater sample-to-sample variability. Overall, these findings reinforce the importance of accounting for acquisition batch during differential abundance modeling, particularly for AlphaDIA, Spectronaut, and MaxDIA.


## 17.Biological QC and acquidtion-batch exclusion
###  - Revise sample_design
```{r group4_exclusion_decision}
# ============================================================
# Biological QC: Exclusion of acquisition Group 4
# ============================================================
#
# Rationale:
#
# The expected reduction in JUN (c-Jun; UniProt P05412)
# abundance in KO relative to CTRL was absent or reversed
# in acquisition Group 4 across all four DIA pipelines.
#
# This finding was supported by:
# 1. Protein-level JUN abundance.
# 2. Multiple JUN peptide sequences.
# 3. Untreated and cisplatin-treated 6h samples.
# 4. Proteome-wide genotype signatures excluding JUN.
# 5. Leave-one-batch-out genotype validation.
#
# In contrast, other acquisition batches generally retained
# the expected genotype-associated proteomic separation.
#
# The observations indicate a batch-specific inconsistency
# in the expected knockout phenotype. They do not establish
# sample mislabeling or its underlying cause.
#
# Decision:
# Exclude all Group 4 runs from the primary analysis to avoid
# potential confounding by uncertain biological sample
# identity or genotype-associated phenotype.
#
# The original 83-run analysis should be retained for
# sensitivity comparisons.
# ============================================================
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("cache_dir", "software_names", "sample_design")))
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

# Record original analysis population
sample_design_before_group4 <- sample_design

# Identify excluded runs
group4_excluded_runs <- sample_design |>
  filter(as.character(Batch) == "Group 4") |>
  select(Run, Condition, Batch) |>
  arrange(Condition, Run)

# Create reduced sample design
sample_design_no_group4 <- sample_design |>
  filter(as.character(Batch) != "Group 4") |>
  mutate(
    Batch = droplevels(factor(Batch)),
    Condition = droplevels(factor(Condition))
  )

# Document exclusion
group4_exclusion_summary <- data.frame(
  Criterion = c(
    "Original QC-retained runs",
    "Excluded Group 4 runs",
    "Runs retained after Group 4 exclusion",
    "Conditions retained"
  ),
  Value = c(
    nrow(sample_design_before_group4),
    nrow(group4_excluded_runs),
    nrow(sample_design_no_group4),
    dplyr::n_distinct(sample_design_no_group4$Condition)
  )
)

print(group4_exclusion_summary)
print(group4_excluded_runs)

# Verify expected sample counts
stopifnot(
  nrow(sample_design_before_group4) == 83,
  nrow(group4_excluded_runs) == 15,
  nrow(sample_design_no_group4) == 68,
  dplyr::n_distinct(sample_design_no_group4$Condition) == 8,
  !any(as.character(sample_design_no_group4$Batch) == "Group 4")
)

# Confirm that the reduced batch-adjusted design is full rank
design_no_group4 <- model.matrix(
  ~ 0 + Condition + Batch,
  data = sample_design_no_group4
)

group4_design_check <- data.frame(
  Parameters = ncol(design_no_group4),
  Rank = qr(design_no_group4)$rank,
  Full_rank = qr(design_no_group4)$rank ==
    ncol(design_no_group4)
)

print(group4_design_check)

# Save the exclusion record
saveRDS(
  list(
    rationale = paste(
      "Group 4 excluded following concordant JUN and",
      "proteome-wide genotype QC anomalies across four",
      "DIA pipelines; sample mislabeling remains unconfirmed."
    ),
    excluded_runs = group4_excluded_runs,
    sample_design_original = sample_design_before_group4,
    sample_design_reduced = sample_design_no_group4,
    exclusion_summary = group4_exclusion_summary,
    design_check = group4_design_check
  ),
  file = file.path("Outputs/group4_exclusion_record.rds")
)

```


### - JUN Precursor

```{r}
# ============================================================
# JUN (P05412): normalized precursor intensities
# CTRL vs KO across five acquisition batches
# ============================================================
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("cache_dir", "software_names", "sample_design")))
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

jun_accession <- "P05412"

filtered_qf_files <- setNames(
  file.path(
    cache_dir,
    paste0("qf_", software_names, "_filtered_final.rds")
  ),
  software_names
)

# Match accession exactly, including semicolon-separated
# protein groups and UniProt-style sp|P05412|JUN_HUMAN IDs
has_accession <- function(ids, accession) {
  
  vapply(as.character(ids), function(id) {
    
    if (is.na(id) || !nzchar(trimws(id))) {
      return(FALSE)
    }
    
    members <- trimws(
      strsplit(id, "[;,]")[[1]]
    )
    
    members <- sub(
      "^(sp|tr)\\|([^|]+)\\|.*$",
      "\\2",
      members
    )
    
    any(members == accession)
    
  }, logical(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}

median_list <- list()
jun_summary <- list()

for (software in software_names) {
  
  message("Processing JUN: ", software)
  
  qf_one <- readRDS(filtered_qf_files[[software]])
  
  se <- qf_one[["precursors_norm"]]
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 1. Identify JUN-associated precursors
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  
  stopifnot(
    "Protein.Group" %in%
      colnames(SummarizedExperiment::rowData(se))
  )
  
  protein_ids <- as.character(
    SummarizedExperiment::rowData(se)[["Protein.Group"]]
  )
  
  jun_idx <- has_accession(
    protein_ids,
    jun_accession
  )
  
  n_jun <- sum(jun_idx)
  
  message(
    software, ": ",
    n_jun,
    " JUN-associated precursors identified"
  )
  
  if (n_jun == 0L) {
    warning(software, ": JUN accession not found")
    next
  }
  
  # Subset BEFORE extracting intensity matrix
  se_jun <- se[jun_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  
  x <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(
    se_jun,
    withDimnames = FALSE
  )
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 2. Extract sample annotations
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  
  runs <- colnames(se_jun)
  
  genotype <- as.character(
    SummarizedExperiment::colData(se_jun)$genotype
  )
  
  batch <- dplyr::case_when(
    grepl("^20260331_", runs) ~ "20260331",
    grepl("^Group1_", runs) ~ "Group1",
    grepl("^Group2_", runs) ~ "Group2",
    grepl("^Group3_", runs) ~ "Group3",
    grepl("^Group4_", runs) ~ "Group4",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )
  
  stopifnot(
    length(genotype) == ncol(se_jun),
    !anyNA(genotype),
    !anyNA(batch),
    all(genotype %in% c("CTRL", "KO"))
  )
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 3. Calculate JUN median intensity per run
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  
  run_medians <- vapply(
    seq_len(ncol(x)),
    function(j) {
      
      values <- x[, j]
      values <- values[is.finite(values)]
      
      if (!length(values)) return(NA_real_)
      
      stats::median(values)
    },
    numeric(1)
  )
  
  median_list[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Run = runs,
    Batch = batch,
    Genotype = genotype,
    Median_Log2 = run_medians
  )
  
  jun_summary[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    JUN_Precursors = n_jun,
    JUN_Protein_Groups = length(unique(protein_ids[jun_idx])),
    Total_Runs = length(runs),
    Quantified_Runs = sum(is.finite(run_medians))
  )
  
  rm(qf_one, se, se_jun, x, protein_ids,
     jun_idx, run_medians)
  
  invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))
}

# ============================================================
# 4. Combine data and calculate genotype summaries
# ============================================================

median_data <- dplyr::bind_rows(median_list) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Software = factor(
      Software,
      levels = software_names
    ),
    Batch = factor(
      Batch,
      levels = c("20260331", paste0("Group", 1:4))
    ),
    Genotype = factor(
      Genotype,
      levels = c("CTRL", "KO")
    )
  )

median_summary <- median_data |>
  dplyr::filter(is.finite(Median_Log2)) |>
```

### - JUN Protein

```{r}
# ============================================================
# JUN (P05412): normalized protein intensities
# CTRL vs KO across five acquisition batches
# ============================================================
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("cache_dir", "software_names", "sample_design")))
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

jun_accession <- "P05412"

filtered_qf_files <- setNames(
  file.path(
    cache_dir,
    paste0("qf_", software_names, "_filtered_final.rds")
  ),
  software_names
)

# Match accession exactly, including semicolon-separated
# protein groups and UniProt-style sp|P05412|JUN_HUMAN IDs
has_accession <- function(ids, accession) {
  
  vapply(as.character(ids), function(id) {
    
    if (is.na(id) || !nzchar(trimws(id))) {
      return(FALSE)
    }
    
    members <- trimws(
      strsplit(id, "[;,]")[[1]]
    )
    
    members <- sub(
      "^(sp|tr)\\|([^|]+)\\|.*$",
      "\\2",
      members
    )
    
    any(members == accession)
    
  }, logical(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}

median_list <- list()
jun_summary <- list()

for (software in software_names) {
  
  message("Processing JUN: ", software)
  
  qf_one <- readRDS(filtered_qf_files[[software]])
  
  se <- qf_one[["proteins"]]
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 1. Identify JUN-associated precursors
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  
  stopifnot(
    "Protein.Group" %in%
      colnames(SummarizedExperiment::rowData(se))
  )
  
  protein_ids <- as.character(
    SummarizedExperiment::rowData(se)[["Protein.Group"]]
  )
  
  jun_idx <- has_accession(
    protein_ids,
    jun_accession
  )
  
  n_jun <- sum(jun_idx)
  
  message(
    software, ": ",
    n_jun,
    " JUN-associated precursors identified"
  )
  
  if (n_jun == 0L) {
    warning(software, ": JUN accession not found")
    next
  }
  
  # Subset BEFORE extracting intensity matrix
  se_jun <- se[jun_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  
  x <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(
    se_jun,
    withDimnames = FALSE
  )
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 2. Extract sample annotations
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  
  runs <- colnames(se_jun)
  
  genotype <- as.character(
    SummarizedExperiment::colData(se_jun)$genotype
  )
  
  batch <- dplyr::case_when(
    grepl("^20260331_", runs) ~ "20260331",
    grepl("^Group1_", runs) ~ "Group1",
    grepl("^Group2_", runs) ~ "Group2",
    grepl("^Group3_", runs) ~ "Group3",
    grepl("^Group4_", runs) ~ "Group4",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )
  
  stopifnot(
    length(genotype) == ncol(se_jun),
    !anyNA(genotype),
    !anyNA(batch),
    all(genotype %in% c("CTRL", "KO"))
  )
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 3. Calculate JUN median intensity per run
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  
  run_medians <- vapply(
    seq_len(ncol(x)),
    function(j) {
      
      values <- x[, j]
      values <- values[is.finite(values)]
      
      if (!length(values)) return(NA_real_)
      
      stats::median(values)
    },
    numeric(1)
  )
  
  median_list[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Run = runs,
    Batch = batch,
    Genotype = genotype,
    Median_Log2 = run_medians
  )
  
  jun_summary[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    JUN_Precursors = n_jun,
    JUN_Protein_Groups = length(unique(protein_ids[jun_idx])),
    Total_Runs = length(runs),
    Quantified_Runs = sum(is.finite(run_medians))
  )
  
  rm(qf_one, se, se_jun, x, protein_ids,
     jun_idx, run_medians)
  
  invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))
}
```

## 18. Filtering out Group4 batch

```{r exclude_group4_68runs}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Preserve original 83-run objects
# ------------------------------------------------------------
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("cache_dir", "software_names", "sample_design")))
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

filtered_qf_files <- setNames(
  file.path(cache_dir, paste0("qf_", software_names, "_filtered_final.rds")),
  software_names
)

qf_alpha <- readRDS(filtered_qf_files[["AlphaDIA"]])
qf_diann <- readRDS(filtered_qf_files[["DIANN"]])
qf_spectro <- readRDS(filtered_qf_files[["Spectronaut"]])
qf_maxdia <- readRDS(filtered_qf_files[["MaxDIA"]])

qf_models <- list(
  AlphaDIA = qf_alpha,
  `DIA-NN` = qf_diann,
  Spectronaut = qf_spectro,
  MaxDIA = qf_maxdia
)

qf_models_83 <- qf_models
sample_design_83 <- sample_design

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Define the 68 retained runs
# ------------------------------------------------------------

sample_design_68 <- sample_design_83 |>
  filter(as.character(Batch) != "Group 4") |>
  mutate(
    Batch = droplevels(factor(Batch)),
    Condition = droplevels(factor(Condition))
  )

runs_68 <- as.character(sample_design_68$Run)

stopifnot(
  nrow(sample_design_83) == 83,
  length(runs_68) == 68,
  !anyDuplicated(runs_68)
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Filter every assay in each QFeatures object
# ------------------------------------------------------------

qf_models_68 <- lapply(qf_models_83, function(qf) {

  # Subset each assay to the retained runs
  for (assay_name in names(qf)) {

    se <- qf[[assay_name]]

    keep <- colnames(se) %in% runs_68

    qf[[assay_name]] <- se[, keep, drop = FALSE]
  }

  qf
})

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Verify sample counts and absence of Group 4
# ------------------------------------------------------------

sample_counts_68 <- data.frame(
  Software = names(qf_models_68),
  Samples = vapply(
  qf_models_68,
  function(qf) ncol(qf[["proteins"]]),
  integer(1)
  ))

print(sample_counts_68)

stopifnot(
  all(sample_counts_68$Samples == 68),
  !any(as.character(sample_design_68$Batch) == "Group 4")
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Check batch-adjusted experimental design
# ------------------------------------------------------------

design_matrix_68 <- model.matrix(
  ~ 0 + Condition + Batch,
  data = sample_design_68
)

design_check_68 <- data.frame(
  Parameters = ncol(design_matrix_68),
  Rank = qr(design_matrix_68)$rank,
  Full_rank = qr(design_matrix_68)$rank ==
    ncol(design_matrix_68)
)

print(design_check_68)

if (!design_check_68$Full_rank) {
  warning(
    "The 68-run batch-adjusted design is not full rank. ",
    "Review estimability before refitting models."
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Save filtered objects for downstream analyses
# ------------------------------------------------------------

saveRDS(
  list(
    qf_models = qf_models_68,
    sample_design = sample_design_68,
    excluded_runs = setdiff(
      sample_design_83$Run,
      sample_design_68$Run
    )
  ),
  file = paste0(cache_dir, "/qf_models_68runs.rds")
)

cat("\n68-run QFeatures dataset prepared successfully.\n")
```
- Exclusion of acquisition Group 4 following biological quality control

Biological quality control revealed an acquisition-batch-specific inconsistency in the expected c-Jun knockout phenotype. In Group 4, the anticipated reduction in JUN abundance in knockout (KO) relative to control (CTRL) samples was absent or reversed across the four DIA analysis pipelines. Examination of individual JUN peptides and proteome-wide genotype-associated signatures further supported this observation. In particular, leave-one-batch-out validation showed that Group 4 was the only acquisition batch consistently lacking the expected genotype-associated proteomic separation. Although these findings do not establish the underlying cause or confirm sample mislabeling, they raise concerns regarding the biological validity of the affected samples. Consequently, all 15 Group 4 runs were excluded from the primary downstream analyses, leaving 68 runs across eight experimental conditions. The supporting biological QC results are presented in Supplementary Figure S[X]. The original 83-run dataset was retained for sensitivity analyses.

- Exploratory assessment of the retained 68-run dataset

Following exclusion, protein-level multidimensional scaling (MDS), experimental condition–batch balance, and sample-to-sample Spearman correlations were reassessed using the 68 retained runs. These analyses were used to characterize the remaining batch-associated variation and evaluate the experimental design before differential abundance modeling.

### - 68 Protein-level MDS

```{r protein_mds_qc, fig.width=15, fig.height=11, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Protein-level MDS: four DIA software packages
# Complete-case proteins, 68 retained LC-MS runs
# ============================================================
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("cache_dir", "software_names",
                          "qf_models_68", "sample_design_68",
                          "proteins_68", "software_order")))
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

mds_list <- list()
mds_summary <- list()

for (software in software_order) {

  message("Running protein-level MDS: ", software)

  se <- proteins_68[[software]]
  x <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(se)

  # Retain proteins quantified in all 68 runs
  keep <- rowSums(is.finite(x)) == ncol(x)

  se_complete <- se[keep, , drop = FALSE]

  stopifnot(nrow(se_complete) >= 2L)

  sce <- as(se_complete, "SingleCellExperiment")

  sce <- scater::runMDS(sce,exprs_values = 1)

  coords <- as.data.frame(
    SingleCellExperiment::reducedDim(sce, "MDS")
  )

  colnames(coords)[1:2] <- c("MDS1", "MDS2")

  # Use the shared, verified sample design
  metadata <- sample_design_68[
    match(colnames(se_complete), sample_design_68$Run),
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  stopifnot(!anyNA(metadata$Run))

  coords$Software <- software
  coords$Run <- metadata$Run
  coords$Condition <- as.character(metadata$Condition)
  coords$Batch <- as.character(metadata$Batch)

  mds_list[[software]] <- coords

  mds_summary[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Proteins_Used = sum(keep),
    Runs = ncol(se_complete)
  )
}
```

- Protein-level dimensionality reduction

Protein-level multidimensional scaling (MDS) was performed independently for AlphaDIA, DIA-NN, Spectronaut, and MaxDIA using the 68 retained LC-MS runs. The analysis included 8,901, 7,570, 7,594, and 7,518 complete-case protein groups, respectively. MDS plots revealed pronounced acquisition-batch-associated clustering across all four pipelines. AlphaDIA, DIA-NN, and Spectronaut exhibited clearly separated batch-associated clusters, whereas MaxDIA showed greater dispersion and partial overlap between batches. In contrast, samples from different experimental conditions frequently occupied overlapping regions within the MDS space, indicating that acquisition batch was more strongly associated with the dominant axes of protein-level variation than experimental condition. These patterns demonstrate that substantial batch-associated variation remained after normalization and exclusion of Group 4.

```{r qc_condition_batch_balance, fig.width=12, fig.height=7, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
    title = "Experimental condition distribution across acquisition batches",
    subtitle = "68 retained LC-MS runs after Group 4 exclusion",
    x = "Acquisition batch",
    y = "Experimental condition",
    fill = "Runs"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank()
  )

print(p_condition_batch)

# Check estimability of the additive condition + batch design
design_68 <- stats::model.matrix(
  ~ 0 + Condition + Batch,
  data = sample_design_68
)

cat(
  "\nDesign rank:",
  qr(design_68)$rank,
  "of",
  ncol(design_68),
  "\n"
)

stopifnot(qr(design_68)$rank == ncol(design_68))
```

- Experimental condition distribution across acquisition batches

Following exclusion of Group 4, the dataset comprised 68 samples across eight experimental conditions and four acquisition batches. Untreated CTRL and KO samples were represented in all four batches, with 15 and 14 samples, respectively. The 24-hour treatment conditions were represented across Groups 1 and 2 and batch 20260331, whereas all three 6-hour treatment conditions were restricted to Group 3, with three replicates per condition. The additive experimental design incorporating condition and acquisition batch was full rank (11 of 11 parameters), supporting estimation of the corresponding model coefficients. Nevertheless, the incomplete crossing of treatment duration and acquisition batch limits the interpretation of direct comparisons between 6-hour and 24-hour responses, which may be influenced by batch-associated variation.


### - 68 Protein level Spearman correlation matrices

```{r qc_protein_spearman_correlation, fig.width=14, fig.height=12, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Protein-level Spearman sample correlation matrices
# 68 retained runs
# ============================================================

correlation_matrices <- list()
correlation_plot_data <- list()
correlation_summary <- list()

ordered_runs <- sample_design_68$Run[
  order(
    sample_design_68$Batch,
    sample_design_68$Condition,
    sample_design_68$Run
  )
]

batch_lookup <- setNames(
  as.character(sample_design_68$Batch),
  sample_design_68$Run
)

for (software in software_order) {

  message("Calculating correlations: ", software)

  se <- proteins_68[[software]]
  x <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(se)

  cor_mat <- stats::cor(
    x,
    method = "spearman",
    use = "pairwise.complete.obs"
  )

  cor_mat <- cor_mat[
    ordered_runs,
    ordered_runs,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  correlation_matrices[[software]] <- cor_mat

  plot_data <- as.data.frame(as.table(cor_mat))

  colnames(plot_data) <- c(
    "Run1", "Run2", "Correlation"
  )

  plot_data$Software <- software

  correlation_plot_data[[software]] <- plot_data

  # Summarize unique sample pairs (exclude diagonal)
  pair_idx <- which(
    upper.tri(cor_mat),
    arr.ind = TRUE
  )

  pair_data <- data.frame(
    Correlation = cor_mat[pair_idx],
    Run1 = rownames(cor_mat)[pair_idx[, 1]],
    Run2 = colnames(cor_mat)[pair_idx[, 2]]
  )

  pair_data$Same_Batch <- batch_lookup[pair_data$Run1] == batch_lookup[pair_data$Run2]

  correlation_summary[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Median_Within_Batch = median(
      pair_data$Correlation[pair_data$Same_Batch],
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    Median_Between_Batch = median(
      pair_data$Correlation[!pair_data$Same_Batch],
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    Minimum_Correlation = min(
      pair_data$Correlation,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    Median_Correlation = median(
      pair_data$Correlation,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  )
}

correlation_plot_data <- dplyr::bind_rows(correlation_plot_data)

correlation_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(correlation_summary)

print(correlation_summary)

correlation_plot_data$Run1 <- factor(
  correlation_plot_data$Run1,
  levels = ordered_runs
)

correlation_plot_data$Run2 <- factor(
  correlation_plot_data$Run2,
  levels = rev(ordered_runs)
)

correlation_plot_data$Software <- factor(
  correlation_plot_data$Software,
  levels = software_order
)

p_correlation <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  correlation_plot_data,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = Run1,
    y = Run2,
    fill = Correlation
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile() +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(
    ~ Software,
    ncol = 2
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "viridis",
    limits = c(0, 1),
    na.value = "grey90"
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_fixed() +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Protein-level Spearman correlation matrices",
    subtitle = "68 retained runs per pipeline, ordered by acquisition batch",
    x = "LC-MS run",
    y = "LC-MS run",
    fill = "Spearman\ncorrelation"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),

print(p_correlation)
```
- Protein-level sample correlations

Sample-to-sample Spearman correlation analysis revealed substantial differences in quantitative consistency among the four DIA pipelines. DIA-NN exhibited the highest median correlation (0.978), followed by AlphaDIA (0.869), Spectronaut (0.829), and MaxDIA (0.720). Within-batch correlations were consistently higher than between-batch correlations, with median values of 0.922 versus 0.850 for AlphaDIA, 0.985 versus 0.976 for DIA-NN, 0.899 versus 0.814 for Spectronaut, and 0.786 versus 0.715 for MaxDIA. The correlation heatmaps showed corresponding block-like patterns associated with acquisition batch, particularly in AlphaDIA, Spectronaut, and MaxDIA. Together with the MDS results, these observations indicate that batch-associated variation remains an important feature of the retained dataset and should be accounted for in subsequent differential abundance analyses.


# - - - - - - - - - - 
## 19. Data modeling
The experimental design also shows that 6-hour treatments were acquired in Groups 3–4, while 24-hour treatments were acquired in Groups 1–2 and 20260331.
This means direct 6-hour versus 24-hour comparisons are particularly vulnerable to batch confounding. However, comparisons such as KO versus CTRL within the same treatment and time point are better supported because those conditions share acquisition batches.

Here, condition represents your eight biological experimental groups, while Batch accounts for systematic differences between the five acquisition batches.
```{r}
model <- ~ Batch + condition
```

### - Construct and evaluate the design matrix

```{r qc_design_matrix, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Design matrix diagnostics before protein-level modeling
# ============================================================
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("cache_dir", "software_names", "sample_design")))
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

filtered_qf_files <- setNames(
  file.path(cache_dir, paste0("qf_", software_names, "_filtered_final.rds")),
  software_names
)

qf_alpha <- readRDS(filtered_qf_files[["AlphaDIA"]])

se <- qf_alpha[["proteins"]]

design_data <- data.frame(
  Run = colnames(se),
  condition = as.character(colData(se)$condition),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Infer acquisition batch from run names
design_data$Batch <- dplyr::case_when(
  grepl("^Group1_", design_data$Run) ~ "Group1",
  grepl("^Group2_", design_data$Run) ~ "Group2",
  grepl("^Group3_", design_data$Run) ~ "Group3",
  grepl("^Group4_", design_data$Run) ~ "Group4",
  grepl("^20260331_", design_data$Run) ~ "20260331",
  TRUE ~ NA_character_
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(design_data) == 83L,
  !anyNA(design_data$condition),
  !anyNA(design_data$Batch),
  !anyDuplicated(design_data$Run)
)

# Define reference levels
design_data$condition <- factor(
  design_data$condition,
  levels = c(
    "CTRL_Untreated_Baseline",
    "KO_Untreated_Baseline",
    "CTRL_cDDP_6h",
    "KO_cDDP_6h",
    "CTRL_JNK_IN_8_cDDP_6h",
    "CTRL_cDDP_24h",
    "KO_cDDP_24h",
    "CTRL_JNK_IN_8_cDDP_24h"
  )
)

design_data$Batch <- factor(
  design_data$Batch,
  levels = c(
    "Group1", "Group2", "Group3",
    "Group4", "20260331"
  )
)

stopifnot(!anyNA(design_data$condition))

# Batch-adjusted model
model <- ~ Batch + condition

design_matrix <- stats::model.matrix(
  model,
  data = design_data
)

# Evaluate matrix rank
design_rank <- qr(design_matrix)$rank
n_parameters <- ncol(design_matrix)

design_summary <- data.frame(
  Runs = nrow(design_matrix),
  Parameters = n_parameters,
  Rank = design_rank,
  Full_Rank = design_rank == n_parameters,
  Residual_DF = nrow(design_matrix) - design_rank
)

print(design_summary)

cat("\nDesign matrix columns:\n")
print(colnames(design_matrix))

cat("\nCondition by batch:\n")
print(table(
  design_data$condition,
  design_data$Batch
))

# Identify non-estimable coefficients if rank deficient
if (design_rank < n_parameters) {

  aliased <- stats::alias(
    stats::lm(
      stats::rnorm(nrow(design_data)) ~
        Batch + condition,
      data = design_data
    )
  )

  print(aliased$Complete)

} else {
  cat("\nDesign matrix is full rank.\n")
}
```


### - Evaluate biologically relevant contrasts
The most informative comparisons include genotype effects, cisplatin treatment effects, and the effect of adding JNK-IN-8 to cisplatin-treated CTRL samples. We can test whether these contrasts are estimable under the batch-adjusted model and whether the compared conditions share acquisition batches.
```{r qc_contrast_estimability, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Evaluate planned biological contrasts
# ============================================================

planned_contrasts <- data.frame(
  Contrast = c(
    "KO vs CTRL baseline",
    "KO vs CTRL cisplatin 6h",
    "KO vs CTRL cisplatin 24h",
    "CTRL cisplatin 6h vs baseline",
    "CTRL cisplatin 24h vs baseline",
    "KO cisplatin 6h vs baseline",
    "KO cisplatin 24h vs baseline",
    "JNK inhibitor effect at 6h",
    "JNK inhibitor effect at 24h",
    "CTRL cisplatin 24h vs 6h",
    "KO cisplatin 24h vs 6h"
  ),
  Numerator = c(
    "KO_Untreated_Baseline",
    "KO_cDDP_6h",
    "KO_cDDP_24h",
    "CTRL_cDDP_6h",
    "CTRL_cDDP_24h",
    "KO_cDDP_6h",
    "KO_cDDP_24h",
    "CTRL_JNK_IN_8_cDDP_6h",
    "CTRL_JNK_IN_8_cDDP_24h",
    "CTRL_cDDP_24h",
    "KO_cDDP_24h"
  ),
  Denominator = c(
    "CTRL_Untreated_Baseline",
    "CTRL_cDDP_6h",
    "CTRL_cDDP_24h",
    "CTRL_Untreated_Baseline",
    "CTRL_Untreated_Baseline",
    "KO_Untreated_Baseline",
    "KO_Untreated_Baseline",
    "CTRL_cDDP_6h",
    "CTRL_cDDP_24h",
    "CTRL_cDDP_6h",
    "KO_cDDP_6h"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Construct model-matrix rows for each condition
# at the same reference acquisition batch.
reference_data <- data.frame(
  Batch = factor(
    rep("Group1", nlevels(design_data$condition)),
    levels = levels(design_data$Batch)
  ),
  condition = factor(
    levels(design_data$condition),
    levels = levels(design_data$condition)
  )
)

reference_matrix <- stats::model.matrix(
  model,
  data = reference_data
)

rownames(reference_matrix) <- as.character(
  reference_data$condition
)

# The row space of X determines estimability.
# SVD gives a numerical basis for its null space.
sv <- svd(design_matrix, nu = 0, nv = ncol(design_matrix))

tol <- max(dim(design_matrix)) *
  max(sv$d) *
  .Machine$double.eps

rank_svd <- sum(sv$d > tol)

null_basis <- if (rank_svd < ncol(design_matrix)) {
  sv$v[, seq.int(rank_svd + 1L, ncol(design_matrix)),
       drop = FALSE]
} else {
  matrix(0, nrow = ncol(design_matrix), ncol = 0)
}

# Count acquisition batches shared by both conditions
batch_sets <- lapply(
  levels(design_data$condition),
  function(cond) {
    as.character(design_data$Batch[
      design_data$condition == cond
    ])
  }
)

names(batch_sets) <- levels(design_data$condition)

contrast_results <- lapply(
  seq_len(nrow(planned_contrasts)),
  function(i) {

    numerator <- planned_contrasts$Numerator[i]
    denominator <- planned_contrasts$Denominator[i]

    contrast_vector <-
      reference_matrix[numerator, ] -
      reference_matrix[denominator, ]

    # A contrast is estimable if orthogonal to
    # every vector in the design matrix null space.
    max_null_component <- if (ncol(null_basis) == 0L) {
      0
    } else {
      max(abs(drop(contrast_vector %*% null_basis)))
    }

    shared_batches <- intersect(
      unique(batch_sets[[numerator]]),
      unique(batch_sets[[denominator]])
    )

    data.frame(
      Contrast = planned_contrasts$Contrast[i],
      Estimable = max_null_component < 1e-8,
      Shared_Batches = length(shared_batches),
      Batch_Names = if (length(shared_batches)) {
        paste(shared_batches, collapse = ", ")
      } else {
        "None"
      },
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }
)

contrast_estimability <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  contrast_results
)

print(contrast_estimability, row.names = FALSE)
```
Nine of the eleven contrasts have direct within-batch support. These should be the primary focus of your differential abundance analysis.

The two 24 h versus 6 h comparisons are mathematically estimable but have no shared acquisition batches. Their estimates depend on the additive batch-effect assumption and the untreated samples that connect batches. I recommend treating these as exploratory rather than primary contrasts.

Although the overall design supports these contrasts, individual proteins may have missing observations. A protein measured only in certain batches or conditions may not support every contrast, even when the overall design matrix is full rank.

# 68 Data modeling
Following the exclusion of acquisition Group 4, the primary analysis comprised 68 LC-MS runs across eight experimental conditions and four acquisition batches. The 6-hour treatment conditions were represented exclusively in Group 3, whereas the 24-hour treatment conditions were distributed across Groups 1, 2, and 20260331. Untreated CTRL and KO samples were represented across all four retained batches.

Protein-level differential abundance was modeled using experimental condition and acquisition batch as additive fixed effects. This approach accounts for systematic batch-associated differences while estimating condition-specific abundance changes. Comparisons between conditions represented within the same acquisition batches have direct within-batch support. In contrast, comparisons between 6-hour and 24-hour treatment conditions lack direct within-batch replication and therefore depend more strongly on the assumption of additive batch effects.

```{r qc_contrast_estimability_68, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

stopifnot(

        levels(design_data_68$condition)),
  all(planned_contrasts_68$Denominator %in%

)

# Construct reference design rows for every condition.
# All conditions are evaluated at the same batch level,
# so the additive batch coefficients cancel in contrasts.

reference_data_68 <- data.frame(
  Batch = factor(
    rep("Group1", nlevels(design_data_68$condition)),

  ),

stopifnot(
  identical(
    colnames(reference_matrix_68),

  )
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Identify the null space of the design matrix
# ------------------------------------------------------------

sv_68 <- svd(
  design_matrix_68,
  nu = 0,
  nv = ncol(design_matrix_68)
)

tol_68 <- max(dim(design_matrix_68)) *
  max(sv_68$d) *
  .Machine$double.eps

rank_svd_68 <- sum(sv_68$d > tol_68)

null_basis_68 <- if (
  rank_svd_68 < ncol(design_matrix_68)
) {
  sv_68$v[
    ,
    seq.int(rank_svd_68 + 1L, ncol(design_matrix_68)),
    drop = FALSE
  ]
} else {

    nrow = ncol(design_matrix_68),

)

names(batch_sets_68) <- levels(design_data_68$condition)

    denominator <- planned_contrasts_68$Denominator[i]

    contrast_vector <-
      reference_matrix_68[numerator, ] -
      reference_matrix_68[denominator, ]

      ncol(null_basis_68) == 0L
    ) {

    } else {
      max(abs(drop(
        contrast_vector %*% null_basis_68
      )))
    }

    shared_batches <- intersect(
      batch_sets_68[[numerator]],

    )

    data.frame(
      Contrast = planned_contrasts_68$Contrast[i],
      Estimable = max_null_component < 1e-8,

      Batch_Names = if (length(shared_batches)) {
        paste(shared_batches, collapse = ", ")
      } else {

      },

)
```

## Protein-level missingness and contrast-specific data availability
```{r qc_protein_contrast_availability, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Protein-level missingness and contrast-specific availability
# ============================================================

qf_list <- list(
  AlphaDIA = qf_alpha,
  `DIA-NN` = qf_diann,
  Spectronaut = qf_spectro,
  MaxDIA = qf_maxdia
)

protein_availability <- list()
contrast_availability <- list()

for (software in names(qf_list)) {

  se <- qf_list[[software]][["proteins"]]
  x <- assay(se)

  # Match sample annotations to assay column order
  metadata <- design_data[
    match(colnames(x), design_data$Run),
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  stopifnot(
    !anyNA(metadata$Run),
    identical(as.character(metadata$Run), colnames(x))
  )

  detected <- is.finite(x)
  n_proteins <- nrow(x)
  n_runs <- ncol(x)

  # Overall protein completeness
  n_detected <- rowSums(detected)

  protein_availability[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Total_Proteins = n_proteins,
    Runs = n_runs,
    Complete_Proteins = sum(n_detected == n_runs),
    Complete_Percent = 100 * mean(n_detected == n_runs),
    Median_Detected_Runs = median(n_detected),
    Proteins_At_Least_Half_Runs = sum(
      n_detected >= ceiling(n_runs / 2)
    )
  )

  # Counts of detected observations by condition
  condition_counts <- sapply(
    levels(metadata$condition),
    function(cond) {
      rowSums(
        detected[, metadata$condition == cond, drop = FALSE]
      )
    }
  )

  # Counts by condition AND batch
  condition_batch_counts <- list()

  for (cond in levels(metadata$condition)) {
    for (batch in levels(metadata$Batch)) {

      idx <- metadata$condition == cond &
        metadata$Batch == batch

      key <- paste(cond, batch, sep = "||")

      condition_batch_counts[[key]] <- if (any(idx)) {
        rowSums(detected[, idx, drop = FALSE])
      } else {
        integer(n_proteins)
      }
    }
  }

  # Evaluate each planned contrast
  contrast_rows <- vector(
    "list",
    nrow(planned_contrasts)
  )

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(planned_contrasts))) {

    numerator <- planned_contrasts$Numerator[i]
    denominator <- planned_contrasts$Denominator[i]

    n_num <- condition_counts[, numerator]
    n_den <- condition_counts[, denominator]

    # Preliminary minimum: >=2 observations per condition
    both_groups <- n_num >= 2 & n_den >= 2

    # A shared batch must contain at least one
    # observed sample from each condition
    shared_batch_support <- rep(FALSE, n_proteins)

    for (batch in levels(metadata$Batch)) {

      num_key <- paste(numerator, batch, sep = "||")
      den_key <- paste(denominator, batch, sep = "||")

      shared_batch_support <- shared_batch_support |
        (
          condition_batch_counts[[num_key]] >= 1 &
          condition_batch_counts[[den_key]] >= 1
        )
    }

    both_and_shared <- both_groups & shared_batch_support

    contrast_rows[[i]] <- data.frame(
      Software = software,
      Contrast = planned_contrasts$Contrast[i],
      Total_Proteins = n_proteins,
      Both_Groups_At_Least_2 = sum(both_groups),
      Both_Groups_Percent = 100 * mean(both_groups),
      Shared_Batch_Support = sum(shared_batch_support),
      Both_And_Shared_Batch = sum(both_and_shared),
      Both_And_Shared_Percent = 100 * mean(both_and_shared),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }

  contrast_availability[[software]] <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    contrast_rows
  )
}

protein_availability_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  protein_availability
)

contrast_availability_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  contrast_availability
)

# Overall summary
print(protein_availability_summary)

# Contrast-specific summary
print(
  contrast_availability_summary |>
    dplyr::select(
      Software,
      Contrast,
      Both_Groups_At_Least_2,
      Both_Groups_Percent,
      Shared_Batch_Support,
      Both_And_Shared_Batch
    ),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
These are strong protein-level completeness results across all four pipelines.

A few observations:
- AlphaDIA quantifies the largest number of proteins.
- Spectronaut has the highest completeness (95.1%), although its previously observed low-intensity reporting floor remains a caveat.
- MaxDIA shows considerably better completeness at protein level than at precursor level, consistent with MaxLFQ aggregation combining information across precursors.
- All four tools have a median detection frequency of 83 runs, meaning at least half their proteins are quantified in every sample.
Importantly, MaxLFQ protein aggregation has substantially reduced the missingness observed at precursor level.

Protein-level missingness is unlikely to be a major limitation for differential abundance analysis across the four DIA pipelines.
Across all 11 planned comparisons, the percentage of proteins quantified in at least two samples in both conditions is:
Software	Range across contrasts	Interpretation
AlphaDIA	98.5–100%	Excellent availability
DIA-NN	97.9–99.8%	Excellent availability
Spectronaut	99.96–100%	Nearly complete
MaxDIA	99.94–99.99%	Nearly complete

This is particularly reassuring because the 6-hour treatment groups contain only six replicates each.

Although the 6 h and 24 h conditions do not share batches, untreated samples connect the groups statistically. Therefore, their contrasts can be estimable under the additive model. But they rely more strongly on assumptions about batch effects. I recommend keeping these two time comparisons as exploratory analyses.


In other word, Protein-level data availability was high across all four DIA analysis pipelines. Between 97.9% and 100% of quantified proteins had at least two observations in each condition for the planned contrasts. Nine of the eleven comparisons had direct within-batch support, whereas comparisons between 6-hour and 24-hour cisplatin treatments lacked overlapping acquisition batches. Although these time-point contrasts were mathematically estimable under the additive batch-adjusted design, their interpretation requires caution because treatment duration and acquisition batch were partially confounded. Overall, the results support proceeding with batch-adjusted differential abundance modeling without additional global completeness filtering.


```{r qc_protein_specific_estimability, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Protein-specific design rank and contrast estimability
# ============================================================

qf_list <- list(
  AlphaDIA = qf_alpha,
  `DIA-NN` = qf_diann,
  Spectronaut = qf_spectro,
  MaxDIA = qf_maxdia
)

# Reconstruct contrast vectors from the existing design matrix
contrast_matrix <- t(vapply(
  seq_len(nrow(planned_contrasts)),
  function(i) {
    reference_matrix[planned_contrasts$Numerator[i], ] -
      reference_matrix[planned_contrasts$Denominator[i], ]
  },
  numeric(ncol(design_matrix))
))

rownames(contrast_matrix) <- planned_contrasts$Contrast

# Verify that contrast coefficients match the design matrix
stopifnot(
  identical(
    colnames(contrast_matrix),
    colnames(design_matrix)
  ),
  nrow(design_matrix) == nrow(design_data)
)

# Assign actual run names to the design matrix
rownames(design_matrix) <- as.character(design_data$Run)

# Confirm alignment
stopifnot(
  identical(
    rownames(design_matrix),
    as.character(design_data$Run)
  )
)

# Function to evaluate a single observed-sample pattern
check_pattern <- function(observed, X, C) {

  X_obs <- X[observed, , drop = FALSE]

  if (nrow(X_obs) == 0L) {
    return(c(
      Rank = 0,
      Full_Rank = 0,
      setNames(
        rep(0, nrow(C)),
        paste0("Contrast_", seq_len(nrow(C)))
      )
    ))
  }

  # QR rank of the observed design
  rank_obs <- qr(X_obs)$rank

  # SVD-based row-space test for contrast estimability
  sv <- svd(X_obs, nu = 0, nv = ncol(X_obs))

  tolerance <- max(dim(X_obs)) *
    max(sv$d) *
    .Machine$double.eps

  rank_svd <- sum(sv$d > tolerance)

  if (rank_svd == ncol(X_obs)) {

    estimable <- rep(TRUE, nrow(C))

  } else {

    null_basis <- sv$v[
      ,
      seq.int(rank_svd + 1L, ncol(X_obs)),
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    null_projection <- C %*% null_basis

    estimable <- apply(
      abs(null_projection),
      1,
      max
    ) < 1e-8
  }

  c(
    Rank = rank_obs,
    Full_Rank = as.integer(rank_obs == ncol(X)),
    setNames(
      as.integer(estimable),
      paste0("Contrast_", seq_len(nrow(C)))
    )
  )
}

protein_rank_results <- list()
protein_contrast_results <- list()

for (software in names(qf_list)) {

  cat("Checking:", software, "\n")

  se <- qf_list[[software]][["proteins"]]
  x <- assay(se)

  # Align design matrix to the assay columns
  sample_idx <- match(colnames(x), design_data$Run)

  stopifnot(
    !anyNA(sample_idx),
    !anyDuplicated(sample_idx)
  )

  X <- design_matrix[sample_idx, , drop = FALSE]

  # Finite protein measurements
  detected <- is.finite(x)

  # Group proteins with identical observed-sample patterns
  pattern_key <- apply(
    detected,
    1,
    function(z) paste0(as.integer(z), collapse = "")
  )

  unique_keys <- unique(pattern_key)

  pattern_results <- lapply(unique_keys, function(key) {

    observed <- which(
      strsplit(key, "", fixed = TRUE)[[1]] == "1"
    )

    check_pattern(
      observed = observed,
      X = X,
      C = contrast_matrix
    )
  })

  pattern_results <- do.call(
    rbind,
    pattern_results
  )

  # Map pattern results back to individual proteins
  protein_results <- pattern_results[
    match(pattern_key, unique_keys),
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  protein_rank_results[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Total_Proteins = nrow(x),
    Unique_Missingness_Patterns = length(unique_keys),
    Full_Rank_Proteins = sum(
      protein_results[, "Full_Rank"] == 1
    ),
    Full_Rank_Percent = 100 * mean(
      protein_results[, "Full_Rank"] == 1
    ),
    Median_Protein_Rank = median(
      protein_results[, "Rank"]
    ),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  protein_contrast_results[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Contrast = planned_contrasts$Contrast,
    Estimable_Proteins = colSums(
      protein_results[
        ,
        paste0("Contrast_", seq_len(nrow(contrast_matrix))),
        drop = FALSE
      ]
    ),
    Total_Proteins = nrow(x),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

protein_rank_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  protein_rank_results
)

protein_contrast_estimability <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  protein_contrast_results
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Estimable_Percent =
      100 * Estimable_Proteins / Total_Proteins
  )

cat("\nProtein-specific design rank:\n")
print(protein_rank_summary, row.names = FALSE)

cat("\nProtein-specific contrast estimability:\n")
print(
  protein_contrast_estimability,
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
The median protein-specific design rank is 12 for every software pipeline, matching the number of model coefficients. This means that nearly all proteins have sufficient observations across the experimental conditions and acquisition batches to estimate every coefficient in the proposed model. Importantly, the remaining rank-deficient proteins are not necessarily unusable. Some can still support particular biological contrasts.
Protein-specific design matrix diagnostics demonstrated high model identifiability across all four DIA analysis pipelines. Full-rank design matrices were obtained for 98.04% of AlphaDIA proteins, 97.70% of DIA-NN proteins, 99.99% of Spectronaut proteins, and 99.93% of MaxDIA proteins. Across the eleven planned biological contrasts, mathematical estimability exceeded 98.9% for every pipeline. These findings indicate that protein-level missingness is unlikely to substantially restrict differential abundance analysis. Nevertheless, direct comparisons between 6-hour and 24-hour cisplatin treatments remain dependent on additive batch-effect assumptions because the treatment groups were acquired in separate batches. Therefore, subsequent statistical modeling will incorporate acquisition batch as a fixed effect, with cross-time-point comparisons interpreted cautiously.

## 68 Protein-level missingness and contrast-specific data availability
```{r qc_protein_availability_estimability_68, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# 68-run protein availability and contrast estimability
C <- t(vapply(seq_len(nrow(planned_contrasts_68)), function(i)
  reference_matrix_68[planned_contrasts_68$Numerator[i], ] -
  reference_matrix_68[planned_contrasts_68$Denominator[i], ],
  numeric(ncol(design_matrix_68))))
rownames(C) <- planned_contrasts_68$Contrast

protein_availability_68 <- list()
contrast_availability_68 <- list()
protein_rank_results_68 <- list()
protein_contrast_results_68 <- list()

for (sw in names(proteins_68)) {
  x <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(proteins_68[[sw]])
  idx <- match(colnames(x), design_data_68$Run)
  stopifnot(ncol(x) == 68L, !anyNA(idx))
  meta <- design_data_68[idx, ]
  X <- design_matrix_68[idx, , drop = FALSE]
  d <- is.finite(x)
  n <- nrow(x)
  counts <- rowSums(d)

  protein_availability_68[[sw]] <- data.frame(
    Software = sw, Total_Proteins = n, Runs = ncol(x),
    Complete_Proteins = sum(counts == ncol(x)),
    Complete_Percent = 100 * mean(counts == ncol(x)),
    Median_Detected_Runs = median(counts),
    Proteins_At_Least_Half_Runs = sum(counts >= ceiling(ncol(x)/2))
  )

  # Cache calculations for identical missingness patterns
  keys <- apply(d, 1, function(z)
  paste0(as.integer(z), collapse = ""))
  unique_keys <- unique(keys)
  pattern_stats <- lapply(unique_keys, function(k) {
    obs <- which(strsplit(k, "", fixed = TRUE)[[1]] == "1")
    Xi <- X[obs, , drop = FALSE]
    if (!nrow(Xi)) return(c(0, 0, rep(0, nrow(C))))
    s <- svd(Xi, nu = 0, nv = ncol(Xi))
    tol <- max(dim(Xi)) * max(s$d) * .Machine$double.eps
    r <- sum(s$d > tol)
    est <- if (r == ncol(Xi)) rep(TRUE, nrow(C)) else {
      N <- s$v[, seq.int(r + 1L, ncol(Xi)), drop = FALSE]
      apply(abs(C %*% N), 1, max) < 1e-8
    }
    c(r, as.integer(r == ncol(X)), as.integer(est))
  })
  stats <- do.call(rbind, pattern_stats)[match(keys, unique_keys), , drop = FALSE]

  protein_rank_results_68[[sw]] <- data.frame(
    Software = sw, Total_Proteins = n,
    Unique_Missingness_Patterns = length(unique_keys),
    Full_Rank_Proteins = sum(stats[, 2]),
    Full_Rank_Percent = 100 * mean(stats[, 2]),
    Median_Protein_Rank = median(stats[, 1])
  )

  protein_contrast_results_68[[sw]] <- data.frame(
    Software = sw, Contrast = rownames(C),
    Estimable_Proteins = colSums(stats[, -(1:2), drop = FALSE]),
    Total_Proteins = n
  )

  contrast_availability_68[[sw]] <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    lapply(seq_len(nrow(planned_contrasts_68)), function(i) {
      a <- planned_contrasts_68$Numerator[i]
      b <- planned_contrasts_68$Denominator[i]
      na <- rowSums(d[, meta$condition == a, drop = FALSE])
      nb <- rowSums(d[, meta$condition == b, drop = FALSE])
      both <- na >= 2 & nb >= 2
      shared <- rep(FALSE, n)
      for (batch in levels(meta$Batch)) {
        ia <- meta$condition == a & meta$Batch == batch
        ib <- meta$condition == b & meta$Batch == batch
        if (any(ia) && any(ib))
          shared <- shared | (
            rowSums(d[, ia, drop = FALSE]) > 0 &
            rowSums(d[, ib, drop = FALSE]) > 0
          )
      }
      data.frame(
        Software = sw, Contrast = planned_contrasts_68$Contrast[i],
        Total_Proteins = n,
        Both_Groups_At_Least_2 = sum(both),
        Both_Groups_Percent = 100 * mean(both),
        Shared_Batch_Support = sum(shared),
        Both_And_Shared_Batch = sum(both & shared),
        Both_And_Shared_Percent = 100 * mean(both & shared)
      )
    })
  )
  rm(x, d, stats, pattern_stats)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

protein_availability_summary_68 <- dplyr::bind_rows(protein_availability_68)
contrast_availability_summary_68 <- dplyr::bind_rows(contrast_availability_68)
protein_rank_summary_68 <- dplyr::bind_rows(protein_rank_results_68)
protein_contrast_estimability_68 <- dplyr::bind_rows(protein_contrast_results_68) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Estimable_Percent = 100 * Estimable_Proteins / Total_Proteins)

print(protein_availability_summary_68, row.names = FALSE)
print(contrast_availability_summary_68, row.names = FALSE)
print(protein_rank_summary_68, row.names = FALSE)
print(protein_contrast_estimability_68, row.names = FALSE)
```


Following exclusion of Group 4, protein-level completeness across the 68 retained runs was 78.6% for AlphaDIA, 77.0% for DIA-NN, 95.3% for Spectronaut, and 88.6% for MaxDIA. Median protein detection was 68 runs across all four pipelines. Protein-specific design matrices were full rank for 97.3%, 95.8%, 99.9%, and 99.9% of proteins, respectively, with a median rank of 11. Across the 11 planned contrasts, mathematical estimability ranged from 98.3–99.9% for AlphaDIA, 97.1–99.8% for DIA-NN, 99.9–100% for Spectronaut, and 99.9–100% for MaxDIA. Nine contrasts had direct within-batch support, whereas the two 6-hour versus 24-hour comparisons lacked overlapping acquisition batches and therefore require cautious interpretation. Overall, these findings support proceeding with batch-adjusted protein-level differential abundance modeling without additional global completeness filtering.

## Statistical inference

This chunk will:
- Add the acquisition batch annotation to the colData of all four QFeatures objects.
- Standardize condition and Batch factor levels.
- Check that the 83 runs align correctly.
- Verify that each software produces the same full-rank design matrix.
- Leave all abundance values and existing assays unchanged.


```{r prepare_batch_metadata_fixed, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
model <- ~ Batch + condition

qf_list <- list(
  AlphaDIA = qf_alpha,
  `DIA-NN` = qf_diann,
  Spectronaut = qf_spectro,
  MaxDIA = qf_maxdia
)

model_design_summary <- list()

for (software in names(qf_list)) {

  qf_one <- qf_list[[software]]
  se <- qf_one[["proteins"]]

  # Match the protein assay samples to the validated design
  idx <- match(colnames(se), design_data$Run)

  stopifnot(
    ncol(se) == 83L,
    !anyNA(idx),
    identical(
      as.character(colData(se)$condition),
      as.character(design_data$condition[idx])
    )
  )

  # Update the parent QFeatures metadata first
  parent_cd <- SummarizedExperiment::colData(qf_one)
  parent_idx <- match(
    rownames(parent_cd),
    design_data$Run
  )

  stopifnot(!anyNA(parent_idx))

  parent_cd$Batch <- factor(
    as.character(design_data$Batch[parent_idx]),
    levels = levels(design_data$Batch)
  )

  SummarizedExperiment::colData(qf_one) <- parent_cd

  # Add the identical batch values to the protein assay
  se <- qf_one[["proteins"]]

  assay_idx <- match(
    colnames(se),
    rownames(parent_cd)
  )

  stopifnot(!anyNA(assay_idx))

  assay_cd <- SummarizedExperiment::colData(se)

  assay_cd$Batch <- parent_cd$Batch[assay_idx]

  SummarizedExperiment::colData(se) <- assay_cd

  qf_one[["proteins"]] <- se

  # Validate the actual metadata used for modeling
  protein_metadata <- as.data.frame(
    SummarizedExperiment::colData(
      qf_one[["proteins"]]
    )
  )

  X <- stats::model.matrix(
    model,
    data = protein_metadata
  )

  model_design_summary[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Runs = nrow(X),
    Parameters = ncol(X),
    Rank = qr(X)$rank,
    Full_Rank = qr(X)$rank == ncol(X),
    Missing_Metadata = sum(
      !stats::complete.cases(
        protein_metadata[, c("Batch", "condition")]
      )
    )
  )

  qf_list[[software]] <- qf_one
}

# Return prepared objects
qf_alpha <- qf_list[["AlphaDIA"]]
qf_diann <- qf_list[["DIA-NN"]]
qf_spectro <- qf_list[["Spectronaut"]]
qf_maxdia <- qf_list[["MaxDIA"]]

model_design_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  model_design_summary
)

print(model_design_summary, row.names = FALSE)
```

## 68 Statistical inference
```{r prepare_batch_metadata_fixed_68, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Prepare batch metadata for 68-run statistical inference
model_68 <- ~ Batch + condition
model_design_summary_68 <- list()

stopifnot(
  identical(names(qf_models_68), software_order),
  nrow(design_data_68) == 68L
)

for (software in names(qf_models_68)) {

  qf <- qf_models_68[[software]]
  se <- qf[["proteins"]]

  # Match protein samples to validated 68-run design
  idx <- match(colnames(se), design_data_68$Run)

  stopifnot(
    ncol(se) == 68L,
    !anyNA(idx)
  )

  # Update QFeatures parent metadata
  cd <- SummarizedExperiment::colData(qf)
  parent_idx <- match(rownames(cd), design_data_68$Run)

  stopifnot(
    nrow(cd) == 68L,
    !anyNA(parent_idx)
  )

  cd$condition <- design_data_68$condition[parent_idx]
  cd$Batch <- design_data_68$Batch[parent_idx]
  SummarizedExperiment::colData(qf) <- cd

  # Update protein assay metadata
  se <- qf[["proteins"]]
  assay_idx <- match(colnames(se), design_data_68$Run)

  assay_cd <- SummarizedExperiment::colData(se)
  assay_cd$condition <- design_data_68$condition[assay_idx]
  assay_cd$Batch <- design_data_68$Batch[assay_idx]
  SummarizedExperiment::colData(se) <- assay_cd

  qf[["proteins"]] <- se

  # Validate modeling design
  X <- stats::model.matrix(
    model_68,
    data = as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::colData(se))
  )

  model_design_summary_68[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Runs = nrow(X),
    Parameters = ncol(X),
    Rank = qr(X)$rank,
    Full_Rank = qr(X)$rank == ncol(X),
    Missing_Metadata = sum(
      !stats::complete.cases(
        as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::colData(se))[
          , c("Batch", "condition")
        ]
      )
    )
  )

  stopifnot(
  nrow(X) == 68L,
  ncol(X) == 11L,
  qr(X)$rank == 11L,
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    X,
    design_matrix_68[
      match(colnames(se), design_data_68$Run),
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ],
    check.attributes = FALSE
  ))
)

  qf_models_68[[software]] <- qf
  rm(qf, se, cd, assay_cd, X)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}
```

```{r qc_msqrob_model_quality, eval=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Model-quality diagnostics across all four DIA pipelines
# ============================================================

qf_models <- list(
  AlphaDIA = qf_alpha,
  `DIA-NN` = qf_diann,
  Spectronaut = qf_spectro,
  MaxDIA = qf_maxdia
)

model_quality_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(names(qf_models), function(software) {

    models <- SummarizedExperiment::rowData(
      qf_models[[software]][["proteins"]]
    )[["msqrobModels"]]

    # Extract diagnostics safely from each fitted model
    diagnostics <- lapply(models, function(m) {

      if (is.null(m) || !methods::is(m, "StatModel")) {
        return(c(
          Valid_Coefficients = FALSE,
          Valid_Sigma = FALSE,
          Positive_Residual_DF = FALSE,
          Valid_Posterior_Variance = FALSE,
          Positive_Posterior_DF = FALSE,
          Residual_DF = NA_real_,
          Sigma = NA_real_
        ))
      }

      coefficients <- m@params$coefficients
      sigma <- m@params$sigma
      df_residual <- m@params$df.residual

      c(
        Valid_Coefficients =
          length(coefficients) == 12 &&
          all(is.finite(coefficients)),

        Valid_Sigma =
          length(sigma) == 1 &&
          is.finite(sigma) &&
          sigma > 0,

        Positive_Residual_DF =
          length(df_residual) == 1 &&
          is.finite(df_residual) &&
          df_residual > 0,

        Valid_Posterior_Variance =
          length(m@varPosterior) == 1 &&
          is.finite(m@varPosterior) &&
          m@varPosterior > 0,

        Positive_Posterior_DF =
          length(m@dfPosterior) == 1 &&
          is.finite(m@dfPosterior) &&
          m@dfPosterior > 0,

        Residual_DF =
          if (length(df_residual) == 1)
            df_residual else NA_real_,

        Sigma =
          if (length(sigma) == 1)
            sigma else NA_real_
      )
    })

    diagnostics <- as.data.frame(
      do.call(rbind, diagnostics)
    )

    data.frame(
      Software = software,
      Total_Models = length(models),
      Valid_Coefficients = sum(
        diagnostics$Valid_Coefficients == 1,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      Valid_Sigma = sum(
        diagnostics$Valid_Sigma == 1,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      Positive_Residual_DF = sum(
        diagnostics$Positive_Residual_DF == 1,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      Valid_Posterior_Variance = sum(
        diagnostics$Valid_Posterior_Variance == 1,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      Positive_Posterior_DF = sum(
        diagnostics$Positive_Posterior_DF == 1,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      Median_Residual_DF = median(
        diagnostics$Residual_DF,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      Median_Sigma = median(
        diagnostics$Sigma,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    )
  })
)

print(model_quality_summary, row.names = FALSE)
```
These results are encouraging. All four DIA pipelines have successfully produced robust models for the overwhelming majority of proteins, but a small subset requires caution before differential abundance testing. The median residual degrees of freedom are approximately 66 across all four pipelines, suggesting that most models retain substantial information after accounting for batch and condition.

### 68 Fit the first protein-level model
```{r fit_msqrob_quality_68, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=run_analysis}

model_fit_summary_68 <- list()
model_quality_summary_68 <- list()

for (sw in names(qf_models_68)) {

  cat("Fitting:", sw, "\n")

  qf_models_68[[sw]] <- msqrob2::msqrob(
    qf_models_68[[sw]],
    i = "proteins",
    formula = model_68,
    robust = TRUE,
    overwrite = TRUE
  )

  se <- qf_models_68[[sw]][["proteins"]]
  models <- SummarizedExperiment::rowData(se)[["msqrobModels"]]

  model_fit_summary_68[[sw]] <- data.frame(
    Software = sw,
    Total_Proteins = nrow(se),
    Model_Entries = length(models),
    Missing_Entries = sum(vapply(models, is.null, logical(1)))
  )

  diagnostics <- lapply(models, function(m) {

    if (is.null(m) || !methods::is(m, "StatModel"))
      return(rep(NA_real_, 7))

    p <- m@params

    c(
      Coef = as.numeric(length(p$coefficients) == 11L &&
        all(is.finite(p$coefficients))),
      Sigma = as.numeric(length(p$sigma) == 1L &&
        is.finite(p$sigma) && p$sigma > 0),
      DF = as.numeric(length(p$df.residual) == 1L &&
        is.finite(p$df.residual) && p$df.residual > 0),
      PostVar = as.numeric(length(m@varPosterior) == 1L &&
        is.finite(m@varPosterior) && m@varPosterior > 0),
      PostDF = as.numeric(length(m@dfPosterior) == 1L &&
        is.finite(m@dfPosterior) && m@dfPosterior > 0),
      ResidualDF = if (length(p$df.residual) == 1L)
        p$df.residual else NA_real_,
      SigmaValue = if (length(p$sigma) == 1L)
        p$sigma else NA_real_
    )
  })

  d <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, diagnostics))
  names(d) <- c(
    "Coef", "Sigma", "DF", "PostVar",
    "PostDF", "ResidualDF", "SigmaValue"
  )

  model_quality_summary_68[[sw]] <- data.frame(
    Software = sw,
    Total_Models = length(models),
    Valid_Coefficients = sum(d$Coef == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    Valid_Sigma = sum(d$Sigma == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    Positive_Residual_DF = sum(d$DF == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    Valid_Posterior_Variance = sum(d$PostVar == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    Positive_Posterior_DF = sum(d$PostDF == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median_Residual_DF = median(d$ResidualDF, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median_Sigma = median(d$SigmaValue, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

  rm(se, models, diagnostics, d)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

model_fit_summary_68 <- dplyr::bind_rows(model_fit_summary_68)
model_quality_summary_68 <- dplyr::bind_rows(model_quality_summary_68)

cat("\n=== Model fitting summary (68 runs) ===\n")
print(model_fit_summary_68, row.names = FALSE)

cat("\n=== Model quality summary (68 runs) ===\n")
print(model_quality_summary_68, row.names = FALSE)
```
Following exclusion of Group 4, robust batch-adjusted protein-level models were fitted across 68 runs using all four DIA analysis pipelines. Model entries were generated for all 11,331 AlphaDIA, 9,833 DIA-NN, 7,970 Spectronaut, and 8,482 MaxDIA protein features. Valid coefficient estimates were obtained for 97.3%, 95.8%, 99.9%, and 99.9% of proteins, respectively. Median residual degrees of freedom ranged from 52.78 to 52.89 across pipelines. These results indicate that the revised experimental design supports robust protein-level modeling for the large majority of quantified proteins, while a small subset remains unsuitable for complete coefficient-based inference.


### Construct the contrast matrix
```{r construct_planned_contrasts}
# ============================================================
# Construct 11 planned contrasts for batch-adjusted models
# ============================================================

# Model coefficient names
parameter_names <- colnames(
  stats::model.matrix(
    model,
    data = as.data.frame(
      SummarizedExperiment::colData(qf_alpha[["proteins"]])
    )
  )
)

# Reference condition has no explicit coefficient
reference_condition <- "CTRL_cDDP_24h"

# Build a coefficient vector for each condition
condition_vector <- function(condition, parameter_names) {

  v <- stats::setNames(
    numeric(length(parameter_names)),
    parameter_names
  )

  if (condition != reference_condition) {
    coefficient <- paste0("condition", condition)

    stopifnot(coefficient %in% parameter_names)

    v[coefficient] <- 1
  }

  v
}

# Each contrast is numerator minus denominator
L <- vapply(
  seq_len(nrow(planned_contrasts)),
  function(i) {
    condition_vector(
      planned_contrasts$Numerator[i],
      parameter_names
    ) -
      condition_vector(
        planned_contrasts$Denominator[i],
        parameter_names
      )
  },
  FUN.VALUE = stats::setNames(
    numeric(length(parameter_names)),
    parameter_names
  )
)

rownames(L) <- parameter_names
colnames(L) <- planned_contrasts$Contrast

# Validate contrast matrix
stopifnot(
  nrow(L) == 12L,
  ncol(L) == 11L,
  all(is.finite(L)),
  all(colSums(abs(L)) > 0)
)

cat("Contrast matrix dimensions:", dim(L), "\n")
print(L)
```

```{r hypothesis_test_alphadia, eval= FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
)

# Avoid repeating hypothesis tests if results already exist

  SummarizedExperiment::rowData(qf_alpha[["proteins"]])
)

if (!all(colnames(L) %in% existing_results)) {

  qf_alpha <- msqrob2::hypothesisTest(
    qf_alpha,
    i = "proteins",

  )

}

# Confirm all 11 contrasts are present

)

stopifnot(all(colnames(L) %in% result_columns))

cat("AlphaDIA: 11 planned contrasts available.\n")
```

```{r summarize_alphadia_da, eval=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
  dplyr::summarise(

```
Three patterns stand out:
1. c-Jun KO is associated with substantial proteomic differences, particularly under cisplatin treatment. At 6h, 3,747 proteins differ between KO and CTRL, compared with 1,850 at baseline.
2. The early cisplatin response differs strongly between genotypes. Relative to their respective baselines, KO has 3,859 significant proteins at 6h versus 434 in CTRL. This suggests a much larger detectable early response in KO, although significance counts alone do not establish the magnitude of biological change.
3. The JNK inhibitor effect is much more extensive at 24h than 6h (3,670 versus 236 significant proteins). This is an interesting time-dependent pattern worth investigating through effect sizes and pathway enrichment.
