```{r hypothesis_testing_68, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=run_analysis}

# Construct 11 contrasts: numerator minus denominator
parameter_names_68 <- colnames(design_matrix_68)

L_68 <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(planned_contrasts_68)), function(i) {
  reference_matrix_68[planned_contrasts_68$Numerator[i], ] -
    reference_matrix_68[planned_contrasts_68$Denominator[i], ]
}, numeric(length(parameter_names_68)))

rownames(L_68) <- parameter_names_68

stopifnot(
  identical(rownames(L_68), parameter_names_68),
  nrow(L_68) == 11L,
  ncol(L_68) == 11L,
  all(is.finite(L_68)),
  all(colSums(abs(L_68)) > 0)
)

# Test and summarize each pipeline
contrast_test_summary_68 <- list()
da_results_68 <- list()
da_summary_68 <- list()

for (sw in names(qf_models_68)) {

  cat("Testing:", sw, "\n")

  # Recompute contrasts from the newly fitted 68-run models
  qf_models_68[[sw]] <- msqrob2::hypothesisTest(
    qf_models_68[[sw]],
    i = "proteins",
    contrast = L_68,
    overwrite = TRUE
  )

  se <- qf_models_68[[sw]][["proteins"]]

  contrast_test_summary_68[[sw]] <- data.frame(
    Software = sw,
    Contrasts_Present = sum(
      colnames(L_68) %in%
        colnames(SummarizedExperiment::rowData(se))
    )
  )

  results <- msqrob2::msqrobCollect(se, L_68)
  da_results_68[[sw]] <- results

  da_summary_68[[sw]] <- results |>
    dplyr::as_tibble() |>
    dplyr::group_by(contrast) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      Software = sw,
      Total_Proteins = dplyr::n(),
      Valid_Tests = sum(is.finite(pval) & is.finite(adjPval)),
      Significant_FDR05 = sum(is.finite(adjPval) & adjPval < 0.05),
      Upregulated = sum(
        is.finite(adjPval) & adjPval < 0.05 &
          is.finite(logFC) & logFC > 0
      ),
      Downregulated = sum(
        is.finite(adjPval) & adjPval < 0.05 &
          is.finite(logFC) & logFC < 0
      ),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  rm(se, results)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
}

```
Following exclusion of Group 4, batch-adjusted differential abundance testing was performed for 11 planned contrasts across four DIA analysis pipelines. All 44 pipeline–contrast combinations were successfully evaluated, with high proportions of proteins yielding valid statistical tests. Significant protein counts varied substantially among pipelines, with AlphaDIA and DIA-NN generally identifying more differentially abundant proteins than Spectronaut and MaxDIA. Across all four pipelines, the cisplatin-associated response at 6h yielded more significant proteins in JUN-knockout than control samples, while JNK inhibitor-associated differences were more extensive at 24h than at 6h. These patterns suggest reproducible qualitative trends across analytical workflows despite substantial differences in statistical detection. Direct comparisons of effect sizes and shared protein-level results are required to establish the concordance and biological significance of these findings.

The UpSet plot shows substantial agreement in protein identification across the four DIA analysis pipelines, with 7,483 protein groups shared by all four tools, representing a large common proteomic core. However, pipeline-specific differences are also evident, particularly for AlphaDIA, which identifies the largest number of protein groups and contributes 2,413 uniquely identified groups. DIA-NN, MaxDIA, and Spectronaut show smaller tool-specific contributions. These findings suggest that while the pipelines consistently identify a substantial shared proteome, their identification coverage differs considerably. Importantly, the overlaps are based on exact protein-group identifiers, so differences in protein grouping between software packages may contribute to the observed discrepancies.

```{r harmonize_precursor_identifiers, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Harmonize precursor identifiers across DIA pipelines
# Stripped peptide sequence + precursor charge
# ============================================================

qf_precursors <- list(
  AlphaDIA = qf_alpha,
  `DIA-NN` = qf_diann,
  Spectronaut = qf_spectro,
  MaxDIA = qf_maxdia
)

precursor_sets <- lapply(names(qf_precursors), function(software) {

  rd <- as.data.frame(
    SummarizedExperiment::rowData(
      qf_precursors[[software]][["precursors"]]
    )
  )

  sequence <- as.character(rd$Stripped.Sequence)

  if (software == "Spectronaut") {

    # Spectronaut precursor IDs end with .charge
    precursor_id <- as.character(rd$Precursor.Id)

    charge <- ifelse(
      grepl("\\.[0-9]+$", precursor_id),
      sub("^.*\\.([0-9]+)$", "\\1", precursor_id),
      NA_character_
    )

  } else {

    charge <- as.character(rd$Precursor.Charge)

  }

  # Exclude entries lacking a valid sequence or charge
  valid <- !is.na(sequence) &
    nzchar(sequence) &
    !is.na(charge) &
    grepl("^[0-9]+$", charge) &
    as.integer(charge) > 0

  # Collapse modified forms sharing the same sequence and charge
  unique(
    paste(sequence[valid], charge[valid], sep = "|")
  )
})

names(precursor_sets) <- names(qf_precursors)

# Compare original entries with harmonized identifiers
precursor_harmonization_summary <- data.frame(
  Software = names(qf_precursors),
  Original_Entries = vapply(
    qf_precursors,
    function(qf) nrow(qf[["precursors"]]),
    integer(1)
  ),
  Unique_Sequence_Charge = lengths(precursor_sets),
  row.names = NULL
)

precursor_harmonization_summary$Collapsed_or_Excluded <-
  precursor_harmonization_summary$Original_Entries -
  precursor_harmonization_summary$Unique_Sequence_Charge

print(precursor_harmonization_summary, row.names = FALSE)
```

Precursor-level identification overlap revealed a substantial shared proteomic core across the four DIA analysis pipelines, with 113,518 peptide sequence–charge combinations identified by all four tools. Nevertheless, considerable pipeline-specific variation was observed, particularly for MaxDIA, which identified the largest number of unique combinations (62,518). Spectronaut exhibited the highest proportion of identifications belonging to the four-way intersection (71.5%), despite having the smallest overall sequence–charge identification set. Compared with the protein-level analysis, these findings indicate greater heterogeneity in precursor identification than in protein-group coverage. This suggests that differences in precursor-level detection and reporting may not translate directly into equivalent differences in protein identification.

```{r precursor_coverage_per_protein, fig.width=11, fig.height=6, dpi=300, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# ============================================================
# Sequence-charge coverage per protein group across DIA tools
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

qf_coverage <- list(
  AlphaDIA = qf_alpha,
  `DIA-NN` = qf_diann,
  Spectronaut = qf_spectro,
  MaxDIA = qf_maxdia
)

# Calculate the number of distinct sequence-charge combinations
# assigned to each protein-group annotation.
get_protein_coverage <- function(qf, software) {

  rd <- as.data.frame(
    SummarizedExperiment::rowData(qf[["precursors"]])
  )

  sequence <- as.character(rd$Stripped.Sequence)

  if (software == "Spectronaut") {
    precursor_id <- as.character(rd$Precursor.Id)

    charge <- ifelse(
      grepl("\\.[0-9]+$", precursor_id),
      sub("^.*\\.([0-9]+)$", "\\1", precursor_id),
      NA_character_
    )
  } else {
    charge <- as.character(rd$Precursor.Charge)
  }

  protein_group <- trimws(as.character(rd$Protein.Group))

  valid <- !is.na(sequence) & nzchar(sequence) &
    !is.na(charge) & grepl("^[0-9]+$", charge) &
    as.integer(charge) > 0 &
    !is.na(protein_group) & nzchar(protein_group)

  precursor_mapping <- data.frame(
    Protein.Group = protein_group[valid],
    Sequence_Charge = paste(
      sequence[valid], charge[valid], sep = "|"
    )
  )

  # Remove duplicate sequence-charge / protein-group mappings
  precursor_mapping <- unique(precursor_mapping)

  coverage <- precursor_mapping %>%
    dplyr::count(Protein.Group, name = "Precursor_Count")

  coverage$Software <- software

  coverage
}

protein_coverage <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(names(qf_coverage), function(software) {
    get_protein_coverage(qf_coverage[[software]], software)
  })
)

protein_coverage$Software <- factor(
  protein_coverage$Software,
  levels = names(qf_coverage)
)

# Summary statistics
protein_coverage_summary <- protein_coverage %>%
  group_by(Software) %>%
  summarise(
    Protein_Groups_With_Precursors = n(),
    Mean_Precursors = mean(Precursor_Count),
    Median_Precursors = median(Precursor_Count),
    Q1 = quantile(Precursor_Count, 0.25),
    Q3 = quantile(Precursor_Count, 0.75),
    Max_Precursors = max(Precursor_Count),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(protein_coverage_summary, n = Inf)

# Visualize coverage distribution
p_precursor_coverage <- ggplot(
  protein_coverage,
  aes(x = Software, y = Precursor_Count, fill = Software)
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    outlier.shape = NA,
    width = 0.6,
    alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = software_colors) +
  scale_y_log10(
    breaks = c(1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500),
    labels = scales::comma
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Precursor coverage per protein group",
    #subtitle = "Distinct sequence–charge combinations assigned to each protein-group annotation",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Precursors per protein",
    # caption = paste(
    #   "Counts derived from precursor-level protein-group annotations;",
    #   "modified forms sharing sequence and charge are collapsed."
    # )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(p_precursor_coverage)

```

To investigate the discrepancy between MaxDIA's high precursor-level coverage and its comparatively lower protein-group identification count, the number of distinct peptide sequence–charge combinations assigned to each protein group was examined. MaxDIA exhibited the highest mean (27.1) and median (20) sequence–charge combinations per protein group, compared with Spectronaut (19.9 and 13), DIA-NN (19.2 and 12), and AlphaDIA (16.0 and 10), respectively. Furthermore, 99.1% of MaxDIA-specific sequence–charge combinations were associated with protein accessions also identified by at least one other pipeline. Together, these findings indicate that MaxDIA's increased precursor-level identification coverage predominantly reflects greater sequence–charge representation of already identified proteins rather than a proportional expansion of protein-group coverage. Nevertheless, differences in precursor reporting, protein inference, and filtering may also contribute to the observed variation.

Protein-group identification showed substantial overlap among the four DIA analysis pipelines, with 7,483 protein groups shared by all workflows. AlphaDIA identified the largest protein-group set (11,331), including 2,413 groups unique to that pipeline. At the precursor level, 113,518 stripped peptide sequence–charge combinations were shared across all four pipelines, although pipeline-specific variation was more pronounced. MaxDIA reported the largest precursor set (230,167 combinations), including 62,518 pipeline-specific combinations, despite identifying fewer protein groups than AlphaDIA and DIA-NN. Consistent with this pattern, MaxDIA exhibited the highest mean and median precursor coverage per protein group (27.1 and 20, respectively), compared with 16.0 and 10 for AlphaDIA, 19.2 and 12 for DIA-NN, and 19.9 and 13 for Spectronaut. These findings demonstrate substantial agreement in protein-group identification alongside greater heterogeneity in precursor-level representation, potentially reflecting differences in precursor reporting, filtering, and protein inference among pipelines.

### Differential abundance comparison
```{r da_summary_all_pipelines, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Differential abundance summary: 4 pipelines x 11 contrasts
# Uses existing msqrob2 fits; no model refitting
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Synchronize with the latest fitted QFeatures objects
qf_models <- list(
  AlphaDIA = qf_alpha,
  `DIA-NN` = qf_diann,
  Spectronaut = qf_spectro,
  MaxDIA = qf_maxdia
)

# Collect existing protein-level differential abundance results
inference_list <- lapply(qf_models, function(qf) {
  msqrob2::msqrobCollect(qf[["proteins"]], L)
})

# Summarize significant proteins for every pipeline and contrast
da_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(names(inference_list), function(software) {

    inference_list[[software]] %>%
      group_by(contrast) %>%
      summarise(
        Total_Proteins = n(),
        Valid_Tests = sum(is.finite(pval)),
        Significant_FDR05 = sum(
          is.finite(adjPval) & adjPval < 0.05
        ),
        Upregulated = sum(
          is.finite(adjPval) & adjPval < 0.05 &
            is.finite(logFC) & logFC > 0
        ),
        Downregulated = sum(
          is.finite(adjPval) & adjPval < 0.05 &
            is.finite(logFC) & logFC < 0
        ),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      mutate(Software = software)
  })
)

# Preserve experimental contrast order
da_summary$contrast <- factor(
  da_summary$contrast,
  levels = planned_contrasts$Contrast
)

da_summary$Software <- factor(
  da_summary$Software,
  levels = names(qf_models)
)

# Confirm 4 pipelines x 11 contrasts
stopifnot(
  nrow(da_summary) == 44,
  !anyNA(da_summary$contrast),
  all(table(da_summary$Software) == 11)
)

# Display complete summary
print(
  da_summary %>%
    select(
      Software, contrast, Total_Proteins, Valid_Tests,
      Significant_FDR05, Upregulated, Downregulated
    ),
  n = Inf
)
```

Differential abundance analysis revealed substantial variation in the number of significant protein groups across the four DIA pipelines and 11 experimental contrasts. AlphaDIA and DIA-NN generally reported the largest numbers of differentially abundant proteins, whereas MaxDIA consistently reported the fewest despite exhibiting the greatest sequence–charge identification coverage. For example, in the KO versus CTRL comparison following 6 hours of cisplatin treatment, DIA-NN identified 4,021 significant proteins, compared with 3,747 for AlphaDIA, 2,709 for Spectronaut, and 647 for MaxDIA. A particularly consistent pattern was observed for the JNK inhibitor contrasts, with all four pipelines identifying substantially more significant proteins at 24 hours than at 6 hours. These findings demonstrate that increased precursor-level coverage does not necessarily correspond to increased differential abundance detection. Differences in quantitative variability, protein inference, missingness, and statistical power may contribute to the observed discrepancies.

Differential abundance overlap analysis for the KO versus CTRL comparison following 6 hours of cisplatin treatment revealed substantial agreement among the DIA pipelines, alongside differences in the number of significant protein groups. A total of 557 protein groups were classified as differentially abundant by all four pipelines, while 1,210 additional groups were shared by AlphaDIA, DIA-NN, and Spectronaut but not MaxDIA. Notably, 86.1% of MaxDIA's 647 significant protein groups were also significant in all three other pipelines, indicating that its smaller differential abundance set largely represented a shared subset of findings. In contrast, AlphaDIA and DIA-NN contributed considerably larger numbers of pipeline-specific significant protein groups. These results demonstrate substantial cross-pipeline agreement for a common set of differential abundance findings, while highlighting differences in the breadth of statistically significant protein detection.

```{r da_upset_all_contrasts, fig.width=13, fig.height=6.5, dpi=300, out.width="100%", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide', eval=FALSE}

library(ComplexUpset)
library(ggplot2)

# ============================================================
# DA UpSet plots for all 11 experimental contrasts
# ============================================================

# Preserve software and contrast order
software_order <- names(inference_list)
contrast_order <- as.character(planned_contrasts$Contrast)

# Function to extract significant protein-group sets
get_da_sets <- function(contrast_name) {

  sets <- lapply(inference_list, function(results) {

    valid <- !is.na(results$contrast) &
      as.character(results$contrast) == contrast_name &
      is.finite(results$adjPval) &
      results$adjPval < 0.05 &
      !is.na(results$feature)

    unique(as.character(results$feature[valid]))
  })

  sets[software_order]
}

# Function to create one DA UpSet plot
make_da_upset <- function(contrast_name) {

  sets <- get_da_sets(contrast_name)
  # Sets with at least one significant protein
  active_software <- software_order[lengths(sets[software_order]) > 0]

  all_ids <- unique(unlist(sets, use.names = FALSE))

  if (length(all_ids) == 0L) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  presence <- data.frame(
    Protein = all_ids,
    check.names = FALSE
  )

  for (software in software_order) {
    presence[[software]] <- all_ids %in% sets[[software]]
  }

  ComplexUpset::upset(
    presence,
    intersect = active_software,
    name = "DIA pipeline",
    sort_intersections_by = "cardinality",
    min_size = 1,
    width_ratio = 0.30,

    set_sizes = ComplexUpset::upset_set_size(
      geom = ggplot2::geom_bar(
        fill = unname(software_colors[active_software]),
        width = 0.65
      )
    ),

    base_annotations = list(
      "Significant protein-group intersections" =
        ComplexUpset::intersection_size(
          text = list(size = 3.2, vjust = -0.3)
        ) +
        ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
          labels = scales::comma,
          expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))
        )
    ),

    stripes = ComplexUpset::upset_stripes(
      colors = c("white", "#F5F7FA")
    )
  ) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = "Differential abundance overlap across DIA pipelines",
      subtitle = contrast_name,
      caption = paste(
        "BH-adjusted p-value < 0.05;",
        "exact protein-group identifier matching."
      )
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(
        face = "bold", size = 16
      ),
      plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(
        size = 12, color = "#667085"
      ),
      axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(
        face = "bold", size = 11
      ),
      axis.text = ggplot2::element_text(
        size = 9, color = "#344054"
      ),
      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      plot.background = ggplot2::element_rect(
        fill = "white", color = NA
      )
    )
}

# Generate and display each plot in the R Markdown output
for (contrast_name in contrast_order) {

  p <- make_da_upset(contrast_name)

  if (!is.null(p)) {
    print(p)
  }
}
```

```{r save_da_upset_plots, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
  if (!is.null(p)) {
    ggplot2::ggsave(
      filename = sprintf("figures/DA_UpSet/DA_UpSet_%02d.png", i),
      plot = p,
      width = 13,
      height = 6.5,
      dpi = 300,
      bg = "white"
    )
  }
}

```

Differential abundance overlap analysis across 11 experimental contrasts revealed a substantial shared set of significant protein groups among AlphaDIA, DIA-NN, Spectronaut, and MaxDIA, alongside pronounced pipeline-dependent differences. AlphaDIA and DIA-NN generally reported the largest numbers of differentially abundant protein groups, although their relative contributions varied across experimental comparisons. MaxDIA consistently reported fewer significant protein groups, but a large proportion of these overlapped with findings from the other pipelines. For example, 557 of 647 MaxDIA-significant protein groups (86.1%) were significant in all four pipelines for the KO versus CTRL comparison following 6 hours of cisplatin treatment. Similarly, four-way intersections accounted for 644 of 871 (73.9%) MaxDIA-significant groups in the 24-hour JNK inhibitor comparison and 397 of 501 (79.2%) in the KO cisplatin 24-hour versus 6-hour comparison. Despite this common core, substantial pipeline-specific intersections were observed, particularly for AlphaDIA and DIA-NN. Collectively, these findings indicate that differential abundance detection is influenced by the analysis pipeline, with considerable agreement among shared significant protein groups but differences in the breadth of detected responses. Because the comparisons were based on exact protein-group identifiers and statistical significance thresholds, further assessment of fold-change magnitude and direction is required to establish quantitative agreement.

```{r differential_abundance_comparison_68, fig.width=13, fig.height=7, dpi=300, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=run_analysis}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Extract significant protein sets for any contrast
# ------------------------------------------------------------

get_da_sets_68 <- function(contrast_name) {

  sets <- lapply(inference_list_68, function(results) {

    valid <- !is.na(results$contrast) &
      as.character(results$contrast) == contrast_name &
      is.finite(results$adjPval) &
      results$adjPval < 0.05 &
      !is.na(results$feature) &
      nzchar(as.character(results$feature))

    unique(as.character(results$feature[valid]))
  })

  sets[software_order_68]
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Reusable DA UpSet plotting function
# ------------------------------------------------------------

make_da_upset_68 <- function(contrast_name) {

  sets <- get_da_sets_68(contrast_name)
  all_ids <- unique(unlist(sets, use.names = FALSE))

  if (length(all_ids) == 0L)
    return(NULL)

  active_software <- software_order_68[lengths(sets) > 0]

  presence <- data.frame(
    Protein = all_ids,
    check.names = FALSE
  )

  for (sw in software_order_68)
    presence[[sw]] <- all_ids %in% sets[[sw]]

  stopifnot(
    identical(
      as.integer(colSums(presence[software_order_68])),
      as.integer(lengths(sets[software_order_68]))
    )
  )

  ComplexUpset::upset(
    presence,
    intersect = active_software,
    name = "DIA pipeline",
    sort_intersections_by = "cardinality",
    min_size = 1,
    width_ratio = 0.30,

    set_sizes = ComplexUpset::upset_set_size(
      geom = ggplot2::geom_bar(
        fill = unname(software_colors[active_software]),
        width = 0.65
      )
    ) +
      ggplot2::scale_y_reverse(
        labels = scales::label_number(
          scale = 1e-3, suffix = "K"
        )
      ),

    base_annotations = list(
      "Shared significant proteins" =
        ComplexUpset::intersection_size(
          mapping = ggplot2::aes(fill = "Intersection"),
          text = list(
            size = 3,
            angle = 90,
            hjust = -0.1,
            vjust = 0.5,
            color = "black"
          )
        ) +
        ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
          values = c(Intersection = "#D8D2C8"),
          guide = "none"
        ) +
        ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
          labels = scales::comma,
          expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25))
        )
    ),

    stripes = ComplexUpset::upset_stripes(
      colors = c("white", "#F5F7FA")
    )
  ) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = "Differential abundance overlap",
      subtitle = contrast_name,
      caption = paste(
        "BH-adjusted p-value < 0.05;",
        "exact protein-group identifier matching."
      )
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(
        face = "bold", size = 14
      ),
      plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(
        size = 11, color = "#667085"
      ),
      axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(
        face = "bold", size = 11
      ),
      axis.text = ggplot2::element_text(
        size = 9, color = "#344054"
      ),
      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      plot.background = ggplot2::element_rect(
        fill = "white", color = NA
      )
    )
}
```

Differential abundance analysis across the 68 retained runs revealed substantial pipeline-dependent variation in significant protein-group detection across the 11 experimental contrasts. AlphaDIA and DIA-NN generally identified the largest numbers of differentially abundant proteins, whereas MaxDIA consistently identified the fewest. Nevertheless, all four pipelines detected a more extensive cisplatin-associated response at 6h in JUN-knockout than control samples and a greater JNK inhibitor-associated response at 24h than at 6h. For the KO versus CTRL comparison following 6h of cisplatin treatment, AlphaDIA, DIA-NN, Spectronaut, and MaxDIA identified 2,349, 2,008, 1,095, and 62 significant protein groups, respectively. Of these, only 57 were shared across all four pipelines, while substantial pipeline-specific contributions were observed, particularly for AlphaDIA (1,182) and DIA-NN (720). These findings highlight consistent qualitative biological response patterns but considerable differences in statistical detection and cross-pipeline agreement.

### Pairwise log2 fold-change comparison

```{r da_logfc_agreement_6h, fig.width=12, fig.height=10, dpi=300, out.width="100%", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=FALSE}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# ============================================================
# Cross-pipeline log2 fold-change agreement
# Contrast: KO vs CTRL cisplatin 6h
# ============================================================

target_contrast <- "KO vs CTRL cisplatin 6h"

software_order <- c(
  "AlphaDIA", "DIA-NN", "Spectronaut", "MaxDIA"
)

# 1. Extract log2 fold changes without filtering on significance
logfc_long <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(software_order, function(software) {

    results <- inference_list[[software]]

    data.frame(
      Software = software,
      Protein = as.character(results$feature),
      logFC = as.numeric(results$logFC),
      Contrast = as.character(results$contrast)
    )
  })
) |>
  dplyr::filter(
    Contrast == target_contrast,
    !is.na(Protein),
    is.finite(logFC)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(Protein, Software, logFC)

# Ensure exact protein identifiers are unique within each pipeline
stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(logfc_long[c("Protein", "Software")])
)

# 2. Create a protein-by-pipeline fold-change table
logfc_wide <- logfc_long |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = Software,
    values_from = logFC
  )

# 3. Calculate pairwise correlations on shared proteins
pipeline_pairs <- combn(software_order, 2, simplify = FALSE)

logfc_pairwise_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(pipeline_pairs, function(pair) {

    paired <- logfc_wide[
      is.finite(logfc_wide[[pair[1]]]) &
      is.finite(logfc_wide[[pair[2]]]),
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    x <- paired[[pair[1]]]
    y <- paired[[pair[2]]]

    data.frame(
      Pipeline_1 = pair[1],
      Pipeline_2 = pair[2],
      Shared_Proteins = length(x),
      Pearson_r = if (length(x) >= 3) {
        cor(x, y, method = "pearson")
      } else {
        NA_real_
      },
      Spearman_rho = if (length(x) >= 3) {
        cor(x, y, method = "spearman")
      } else {
        NA_real_
      },
      Same_Direction_Percent = if (length(x) > 0) {
        100 * mean(sign(x) == sign(y))
      } else {
        NA_real_
      }
    )
  })
)

print(
  logfc_pairwise_summary |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      dplyr::across(
        c(Pearson_r, Spearman_rho, Same_Direction_Percent),
        ~ round(.x, 3)
      )
    ),
  row.names = FALSE
)

# 4. Prepare six pairwise scatterplots
plot_data <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(pipeline_pairs, function(pair) {

    paired <- logfc_wide[
      is.finite(logfc_wide[[pair[1]]]) &
      is.finite(logfc_wide[[pair[2]]]),
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    data.frame(
      Pair = paste(pair, collapse = " vs "),
      x = paired[[pair[1]]],
      y = paired[[pair[2]]]
    )
  })
)

# Shared axis limits across all six panels
axis_limit <- max(
  abs(c(plot_data$x, plot_data$y)),
  na.rm = TRUE
)

# 5. Visualize agreement
p_logfc_agreement_6h <- ggplot(
  plot_data,
  aes(x = x, y = y)
) +
  geom_point(
    color = "#0072B2",
    alpha = 0.16,
    size = 0.55
  ) +
  geom_abline(
    slope = 1,
    intercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "#D55E00",
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Pair,
    ncol = 2
  ) +
  coord_equal(
    xlim = c(-axis_limit, axis_limit),
    ylim = c(-axis_limit, axis_limit)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Cross-pipeline agreement in protein log2 fold changes",
    subtitle = target_contrast,
    x = "Pipeline 1 log2 fold change",
    y = "Pipeline 2 log2 fold change",
    caption = paste(
      "All shared protein groups with finite log2 fold changes;",
      "exact protein-group identifier matching.",
      "Dashed line: y = x."
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#667085"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(p_logfc_agreement_6h)
```
Pairwise comparison of protein-level log2 fold changes for the KO versus CTRL contrast following 6 hours of cisplatin treatment revealed positive quantitative agreement across all four DIA analysis pipelines, although the strength of agreement varied. AlphaDIA and DIA-NN exhibited the strongest concordance (Pearson r = 0.845; Spearman ρ = 0.815), with 83.0% of shared protein groups showing consistent fold-change directions. Comparisons involving Spectronaut demonstrated intermediate agreement (Pearson r = 0.755–0.787), whereas MaxDIA exhibited weaker correlations with the other pipelines (Pearson r = 0.613–0.653) and lower directional concordance (72.4–72.9%). These findings indicate that differences in differential abundance detection are accompanied by variation in estimated protein abundance changes, particularly for MaxDIA. Although MaxDIA showed the highest precursor sequence–charge coverage per protein group, this did not translate into greater differential abundance detection or stronger quantitative agreement. Further assessment of fold-change magnitude and statistical uncertainty is needed to clarify the factors contributing to these differences.

```{r da_abs_logfc_distribution_6h, fig.width=12, fig.height=6.5, dpi=300, out.width="100%", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=FALSE}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

software_order <- c("AlphaDIA", "DIA-NN", "Spectronaut", "MaxDIA")

# 1. Identify proteins with finite logFC in all four pipelines
common_proteins <- logfc_wide |>
  dplyr::filter(
    dplyr::if_all(
      dplyr::all_of(software_order),
      is.finite
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::pull(Protein)

# 2. Prepare both comparison populations
abs_logfc_data <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  logfc_long |>
    dplyr::mutate(Population = "All testable proteins"),

  logfc_long |>
    dplyr::filter(Protein %in% common_proteins) |>
    dplyr::mutate(Population = "Shared by all four pipelines")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Absolute_logFC = abs(logFC),
    Software = factor(Software, levels = software_order),
    Population = factor(
      Population,
      levels = c(
        "All testable proteins",
        "Shared by all four pipelines"
      )
    )
  )

# 3. Summarize effect-size distributions
abs_logfc_summary <- abs_logfc_data |>
  dplyr::group_by(Population, Software) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    N = dplyr::n(),
    Median_Abs_logFC = median(Absolute_logFC),
    Mean_Abs_logFC = mean(Absolute_logFC),
    Q1 = unname(quantile(Absolute_logFC, 0.25)),
    Q3 = unname(quantile(Absolute_logFC, 0.75)),
    P90 = unname(quantile(Absolute_logFC, 0.90)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(
  abs_logfc_summary |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      dplyr::across(
        c(Median_Abs_logFC, Mean_Abs_logFC, Q1, Q3, P90),
        ~ round(.x, 3)
      )
    ),
  n = Inf
)

# 4. Plot distributions with violin + boxplot
p_abs_logfc <- ggplot(
  abs_logfc_data,
  aes(x = Software, y = Absolute_logFC, fill = Software)
) +
  geom_violin(
    trim = TRUE,
    alpha = 0.55,
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.16,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    fill = "white",
    color = "#344054",
    linewidth = 0.45
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Population,
    nrow = 1
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(
      0,
      unname(quantile(abs_logfc_data$Absolute_logFC, 0.99))
    )
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = software_colors,
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Absolute protein log2 fold-change distributions",
    subtitle = "KO vs CTRL cisplatin 6h",
    x = NULL,
    y = "|log2 fold change|",
    # caption = paste(
    #   "Finite log2 fold changes only.",
    #   "Shared comparison uses exact protein-group identifiers.",
    #   "Display truncated at the pooled 99th percentile."
    # )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#667085"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(p_abs_logfc)
```

These results are important because they challenge our earlier hypothesis that MaxDIA detects fewer differentially abundant proteins primarily because it estimates smaller fold changes.

Comparison of absolute protein-level log2 fold-change distributions for the KO versus CTRL cisplatin 6h contrast showed that MaxDIA's lower number of significant protein groups was not accompanied by uniformly smaller estimated abundance changes. Among 7,474 protein groups with finite fold-change estimates in all four pipelines, the median absolute log2 fold change was 0.156 for AlphaDIA, 0.184 for DIA-NN, 0.215 for Spectronaut, and 0.181 for MaxDIA. Spectronaut exhibited the largest overall effect-size distribution, whereas MaxDIA showed magnitudes broadly comparable to DIA-NN and greater than AlphaDIA. These results do not support systematic attenuation of fold-change magnitudes as the principal explanation for MaxDIA's reduced differential abundance detection. Together with its weaker cross-pipeline fold-change correlations and higher median model residual variability, the findings suggest that differences in quantitative precision and statistical uncertainty may contribute to the observed discrepancies. Direct comparison of contrast-specific standard errors is required to evaluate this explanation.

```{r da_statistical_precision_6h, fig.width=12, fig.height=6.5, dpi=300, out.width="100%", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=FALSE}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

target_contrast <- "KO vs CTRL cisplatin 6h"

software_order <- c("AlphaDIA", "DIA-NN", "Spectronaut", "MaxDIA")

# 1. Extract existing contrast-specific statistical results
precision_long <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(software_order, function(software) {

    results <- inference_list[[software]]

    data.frame(
      Software = software,
      Protein = as.character(results$feature),
      Contrast = as.character(results$contrast),
      logFC = as.numeric(results$logFC),
      SE = as.numeric(results$se),
      t_stat = as.numeric(results$t)
    )
  })
) |>
  dplyr::filter(
    Contrast == target_contrast,
    !is.na(Protein),
    is.finite(logFC),
    is.finite(SE),
    SE > 0,
    is.finite(t_stat)
  )

# Check unique protein identifiers within each pipeline
stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(precision_long[c("Protein", "Software")])
)

# 2. Restrict to proteins with valid statistics in ALL four pipelines
common_precision_proteins <- Reduce(
  intersect,
  lapply(software_order, function(software) {
    precision_long$Protein[precision_long$Software == software]
  })
)

precision_shared <- precision_long |>
  dplyr::filter(Protein %in% common_precision_proteins) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Software = factor(Software, levels = software_order),
    Absolute_t = abs(t_stat)
  )

cat(
  "Protein groups with valid statistics in all four pipelines:",
  length(common_precision_proteins), "\n"
)

# 3. Summary statistics
precision_summary <- precision_shared |>
  dplyr::group_by(Software) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    N = dplyr::n(),
    Median_SE = median(SE),
    Q1_SE = unname(quantile(SE, 0.25)),
    Q3_SE = unname(quantile(SE, 0.75)),
    Median_Abs_t = median(Absolute_t),
    Q1_Abs_t = unname(quantile(Absolute_t, 0.25)),
    Q3_Abs_t = unname(quantile(Absolute_t, 0.75)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(
  precision_summary |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      dplyr::across(
        -c(Software, N),
        ~ round(.x, 3)
      )
    ),
  n = Inf
)

# 4. Prepare data for visualization
precision_plot_data <- precision_shared |>
  dplyr::select(Software, SE, Absolute_t) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(SE, Absolute_t),
    names_to = "Metric",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Metric = factor(
      Metric,
      levels = c("SE", "Absolute_t"),
      labels = c(
        "Contrast-specific standard error",
        "Absolute t-statistic"
      )
    )
  )

# 5. Plot distributions
p_precision <- ggplot(
  precision_plot_data,
  aes(x = Software, y = Value, fill = Software)
) +
  geom_violin(
    alpha = 0.55,
    trim = TRUE,
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.16,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    fill = "white",
    color = "#344054",
    linewidth = 0.45
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Metric,
    scales = "free_y",
    nrow = 1
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = software_colors,
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Statistical precision across pipelines",
    subtitle = paste0(
      target_contrast,
      " | Shared protein groups"
    ),
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    # caption = paste(
    #   "Only proteins with finite log2FC, positive finite SE,",
    #   "and finite t-statistics in all four pipelines.",
    #   "Exact protein-group identifier matching."
    # )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#667085"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(p_precision)
```
Despite comparable median absolute log2 fold changes between MaxDIA and DIA-NN (0.181 versus 0.184) among 7,474 commonly quantified protein groups, MaxDIA exhibited substantially higher contrast-specific standard errors (median 0.182 versus 0.085) and lower absolute t-statistics (median 0.951 versus 2.19). These findings suggest that reduced statistical precision, rather than systematically smaller estimated abundance changes, is a major contributor to MaxDIA's lower differential abundance detection rate. The results also demonstrate that greater precursor coverage per protein group does not necessarily translate into greater sensitivity for detecting differential protein abundance.


```{r residual-variability-comparison, eval=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=11, fig.height=6, dpi=300, out.width="100%"}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Existing fitted QFeatures objects
qf_models <- list(
  AlphaDIA = qf_alpha,
  `DIA-NN` = qf_diann,
  Spectronaut = qf_spectro,
  MaxDIA = qf_maxdia
)

software_colors <- c(
  AlphaDIA = "#0072B2",
  `DIA-NN` = "#E69F00",
  Spectronaut = "#009E73",
  MaxDIA = "#CC79A7"
)

# Extract residual sigma from existing msqrob2 StatModel objects
sigma_data <- lapply(names(qf_models), function(software) {

  assay <- qf_models[[software]][["proteins"]]
  models <- SummarizedExperiment::rowData(assay)$msqrobModels

  data.frame(
    Protein = rownames(assay),
    Software = software,
    Sigma = vapply(
      models,
      function(m) {
        if (is.null(m)) return(NA_real_)

        sigma <- methods::slot(m, "params")$sigma

        if (length(sigma) != 1 ||
            !is.finite(sigma) ||
            sigma <= 0) {
          return(NA_real_)
        }

        as.numeric(sigma)
      },
      numeric(1)
    )
  )
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()

# Restrict to the 7,474 proteins used in the previous SE/t-statistic analysis
# and retain only proteins with valid sigma in all four pipelines
sigma_shared <- sigma_data |>
  dplyr::filter(
    Protein %in% common_precision_proteins,
    is.finite(Sigma),
    Sigma > 0
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(Protein) |>
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::n_distinct(Software) == 4) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Software = factor(Software, levels = names(qf_models))
  )

# Summary statistics for matched proteins
sigma_summary <- sigma_shared |>
  dplyr::group_by(Software) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    N = dplyr::n(),
    Median_Sigma = median(Sigma),
    Mean_Sigma = mean(Sigma),
    Q1_Sigma = unname(quantile(Sigma, 0.25)),
    Q3_Sigma = unname(quantile(Sigma, 0.75)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat(
  "Matched proteins with valid residual sigma in all four pipelines:",
  dplyr::n_distinct(sigma_shared$Protein),
  "\n\n"
)

print(sigma_summary, n = Inf)

# Visualize residual variability
p_sigma <- ggplot(
  sigma_shared,
  aes(x = Software, y = Sigma, fill = Software)
) +
  geom_violin(
    trim = TRUE,
    alpha = 0.65,
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.15,
    fill = "white",
    color = "#344054",
    outlier.shape = NA
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = software_colors) +
  scale_y_log10(
    labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.01)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Protein-level residual variability across DIA pipelines",
    subtitle = paste0(
      dplyr::n_distinct(sigma_shared$Protein),
      " matched protein groups with valid residual sigma"
    ),
    x = NULL,
    y = "Residual standard deviation, sigma (log10 scale)",
    caption = paste(
      "Existing batch-adjusted msqrob2 models.",
      "Identical protein groups compared across all four pipelines."
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#667085"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(p_sigma)
```
MaxDIA has substantially greater protein-level residual variability than the other three pipelines, even when we compare exactly the same 7,474 protein groups. On 7,474 matched protein groups, MaxDIA exhibited the highest residual variability (median σ = 0.309), approximately 2.22-fold greater than DIA-NN (0.139). This difference was accompanied by a 2.14-fold higher median standard error for the KO versus CTRL cisplatin 6h contrast, despite comparable median absolute log2 fold changes. These findings suggest that increased residual variability, rather than uniformly smaller estimated biological effects, contributes substantially to MaxDIA's lower number of statistically significant differentially abundant proteins. MaxDIA's lower differential abundance sensitivity is associated with substantially greater residual variability and higher statistical uncertainty, despite its greater precursor coverage per protein.

```{r precision-all-contrasts, fig.width=13, fig.height=9, dpi=300, out.width="100%", eval=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

software_order <- c("AlphaDIA", "DIA-NN", "Spectronaut", "MaxDIA")

software_colors <- c(
  AlphaDIA = "#0072B2",
  `DIA-NN` = "#E69F00",
  Spectronaut = "#009E73",
  MaxDIA = "#CC79A7"
)

contrast_order <- planned_contrasts$Contrast

# Collect valid contrast-specific statistics
precision_all <- lapply(software_order, function(software) {

  inference_list[[software]] |>
    dplyr::filter(
      contrast %in% contrast_order,
      is.finite(logFC),
      is.finite(se),
      se > 0,
      is.finite(t)
    ) |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      Software = software,
      Protein = as.character(feature),
      Contrast = as.character(contrast),
      Abs_logFC = abs(logFC),
      SE = se,
      Abs_t = abs(t)
    )

}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()

# Match proteins separately within each contrast
# Retain only proteins with valid results from all four pipelines
precision_matched <- precision_all |>
  dplyr::group_by(Contrast, Protein) |>
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::n_distinct(Software) == 4) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Software = factor(Software, levels = software_order),
    Contrast = factor(Contrast, levels = contrast_order)
  )

# Summarize matched-protein statistics
precision_all_summary <- precision_matched |>
  dplyr::group_by(Contrast, Software) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    N = dplyr::n(),
    Median_Abs_logFC = median(Abs_logFC),
    Median_SE = median(SE),
    Median_Abs_t = median(Abs_t),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(precision_all_summary, n = Inf)

# Prepare three metrics for a faceted comparison
precision_plot_data <- precision_all_summary |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Median_Abs_logFC, Median_SE, Median_Abs_t),
    names_to = "Metric",
    values_to = "Median"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Metric = factor(
      Metric,
      levels = c("Median_Abs_logFC", "Median_SE", "Median_Abs_t"),
      labels = c(
        "Median absolute log2 fold change",
        "Median standard error",
        "Median absolute t-statistic"
      )
    )
  )

p_precision_all <- ggplot(
  precision_plot_data,
  aes(x = Software, y = Median, fill = Software)
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  facet_grid(
    Metric ~ Contrast,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = software_colors) +
  labs(
    title = "Statistical precision across all planned contrasts",
    subtitle = "Only protein groups with valid results in all four pipelines within each contrast",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#667085"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1),
    strip.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, size = 8),
    strip.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(p_precision_all)
```

Across all 11 differential abundance contrasts, MaxDIA consistently exhibited the highest median standard errors and lowest median absolute t-statistics among the four DIA analysis pipelines. This pattern persisted when restricting each contrast to approximately 7,475 protein groups with valid estimates in all four pipelines. MaxDIA did not systematically produce smaller effect sizes; in seven contrasts, it exhibited the largest median absolute log2 fold change. Combined with its substantially higher protein-level residual variability, these findings indicate that increased statistical uncertainty is a major contributor to MaxDIA's lower differential abundance detection rate.

```{r da_logfc_agreement_all, fig.width=12, fig.height=8, dpi=300, out.width="100%", results="asis", eval=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

software_order <- c("AlphaDIA", "DIA-NN", "Spectronaut", "MaxDIA")
contrast_order <- planned_contrasts$Contrast

software_colors <- c(
  AlphaDIA = "#0072B2",
  `DIA-NN` = "#E69F00",
  Spectronaut = "#009E73",
  MaxDIA = "#CC79A7"
)

# Collect finite log2 fold changes for all contrasts
logfc_all_long <- lapply(software_order, function(software) {

  inference_list[[software]] |>
    dplyr::filter(
      contrast %in% contrast_order,
      is.finite(logFC)
    ) |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      Contrast = as.character(contrast),
      Protein = as.character(feature),
      Software = software,
      logFC = logFC
    )

}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()

# Create one row per protein and contrast, with four pipeline columns
logfc_all_wide <- logfc_all_long |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(Contrast, Protein),
    names_from = Software,
    values_from = logFC
  )

# Six unique pipeline pairs
software_pairs <- combn(software_order, 2, simplify = FALSE)

# Pairwise agreement metrics and scatterplots for each contrast
agreement_results <- list()
agreement_plots <- list()

for (contrast_name in contrast_order) {

  contrast_data <- logfc_all_wide |>
    dplyr::filter(Contrast == contrast_name)

  pair_data <- lapply(software_pairs, function(pair) {

    x <- contrast_data[[pair[1]]]
    y <- contrast_data[[pair[2]]]

    valid <- is.finite(x) & is.finite(y)

    data.frame(
      Protein = contrast_data$Protein[valid],
      Pipeline_1 = pair[1],
      Pipeline_2 = pair[2],
      Pair = paste(pair, collapse = " vs "),
      logFC_1 = x[valid],
      logFC_2 = y[valid]
    )
  }) |>
    dplyr::bind_rows()

  # Agreement statistics
  agreement_results[[contrast_name]] <- pair_data |>
    dplyr::group_by(Pipeline_1, Pipeline_2, Pair) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      Shared_Proteins = dplyr::n(),
      Pearson_r = cor(logFC_1, logFC_2, method = "pearson"),
      Spearman_rho = cor(logFC_1, logFC_2, method = "spearman"),
      Same_Direction_Percent = 100 * mean(
        sign(logFC_1) == sign(logFC_2)
      ),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(Contrast = contrast_name, .before = 1)

  # Scatterplot: shared axes and identity line
  p <- ggplot(
    pair_data,
    aes(x = logFC_1, y = logFC_2)
  ) +
    geom_point(
      alpha = 0.15,
      size = 0.5,
      color = "#344054"
    ) +
    geom_abline(
      slope = 1,
      intercept = 0,
      linetype = "dashed",
      color = "#D55E00",
      linewidth = 0.5
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~ Pair, ncol = 3, scales = "fixed") +
    coord_equal() +
    labs(
      title = paste("Log2 fold-change agreement:", contrast_name),
      subtitle = "Matched protein groups; dashed line indicates identical fold changes",
      x = "Pipeline 1 log2 fold change",
      y = "Pipeline 2 log2 fold change"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#667085"),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )

  agreement_plots[[contrast_name]] <- p

  cat("\n\n### ", contrast_name, "\n\n", sep = "")
  print(p)
}

# Combine agreement statistics across all 11 contrasts
logfc_agreement_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(agreement_results) |>
  dplyr::arrange(
    factor(Contrast, levels = contrast_order),
    Pipeline_1,
    Pipeline_2
  )

cat("\n\n### Pairwise fold-change agreement summary\n\n")

print(logfc_agreement_summary, n = Inf)
```

Pairwise comparison of protein-level log2 fold changes across 11 differential abundance contrasts revealed substantial differences in agreement among DIA analysis pipelines. AlphaDIA and DIA-NN showed the strongest overall concordance, with a median Pearson correlation of 0.719 and median directional agreement of 77.5%. DIA-NN and Spectronaut also exhibited relatively strong agreement (median r = 0.671). In contrast, comparisons involving MaxDIA consistently showed lower correlations, ranging from median r = 0.378 to 0.500, and lower directional agreement, ranging from 63.9% to 68.0%. Agreement was contrast-dependent, with stronger concordance for prominent treatment-associated responses and weaker concordance for the JNK inhibitor effect at 6h. Combined with MaxDIA's higher residual variability and standard errors, these findings suggest that pipeline-specific differences in protein quantification and statistical precision contribute to variability in differential abundance results. Nevertheless, cross-pipeline agreement alone cannot establish which pipeline provides the most accurate estimates.


```{r da_volcano_all, fig.width=13, fig.height=9, dpi=300, out.width="100%", eval=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

software_order <- c("AlphaDIA", "DIA-NN", "Spectronaut", "MaxDIA")
contrast_order <- planned_contrasts$Contrast

software_colors <- c(
  AlphaDIA = "#0072B2",
  `DIA-NN` = "#E69F00",
  Spectronaut = "#009E73",
  MaxDIA = "#CC79A7"
)

# Significance threshold
fdr_cutoff <- 0.05

# Output folders
volcano_dir <- "figures/volcano_plots"
individual_dir <- file.path(volcano_dir, "individual")
combined_dir <- file.path(volcano_dir, "combined")

dir.create(individual_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(combined_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Collect differential abundance results
volcano_data <- lapply(software_order, function(software) {

  inference_list[[software]] |>
    dplyr::filter(
      contrast %in% contrast_order,
      is.finite(logFC),
      is.finite(adjPval),
      adjPval >= 0,
      adjPval <= 1
    ) |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      Software = software,
      Contrast = as.character(contrast),
      Protein = as.character(feature),
      logFC = logFC,
      adjPval = adjPval
    )

}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Software = factor(Software, levels = software_order),
    Contrast = factor(Contrast, levels = contrast_order),
    Significant = adjPval < fdr_cutoff,
    neg_log10_FDR = -log10(pmax(adjPval, .Machine$double.xmin))
  )

# Count significant proteins per contrast and pipeline
volcano_summary <- volcano_data |>
  dplyr::group_by(Contrast, Software) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Tested_Proteins = dplyr::n(),
    Significant_Proteins = sum(Significant),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(volcano_summary, n = Inf)

# File-safe contrast names
safe_filename <- function(x) {
  gsub(
    "_+$", "",
    gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", x)
  )
}

# Store generated plots
volcano_plots <- list()
volcano_combined <- list()

for (i in seq_along(contrast_order)) {

  contrast_name <- contrast_order[i]

  contrast_data <- volcano_data |>
    dplyr::filter(Contrast == contrast_name)

  # Common limits across pipelines within this contrast
  x_limit <- max(abs(contrast_data$logFC), na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05
  y_limit <- max(contrast_data$neg_log10_FDR, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05

  x_limit <- max(x_limit, 0.5)
  y_limit <- max(y_limit, -log10(fdr_cutoff) * 1.1)

  # Individual volcano plots
  for (software in software_order) {

    plot_data <- contrast_data |>
      dplyr::filter(Software == software)

    n_sig <- sum(plot_data$Significant)

    p <- ggplot(
      plot_data,
      aes(x = logFC, y = neg_log10_FDR)
    ) +
      geom_point(
        data = function(d) d[!d$Significant, ],
        color = "#B8BDC7",
        alpha = 0.45,
        size = 0.65
      ) +
      geom_point(
        data = function(d) d[d$Significant, ],
        color = unname(software_colors[software]),
        alpha = 0.7,
        size = 0.8
      ) +
      geom_hline(
        yintercept = -log10(fdr_cutoff),
        linetype = "dashed",
        color = "#667085",
        linewidth = 0.5
      ) +
      geom_vline(
        xintercept = 0,
        color = "#98A2B3",
        linewidth = 0.4
      ) +
      coord_cartesian(
        xlim = c(-x_limit, x_limit),
        ylim = c(0, y_limit)
      ) +
      labs(
        title = software,
        subtitle = paste0(n_sig, " proteins at FDR < 0.05"),
        x = "Log2 fold change",
        y = expression(-log[10]("adjusted p-value"))
      ) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#667085"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
      )

    volcano_plots[[paste(contrast_name, software, sep = " | ")]] <- p

    ggplot2::ggsave(
      filename = file.path(
        individual_dir,
        sprintf(
          "%02d_%s_%s.png",
          i,
          safe_filename(contrast_name),
          safe_filename(software)
        )
      ),
      plot = p,
      width = 7,
      height = 5.5,
      dpi = 300,
      bg = "white"
    )
  }

  # Four-panel comparison with common axes
  combined_plot <- ggplot(
    contrast_data,
    aes(x = logFC, y = neg_log10_FDR)
  ) +
    geom_point(
      data = function(d) d[!d$Significant, ],
      color = "#B8BDC7",
      alpha = 0.4,
      size = 0.5
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = function(d) d[d$Significant, ],
      aes(color = Software),
      alpha = 0.65,
      size = 0.65
    ) +
    geom_hline(
      yintercept = -log10(fdr_cutoff),
      linetype = "dashed",
      color = "#667085"
    ) +
    geom_vline(
      xintercept = 0,
      color = "#98A2B3"
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~ Software, ncol = 2) +
    scale_color_manual(values = software_colors) +
    coord_cartesian(
      xlim = c(-x_limit, x_limit),
      ylim = c(0, y_limit)
    ) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Differential abundance:", contrast_name),
      subtitle = "FDR < 0.05; identical axes across all four pipelines",
      x = "Log2 fold change",
      y = expression(-log[10]("adjusted p-value"))
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#667085"),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )

  volcano_combined[[contrast_name]] <- combined_plot

  ggplot2::ggsave(
    filename = file.path(
      combined_dir,
      sprintf(
        "%02d_%s.png",
        i,
        safe_filename(contrast_name)
      )
    ),
    plot = combined_plot,
    width = 12,
    height = 9,
    dpi = 300,
    bg = "white"
  )

  print(combined_plot)
}

# Save summary table
utils::write.csv(
  volcano_summary,
  file = file.path(volcano_dir, "volcano_summary.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

cat(
  "\nSaved 44 individual volcano plots,",
  "11 four-panel figures, and 1 summary CSV to:",
  normalizePath(volcano_dir),
  "\n"
)
```

```{r da_quantitative_comparison_68, fig.width=12, fig.height=8, dpi=300, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=run_analysis}
sigma_data_68 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(software_order_68, function(sw) {

    se <- qf_models_68[[sw]][["proteins"]]
    models <- SummarizedExperiment::rowData(se)[["msqrobModels"]]

    data.frame(
      Protein = rownames(se),
      Software = sw,
      Sigma = vapply(models, function(m) {
        if (is.null(m) || !methods::is(m, "StatModel"))
          return(NA_real_)

        s <- m@params$sigma

        if (length(s) != 1L || !is.finite(s) || s <= 0)
          return(NA_real_)

        as.numeric(s)
      }, numeric(1))
    )
  })
)

fdr_cutoff_68 <- 0.05

volcano_dir_68 <- "figures/volcano_plots_68"

    Contrast = factor(Contrast, levels = contrast_order_68),
    Significant = adjPval < fdr_cutoff_68,
    neg_log10_FDR = -log10(
      pmax(adjPval, .Machine$double.xmin)
    )
  )

volcano_summary_68 <- volcano_data_68 |>
  dplyr::group_by(Contrast, Software) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Tested_Proteins = dplyr::n(),

  )

for (i in seq_along(contrast_order_68)) {

  contrast_name <- contrast_order_68[i]

  contrast_data <- volcano_data_68 |>
    dplyr::filter(Contrast == contrast_name)

  x_limit <- max(
    0.5, max(abs(contrast_data$logFC), na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05
  )

  y_limit <- max(
    -log10(fdr_cutoff_68) * 1.1,

        alpha = 0.45,
        size = 0.65
      ) +

        alpha = 0.7,
        size = 0.8
      ) +
      geom_hline(
        yintercept = -log10(fdr_cutoff_68),

        color = "#667085"
      ) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "#98A2B3") +
      coord_cartesian(
        xlim = c(-x_limit, x_limit),
        ylim = c(0, y_limit)
      ) +
      labs(
        title = sw,
        subtitle = paste0(n_sig, " proteins at FDR < 0.05"),
        x = "Log2 fold change",
        y = expression(-log[10]("adjusted p-value"))
      ) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
      )

    volcano_plots_68[[paste(contrast_name, sw, sep = " | ")]] <- p

    ggplot2::ggsave(
      file.path(
        individual_dir_68,
        sprintf(
          "%02d_%s_%s.png",
          i,
          safe_filename_68(contrast_name),
          safe_filename_68(sw)
        )
      ),
      plot = p,
      width = 7,
      height = 5.5,
      dpi = 300,
      bg = "white"
    )
  }

  combined_plot <- ggplot(
    contrast_data,
    aes(x = logFC, y = neg_log10_FDR)
  ) +
    geom_point(
      data = function(d) d[!d$Significant, ],
      color = "#B8BDC7",
      alpha = 0.4,
      size = 0.5
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = function(d) d[d$Significant, ],
      aes(color = Software),
      alpha = 0.65,
      size = 0.65
    ) +
    geom_hline(
      yintercept = -log10(fdr_cutoff_68),
      linetype = "dashed",
      color = "#667085"
    ) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "#98A2B3") +
    facet_wrap(~ Software, ncol = 2) +
    scale_color_manual(values = software_colors) +
    coord_cartesian(
      xlim = c(-x_limit, x_limit),
      ylim = c(0, y_limit)
    ) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Differential abundance:", contrast_name),
      subtitle = "FDR < 0.05; identical axes across pipelines",
      x = "Log2 fold change",
      y = expression(-log[10]("adjusted p-value"))
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )

```
Pairwise comparison of protein-level log2 fold changes for the KO versus CTRL cisplatin 6h contrast revealed positive but variable agreement across the four DIA pipelines. AlphaDIA and DIA-NN showed the strongest concordance (Pearson r = 0.711; Spearman ρ = 0.677), followed by DIA-NN and Spectronaut (r = 0.627). Comparisons involving MaxDIA exhibited weaker correlations (r = 0.389–0.476), indicating greater variability in estimated abundance changes. Among 7,465 protein groups quantified by all four pipelines, MaxDIA showed the highest median absolute log2 fold change (0.190), but also the highest median standard error (0.254) and residual variability (σ = 0.309). These findings suggest that reduced statistical precision, rather than smaller estimated fold changes, contributes to MaxDIA's lower differential abundance detection rate.


### Temporal patterns of cisplatin response and c-Jun-dependent regulation

The cisplatin response was investigated across untreated baseline, 6-hour,
and 24-hour conditions in CTRL and c-Jun KO cells. Although the existing
batch-adjusted differential abundance model includes these experimental
conditions, individual pairwise contrasts do not provide a joint test of
temporal response.

We therefore examine the experimental design before evaluating overall
cisplatin-associated changes and genotype-dependent differences in response.

```{r temporal-design-check}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Focus on CTRL and KO baseline/cisplatin conditions
temporal_conditions <- c(
  "CTRL_Untreated_Baseline",
  "CTRL_cDDP_6h",
  "CTRL_cDDP_24h",
  "KO_Untreated_Baseline",
  "KO_cDDP_6h",
  "KO_cDDP_24h"
)

temporal_design <- design_data |>
  dplyr::filter(condition %in% temporal_conditions) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Genotype = ifelse(
      grepl("^KO_", condition), "KO", "CTRL"
    ),
    Time = dplyr::case_when(
      grepl("Baseline$", condition) ~ "Baseline",
      grepl("_6h$", condition) ~ "6h",
      grepl("_24h$", condition) ~ "24h"
    ),
    Genotype = factor(Genotype, levels = c("CTRL", "KO")),
    Time = factor(Time, levels = c("Baseline", "6h", "24h"))
  )

# Number of samples in each genotype/time/batch combination
temporal_batch_table <- temporal_design |>
  dplyr::count(Genotype, Time, Batch, name = "N") |>
  tidyr::complete(
    Genotype,
    Time,
    Batch,
    fill = list(N = 0)
  )

print(temporal_batch_table, n = Inf)

# Visualize batch support
p_temporal_design <- ggplot(
  temporal_batch_table,
  aes(x = Time, y = Batch, fill = N)
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(N > 0, N, "")), size = 4) +
  facet_wrap(~ Genotype, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#F2F4F7",
    high = "#0072B2"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Sample distribution across cisplatin-response conditions",
    subtitle = "Number of samples per genotype, condition, and acquisition batch",
    x = "Experimental condition",
    y = "Acquisition batch",
    fill = "Samples"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )

print(p_temporal_design)
```

```{r temporal-joint-tests, eval=FALSE}
library(dplyr)

# Existing fitted protein models
qf_models <- list(
  AlphaDIA = qf_alpha,
  `DIA-NN` = qf_diann,
  Spectronaut = qf_spectro,
  MaxDIA = qf_maxdia
)

# Uses temporal_matrices created in the previous chunk:
# CTRL_response, KO_response, Genotype_interaction

joint_test_protein <- function(m, C) {

  empty <- c(F_stat = NA_real_, df1 = 2, df2 = NA_real_,
             pval = NA_real_)

  if (is.null(m)) return(empty)

  # Coefficient estimates for the two contrasts
  beta <- methods::slot(m, "params")$coefficients

  # Posterior degrees of freedom
  df2 <- methods::slot(m, "dfPosterior")

  if (length(df2) != 1 || !is.finite(df2) || df2 <= 0) {
    return(empty)
  }

  # Obtain the two contrast estimates and their covariance
  result <- tryCatch({

    estimate <- as.numeric(
      crossprod(C, beta[rownames(C)])
    )

    covariance <- msqrob2::varContrast(m, L = C)

    if (
      any(!is.finite(estimate)) ||
      any(!is.finite(covariance)) ||
      qr(covariance)$rank < 2
    ) {
      return(empty)
    }

    # Joint Wald F-statistic
    F_stat <- as.numeric(
      crossprod(
        estimate,
        solve(covariance, estimate)
      )
    ) / 2

    F_stat <- max(0, F_stat)

    c(
      F_stat = F_stat,
      df1 = 2,
      df2 = df2,
      pval = pf(F_stat, df1 = 2, df2 = df2,
                lower.tail = FALSE)
    )

  }, error = function(e) empty)

  result
}

# Run all three joint hypotheses on existing fitted models
temporal_joint_results <- list()

for (software in names(qf_models)) {

  assay <- qf_models[[software]][["proteins"]]

  models <- SummarizedExperiment::rowData(assay)$msqrobModels
  proteins <- rownames(assay)

  for (hypothesis_name in names(temporal_matrices)) {

    C <- temporal_matrices[[hypothesis_name]]

    test_matrix <- t(vapply(
      models,
      joint_test_protein,
      numeric(4),
      C = C
    ))

    results <- data.frame(
      Software = software,
      Hypothesis = hypothesis_name,
      Protein = proteins,
      F_stat = test_matrix[, "F_stat"],
      df1 = test_matrix[, "df1"],
      df2 = test_matrix[, "df2"],
      pval = test_matrix[, "pval"]
    )

    results$adjPval <- p.adjust(results$pval, method = "BH")

    temporal_joint_results[[
      paste(software, hypothesis_name, sep = " | ")
    ]] <- results
  }
}

temporal_joint_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  temporal_joint_results
)

# Summarize the number of significant proteins
temporal_joint_summary <- temporal_joint_results |>
  dplyr::group_by(Hypothesis, Software) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Tested_Proteins = sum(is.finite(pval)),
    Significant_Proteins = sum(adjPval < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(temporal_joint_summary, n = Inf)
```
These results show a clear pattern: the c-Jun KO samples exhibit a broader cisplatin-associated proteomic response than CTRL, and all four pipelines detect evidence of genotype-dependent responses.

1. KO response is consistently more extensive than CTRL response.

Across all four pipelines, substantially more proteins show a significant joint cisplatin-associated response in KO than CTRL. This is consistent with c-Jun loss being associated with altered cellular responses to cisplatin.

However, significance counts alone do not establish that KO responses have larger effect sizes or that every response is stronger. We would need to examine the direction and magnitude of the individual changes.

2. The genotype interaction is substantial.

AlphaDIA identifies 2,820 proteins, DIA-NN 2,678, and Spectronaut 1,698 with significant joint genotype-dependent responses. MaxDIA identifies 280.

This means that, for those proteins, the KO-versus-CTRL difference in cisplatin-associated abundance changes is statistically detectable at 6h, 24h, or both.

It does not necessarily mean that a protein responds significantly in KO but not CTRL. The interaction directly tests the difference between the two responses, which is the more appropriate statistical question.

3. MaxDIA remains much less sensitive.

Its lower discovery counts are consistent with your earlier finding of substantially higher residual variability and contrast standard errors in MaxDIA. The joint test has not eliminated that difference.

4. The experimental batch structure still matters.

The 6h and 24h cisplatin samples occupy different batches. The fitted additive batch model adjusts for this, but interpretation relies on its assumptions. These are cisplatin-response comparisons across experimental conditions, not repeated measurements of the same samples over time.

243 proteins have significant genotype-dependent cisplatin responses in all four DIA pipelines, despite substantial differences in the total number of discoveries. The most interesting observation is that MaxDIA identifies only 273 significant interaction proteins among the shared proteins, while 243 proteins are significant in all four pipelines. This means at least 89.0% of MaxDIA's interaction discoveries are supported by all three other pipelines.

That suggests MaxDIA's smaller discovery set is largely a high-confidence subset of the other pipelines' discoveries, rather than a completely different biological signal. This is consistent with your earlier finding that MaxDIA has higher residual variability and lower statistical sensitivity.

One caveat: these 243 proteins agree in statistical significance, not necessarily in the direction of their 6h and 24h interaction effects.

To investigate genotype-dependent cisplatin responses, two-degree-of-freedom joint tests were performed using the existing batch-adjusted, moderated protein abundance models. The tests evaluated cisplatin-associated changes at 6 and 24 hours relative to untreated baseline in CTRL and c-Jun KO cells, as well as differences in these responses between genotypes.

All four DIA pipelines identified more proteins with significant cisplatin-associated responses in c-Jun KO cells than in CTRL cells. Significant joint genotype interactions were also detected across all pipelines, although the number of discoveries varied substantially. When the analysis was restricted to 7,466 proteins tested by all four pipelines, DIA-NN identified 2,395 significant genotype interactions, followed by AlphaDIA (2,102), Spectronaut (1,632), and MaxDIA (273). Of these, 243 proteins were significant in all four pipelines, representing 89.0% of MaxDIA's significant interaction proteins.

The 243 consensus proteins showed particularly strong agreement at 6 hours. All four pipelines estimated the same direction of genotype interaction for every protein, with pairwise Pearson correlations ranging from 0.930 to 0.982. Individual interaction testing identified significant 6-hour effects for 243 proteins in DIA-NN and Spectronaut, 242 in AlphaDIA, and 212 in MaxDIA. In contrast, none of these consensus proteins showed a significant individual 24-hour interaction in any pipeline. Agreement in 24-hour effect estimates was also lower, with 49.4% directional concordance and pairwise correlations ranging from 0.276 to 0.647.

Together, these findings indicate that the strongest cross-pipeline consensus in genotype-dependent cisplatin responses is concentrated at 6 hours. The results also reinforce the broader benchmarking findings: pipelines differ substantially in their ability to detect statistically significant abundance changes, while showing strong agreement in effect direction and magnitude for robust shared signals. Because the experimental conditions were distributed unevenly across acquisition batches, temporal comparisons should be interpreted as batch-adjusted cisplatin-response contrasts rather than longitudinal measurements.

```{r temporal_cisplatin_analysis_68, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=run_analysis}
# ============================================================
# 3. Joint Wald F-tests using existing fitted models
# ============================================================

joint_test_protein_68 <- function(m, C) {

  empty <- c(
    F_stat = NA_real_,
    df1 = 2,
    df2 = NA_real_,
    pval = NA_real_
  )

  if (is.null(m) || !methods::is(m, "StatModel"))
    return(empty)

  tryCatch({

    beta <- m@params$coefficients
    df2 <- as.numeric(m@dfPosterior)

    if (
      length(df2) != 1L ||
      !is.finite(df2) ||
      df2 <= 0 ||
      !all(rownames(C) %in% names(beta))
    ) return(empty)

    estimate <- as.numeric(
      crossprod(C, beta[rownames(C)])
    )

    covariance <- msqrob2::varContrast(m, L = C)

    if (
      any(!is.finite(estimate)) ||
      any(!is.finite(covariance)) ||
      qr(covariance)$rank < 2L
    ) return(empty)

    F_stat <- max(
      0,
      as.numeric(
        crossprod(estimate, solve(covariance, estimate))
      ) / 2
    )

    c(
      F_stat = F_stat,
      df1 = 2,
      df2 = df2,
      pval = pf(F_stat, 2, df2, lower.tail = FALSE)
    )

  }, error = function(e) empty)
}

temporal_joint_results_68 <- list()

for (sw in software_order_68) {

  cat("Joint temporal tests:", sw, "\n")

  se <- qf_models_68[[sw]][["proteins"]]
  models <- SummarizedExperiment::rowData(se)[["msqrobModels"]]

  for (hypothesis in names(temporal_matrices_68)) {

    C <- temporal_matrices_68[[hypothesis]]

    tests <- t(vapply(
      models,
      joint_test_protein_68,
      numeric(4),
      C = C
    ))

    results <- data.frame(
      Software = sw,
      Hypothesis = hypothesis,
      Protein = rownames(se),
      F_stat = tests[, "F_stat"],
      df1 = tests[, "df1"],
      df2 = tests[, "df2"],
      pval = tests[, "pval"]
    )

    results$adjPval <- p.adjust(results$pval, method = "BH")

    temporal_joint_results_68[[
      paste(sw, hypothesis, sep = " | ")
    ]] <- results
  }

  rm(se, models, tests, results)
}

temporal_joint_results_68 <- bind_rows(temporal_joint_results_68)

temporal_joint_summary_68 <- temporal_joint_results_68 |>
  group_by(Hypothesis, Software) |>
  summarise(
    Tested_Proteins = sum(is.finite(pval)),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

interaction_effects_68 <- bind_rows(
  lapply(software_order_68, function(sw) {

    se <- qf_models_68[[sw]][["proteins"]]
    models <- SummarizedExperiment::rowData(se)[["msqrobModels"]]
    C <- L_temporal_interaction_68

    idx <- match(interaction_consensus_68, rownames(se))
    keep <- which(!is.na(idx))

    estimates <- t(vapply(models[idx[keep]], function(m) {

      if (is.null(m) || !methods::is(m, "StatModel"))
        return(rep(NA_real_, ncol(C)))

      beta <- m@params$coefficients

      if (!all(rownames(C) %in% names(beta)))
        return(rep(NA_real_, ncol(C)))

      as.numeric(crossprod(C, beta[rownames(C)]))

    }, numeric(ncol(C))))

    colnames(estimates) <- colnames(C)

    data.frame(
      Software = sw,
      Protein = interaction_consensus_68[keep],
      estimates,
      check.names = FALSE
    )
  })
) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(colnames(L_temporal_interaction_68)),
    names_to = "Time",
    values_to = "Interaction_log2FC"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Time = ifelse(grepl("6h", Time), "6h", "24h"),
    Software = factor(Software, levels = software_order_68)
  )
```
